# Overview – Stage 2 of 6

Stage 2 estimates the **global XYZ rotation** (full 3D, yaw retained) between
`las_1` and `las_2` from per-stem axis vectors fit by robust Theil–Sen
regression, using IRLS with Tukey biweighting and a weighted Kabsch/SVD solve.

What this stage does and does not do

- **Does**: fit a stem axis per tree from the Stage 1 ellipse centres by
  Theil–Sen regression (`y ~ z`, `x ~ z`), compare the paired axes, and solve
  one rotation matrix `R_xyz`.
- **Does not**: use point clouds in the solve. The rotation is fit entirely
  from ellipse-centre axis vectors; only the optional 3-D visualisation chunks
  read a cloud, and they do so on demand. The stage never *applies* the
  rotation it solves – not to the clouds and not to the stem axis vectors.
  `R_xyz` is written to the Stage 2 checkpoint and first
  *applied* at the start of Stage 3.

Keeping the solve and the application in different stages means the rotation
can be re-solved, inspected or overridden without re-reading gigabytes of LAS
data, and guarantees there is exactly one place in the whole workflow where
each transform is applied to the cloud.

Inputs and outputs

- **In**: the Stage 1 checkpoint (`stage1_rds_path`).
- **Out**: `R_xyz`, `angle_xyz`, the per-pair residual/weight diagnostics, and
  `pairs_stage2` – `pairs_stage1` minus the pairs whose angular residual
  exceeded the final IRLS cutoff. Also `R_align_xyz_1` – the Stage 1A rough
  rotation composed with `R_xyz` into the single rotation carrying raw `las_1`
  to the final XYZ-aligned frame (a record object; `R_xyz` and `R_align_1` are
  still written separately and applied separately downstream).

# Stage 0 - Setup


## 0.1 Load libraries
```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Load libraries and set plot theme"

library(lidR)       # LAS I/O and point cloud processing
library(ggplot2)    # Plotting
library(dplyr)      # Data wrangling
library(knitr)      # is_html_output() / is_latex_output() output switch
library(plotly)     # Interactive 3D axis/overlay figures
library(tidyr)      # pivot_wider for verdict tables
library(base64enc)  # Embed rendered plots into HTML galleries
library(htmltools)  # Assemble the HTML gallery output

# ── Driver-supplied parameter overrides ──────────────────────────────────────
# Every params-* chunk in this file ends with .par_apply("<its label>"). Run the
# file by hand and that call does nothing: the values the chunk just assigned
# stand. Run it under the batch driver, which puts a .batch_params list in the
# environment before the first chunk, and any entry keyed to that chunk label is
# assigned here - AFTER the defaults, so the driver's value is the one that
# survives into the functional chunk that follows.
#
# Why this exists. Parameters used to sit in the same chunk as the code that
# consumed them, so the driver's overrides - which land after a chunk finishes -
# arrived too late to matter, and every pair silently used the .qmd's hardcoded
# value. Splitting each chunk in two fixes the ordering; this helper is what the
# driver reaches through.
#
# The defaults stay in this file rather than moving into the driver. They are
# the single definition, the driver names only what a batch changes, and there
# is no second copy of ~670 parameters to drift out of step with this one.
#
# envir = parent.frame() so a call at chunk top level lands in the environment
# the chunk is being evaluated in - globalenv by hand, the pair environment
# under the driver - without needing .stage_env(), which is defined further down.
.par_apply <- function(label, envir = parent.frame()) {
  bp <- mget(".batch_params", envir = envir, ifnotfound = list(NULL),
             inherits = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (is.null(bp) || is.null(bp[[label]])) return(invisible(character(0)))
  vals <- bp[[label]]
  if (!length(vals)) return(invisible(character(0)))
  if (is.null(names(vals)) || any(!nzchar(names(vals))))
    stop(sprintf("[.par_apply] .batch_params[['%s']] must be a fully NAMED list.", label))
  # A name the chunk did not define is almost always a typo or a rename in the
  # .qmd that the driver has not caught up with. Silence there would mean the
  # batch runs on the default while looking like it was overridden, so it stops.
  unknown <- names(vals)[!vapply(names(vals), exists, logical(1),
                                 envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)]
  if (length(unknown))
    stop(sprintf(paste0("[.par_apply] %s: %d override(s) name nothing this chunk assigns:\n  %s\n",
                        "  Fix the name in the driver's .build_params(), or remove it."),
                 label, length(unknown), paste(unknown, collapse = "\n  ")))
  for (nm in names(vals)) assign(nm, vals[[nm]], envir = envir)
  cat(sprintf("  [params] %s <- driver (%s)\n", label, paste(names(vals), collapse = ", ")))
  invisible(names(vals))
}
```

## 0.2 Global Helpers
```{r}
#| label: params-helpers
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Colours, ggplot theme, stage save/load utilities, and the on-demand point-cloud loader"

# ============================================================
# Colours
# ============================================================
COL_1     <- "#2196F3"
COL_2     <- "#FF5722"
COL_MATCH <- "#D9F9A5"

# ============================================================
# Progress bars
#
# Thin wrappers around cli, using EXACTLY the idiom Stage 3's axis-RANSAC fit
# has always used, because that one works when these documents are run on their
# own. Their only job is to save repeating the same six lines at every long
# loop.
#
# THE ONE THING THAT MUST NOT BE CHANGED HERE is `.envir = parent.frame()`.
# cli ties a progress bar's lifetime to a frame and tears the bar down when
# that frame exits. .pb_new() is a function, so a bar created with cli's
# default `.envir` would be created and immediately destroyed the moment
# .pb_new returned - the loop then ticks a bar that no longer exists and
# nothing is ever drawn. parent.frame() hands the bar to the CALLER's frame,
# which is the loop, and is the difference between this working and silently
# doing nothing. (An earlier revision passed globalenv() here, which is why the
# bars added through this helper never appeared while the hand-written ones in
# 3.3, 3.6 and 3.9 did.)
#
# Under the batch driver these will NOT be visible: cli draws on stderr, and
# the driver holds a message sink, which cannot be split. That is expected and
# is not worked around here - the driver prints its own progress instead.
# ============================================================
# Progress bars
# ============================================================
# One set of helpers, two renderers, chosen at the moment a bar is created.
#
#   cli    a redrawing bar, when there is a terminal able to show one
#   lines  one ordinary printed line per update, when there is not
#
# The choice is not cosmetic. cli draws on STDERR, and the batch driver holds a
# sink(type = "message"), which cannot split - so under the driver a cli bar
# goes to the log file and nowhere else, arriving as carriage returns and
# escape codes wrapped around each other. That is what the last run's log shows
# for every fitting step except the library's own: minutes of work with nothing
# on screen, and an unreadable smear in the log afterwards.
#
# The printed-line renderer is what the RANSAC library's cat handler already
# does, and it is the one visible line in that log. Same format here, so a fit
# reports identically whether the progress comes from the library or from a
# loop in this file.
show_progress_bars <- TRUE

# Print at most one line per 5% of the total or per 15 seconds, whichever comes
# first, plus always the first and last. A 20-stem fit gives ~20 lines; a
# 5000-slice loop does not give 5000.
progress_step_frac    <- 0.05
progress_min_seconds  <- 15

.par_apply("params-helpers")
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| code-summary: "Colours, ggplot theme, stage save/load utilities, and the on-demand point-cloud loader"

# ============================================================
# ggplot theme
# ============================================================
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position  = "bottom"
    )
)

# ============================================================
# Stage save/load utilities – shared by every stage file.
#
# Contract (identical in all six stage files):
#   SAVE  → hard ERROR if any *required* object is missing from the
#           environment, so a checkpoint can never be written half-empty.
#           A *warning* is raised for any missing *optional* object
#           (diagnostic products that may legitimately not have been run);
#           those are simply omitted from the file.
#   LOAD  → never errors on content. A *warning* is raised for each
#           requested object that is absent from the RDS. Objects present in
#           the RDS but not requested are COUNTED in the summary line and
#           never listed. Everything found in the file is loaded either way,
#           so nothing is silently discarded.
#   PATHS → a save never overwrites: if the target path exists, a numeric
#           suffix (_001, _002, ...) is appended until the name is free.
# ============================================================

#' Return `path` if free, otherwise path_001 / path_002 / ... (first free one).
.unique_path <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(path)
  base_noext <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(path)
  ext        <- tools::file_ext(path)
  counter    <- 1L
  repeat {
    candidate <- sprintf("%s_%03d.%s", base_noext, counter, ext)
    if (!file.exists(candidate)) {
      cat(sprintf("Target already exists - using unique name: %s\n", candidate))
      return(candidate)
    }
    counter <- counter + 1L
  }
}

#' Which environment do the stage helpers read and write?
#'
#' A .qmd rendered or run by hand evaluates its chunks in the global
#' environment. The batch driver does not: it gives every LAS pair a fresh
#' environment of its own, so that a leftover object from the previous pair
#' cannot be picked up by one of the exists() guards this pipeline is full of.
#' Under the driver, everything the stages assign therefore lives THERE, and
#' not in globalenv.
#'
#' parent.env(environment()) is the environment this chunk was evaluated in:
#' globalenv() by hand, the pair environment under the driver. It is resolved
#' from where .stage_env was DEFINED rather than from where it is called, so it
#' returns the same environment inside a function as it does at chunk top
#' level, and nothing has to be told which mode it is in.
#'
#' This replaced a hardcoded .stage_env() throughout. Under the driver that
#' pointed at an environment the pipeline had never written to, so every object
#' in a save manifest read as missing and the checkpoint refused to write - the
#' Stage 1 failure that reported 30 missing required objects after a 64-minute
#' fit. (`run_counts` was the one it did find, and only because .tally()'s `<<-`
#' walked past the pair environment into globalenv. That is fixed below too.)
.stage_env <- function() parent.env(environment())

#' Is a batch driver running this file?
#'
#' The driver assigns .batch_mode <- TRUE into the pair environment before the
#' first chunk runs. It changes one thing, and only for the checkpoints: in a
#' batch, every stage runs in ONE session, so Stage N+1 already holds in memory
#' everything Stage N computed and never has to read it back off disk. The
#' checkpoints stop being load-bearing and become a record of the run.
#'
#' So under a batch: nothing in a manifest is required (a missing object is
#' reported and left out, and the pair carries on), a failed write is reported
#' rather than thrown, and .stage_load is a no-op. Run the same .qmd by hand and
#' every one of those is an error again, which is what it should be when the
#' checkpoint is the only thing carrying the stage forward.
.in_batch <- function() {
  isTRUE(mget(".batch_mode", envir = .stage_env(),
              ifnotfound = list(FALSE), inherits = FALSE)[[1]])
}

#' Read one of the driver's batch settings out of the pair environment.
#' Absent - i.e. this file is being run by hand - gives `default`.
.batch_opt <- function(name, default = NULL) {
  v <- mget(name, envir = .stage_env(), ifnotfound = list(NULL), inherits = FALSE)[[1]]
  if (is.null(v)) default else v
}

#' Where a checkpoint goes when a batch is running.
#'
#' Every save chunk in this pipeline assigns its .rds path and then USES it a
#' few lines later, in the same chunk. The driver applies its overrides AFTER a
#' chunk has run, so an override of stage1_rds_path arrives after the file has
#' already been written to the path hardcoded here - which means, without this,
#' every sample in a batch writes over the same hardcoded name.
#'
#' So in batch mode the destination is derived instead, from two values the
#' driver puts in the environment before anything runs: .batch_rds_dir and
#' .batch_sample. The label the save chunk already passes supplies the rest, so
#' "Stage 3.2" becomes <dir>/<sample>_Stage3_2.rds with nothing to keep in sync.
#'
#' NULL means: not in a batch, or the driver did not set the directory - use the
#' path the chunk asked for.
.batch_rds_path <- function(label) {
  dir <- .batch_opt(".batch_rds_dir")
  smp <- .batch_opt(".batch_sample")
  if (is.null(dir) || is.null(smp)) return(NULL)
  file.path(dir, sprintf("%s_%s.rds", smp,
                         gsub("\\.", "_", gsub("\\s+", "", label))))
}

#' Save a stage checkpoint. Errors on missing required objects - unless the
#' batch driver is running this file, in which case nothing is required, the
#' destination is the per-sample one derived above, and a failure to write is
#' reported rather than thrown. See .in_batch() above.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

.stage_save <- function(path, required, optional = character(0),
                        label = "stage", envir = .stage_env(),
                        strict = !.in_batch()) {

  required <- unique(required)
  optional <- setdiff(unique(optional), required)

  # A batch may switch an individual checkpoint off by label - the driver's
  # keep_stage3_fit_checkpoint does exactly this for "Stage 3.1", whose chunk
  # must still RUN (the final Stage 3 manifest inherits from it) but need not
  # write a second large file per sample.
  if (!strict && label %in% .batch_opt(".batch_skip_saves", character(0))) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Skipped - switched off for this batch.\n", label))
    return(invisible(NA_character_))
  }

  # inherits = FALSE, matching the mget() below, which has always been strict.
  # With inheritance on, an object could be FOUND in a parent environment and
  # then fail to be FETCHED, and under the driver the parent is globalenv -
  # i.e. the previous pair's leftovers.
  .have <- function(x)
    if (!length(x)) logical(0)
    else vapply(x, exists, logical(1), envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)

  missing_req <- required[!.have(required)]
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L) {
    if (strict)
      stop(sprintf(
        "[%s save] Cannot save - %d required object(s) missing from the environment:\n  %s",
        label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s save] %d required object(s) missing - treated as optional and omitted (batch mode):\n  %s\n",
      label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))
  }

  missing_opt <- optional[!.have(optional)]
  if (length(missing_opt) > 0L) {
    msg <- sprintf(
      "[%s save] %d optional object(s) missing - omitted from the checkpoint:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_opt), paste(missing_opt, collapse = "\n  "))
    if (strict) warning(msg) else cat(msg, "\n", sep = "")
  }

  present  <- c(setdiff(required, missing_req), setdiff(optional, missing_opt))
  n_opt_in <- length(setdiff(optional, missing_opt))
  dat      <- mget(present, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)

  # ── The checkpoint describes itself ────────────────────────────────────────
  # The manifest travels INSIDE the file. Without it, loading a checkpoint means
  # first reconstructing the exact `required`/`optional` vectors it was written
  # with - and those are built by chunks, so a later checkpoint could only be
  # loaded after running the chunks that define an earlier one's manifest. That
  # made resuming from an arbitrary point in a fresh session impossible: the
  # Stage 3.2 chunk, for instance, stops outright unless .stage3_1_required is
  # already in scope.
  #
  # Stored under a name no manifest can collide with, and stripped again on
  # load, so it never reaches the session as an object.
  dat[[".__manifest__"]] <- list(
    required = setdiff(required, missing_req),
    optional = setdiff(optional, missing_opt),
    label    = label,
    saved_utc = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE))

  .write <- function() {
    p <- path
    if (!strict) {
      bp <- .batch_rds_path(label)
      if (!is.null(bp)) p <- bp
    }
    dir.create(dirname(p), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    # .unique_path only interactively. A batch path already carries the sample
    # name, so it cannot collide with another sample, and a re-run of the same
    # sample should REPLACE its checkpoint rather than leave _001, _002 behind
    # for the next reader to guess between.
    if (strict) p <- .unique_path(p)
    saveRDS(dat, p)
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Saved %d object(s) (%d required, %d optional) -> %s\n",
                label, length(dat), length(present) - n_opt_in, n_opt_in, p))
    p
  }

  if (strict) return(invisible(.write()))

  out <- tryCatch(.write(), error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Checkpoint NOT written: %s\n", label, conditionMessage(e)))
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Batch mode - the objects are still in this session, so the run continues.\n",
                label))
    NA_character_
  })
  invisible(out)
}

#' Load a stage checkpoint. Warns (never errors) on content mismatches, and
#' under the batch driver does not read at all - see .in_batch() above.
.stage_load <- function(path, required, optional = character(0),
                        label = "stage", envir = .stage_env(),
                        strict = !.in_batch()) {

  # In a batch the objects this would read are already live in `envir`, put
  # there by the stage that just ran. Reading them back would at best be a
  # no-op. At worst it would be wrong: checkpoint paths are per-sample and
  # .unique_path() means a re-run writes _001 rather than replacing the
  # original, so the path named here can easily be an EARLIER run's file. And
  # if the write failed or was partial, there would be nothing to read and the
  # pair would die at the start of the next stage having done all the work.
  if (!strict) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s load] Skipped - batch mode: this stage's objects are already in the session.\n",
                label))
    return(invisible(character(0)))
  }

  if (!file.exists(path))
    stop(sprintf("[%s load] File not found:\n  %s", label, path))

  dat <- readRDS(path)

  # ── Prefer the manifest the file carries ───────────────────────────────────
  # A checkpoint written by .stage_save records what it holds, so a load needs
  # nothing from the session - no earlier chunk, no earlier checkpoint, no
  # reconstructed name vectors. `required` and `optional` become a CHECK against
  # what the caller expected rather than the definition of what to read, which
  # is what lets any stage be resumed from any checkpoint in a fresh session.
  #
  # Files written before manifests existed simply have none; those fall back to
  # the caller's vectors, exactly as before.
  mf <- dat[[".__manifest__"]]
  dat[[".__manifest__"]] <- NULL
  caller_req <- unique(required)
  caller_opt <- setdiff(unique(optional), caller_req)

  if (!is.null(mf)) {
    required <- unique(mf$required)
    optional <- setdiff(unique(mf$optional), required)
    src <- sprintf("its own manifest (written %s)", mf$saved_utc %||% "?")
  } else {
    required <- caller_req; optional <- caller_opt
    src <- "the caller's manifest - this file predates self-describing checkpoints"
  }
  expected <- c(required, optional)

  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Reading %d object(s) from: %s\n",
              label, length(dat), path))
  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Manifest: %s\n", label, src))

  # Named by the caller but absent from the file: the real incompatibility, and
  # the only one worth a warning when the file describes itself.
  if (!is.null(mf)) {
    unmet <- setdiff(caller_req, names(dat))
    if (length(unmet))
      warning(sprintf(
        "[%s load] %d object(s) this stage expects are not in the checkpoint:\n  %s",
        label, length(unmet), paste(unmet, collapse = "\n  ")))
  }

  missing_req <- required[!required %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s load] %d REQUIRED object(s) absent from the RDS - downstream chunks that use them will fail:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))

  missing_opt <- optional[!optional %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(missing_opt) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s load] %d optional object(s) absent from the RDS:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_opt), paste(missing_opt, collapse = "\n  ")))

  # Unrequested objects are COUNTED, never listed. Every checkpoint from Stage 2
  # onward is cumulative, so this set is routinely hundreds of names long and
  # printing it buried the two messages that actually matter - an absent
  # required object, and an absent optional one - under a wall of text. The
  # count still appears in the summary line below, which is the only part of it
  # anyone reads.
  extra <- setdiff(names(dat), expected)

  # ── Publish what was loaded, for the next stage's save manifest ────────────
  # Every stage's SAVE manifest is built as "the previous stage's manifest, plus
  # my own objects", and the previous manifest is a vector defined by that
  # stage's LOAD chunk. Load a LATER checkpoint directly and that chunk never
  # runs, so the save dies on a missing .stageN_required - which is exactly the
  # resume-from-anywhere case these checkpoints now exist to support.
  #
  # Recording the manifest here breaks the dependency: .manifest_from() below
  # falls back to whatever was actually loaded, whichever chunk did it.
  assign(".stage_last_manifest",
         list(required = required, optional = optional,
              names = names(dat), label = label, path = path),
         envir = envir)

  list2env(dat, envir = envir)

  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Loaded %d object(s) | required present: %d/%d | optional present: %d/%d | unrequested: %d\n",
              label, length(dat),
              length(required) - length(missing_req), length(required),
              length(optional) - length(missing_opt), length(optional),
              length(extra)))
  invisible(names(dat))
}

#' The manifest a save chunk inherits from the stage before it.
#'
#' Looks for the named vector first - that is the normal path, when this
#' session's own load chunk built it. Falls back to the manifest carried by
#' whichever checkpoint was last loaded, which is what makes it possible to load
#' any checkpoint and still save the next one.
#'
#' `which` is "required" or "optional". Stops with something actionable rather
#' than returning character(0): a save that silently inherits nothing writes a
#' checkpoint missing every object from every earlier stage, and nothing would
#' notice until a later stage failed to find them.
.manifest_from <- function(name, which = c("required", "optional"),
                           envir = .stage_env()) {
  which <- match.arg(which)
  if (exists(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))
    return(get(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))

  lm <- if (exists(".stage_last_manifest", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))
          get(".stage_last_manifest", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE) else NULL

  if (!is.null(lm)) {
    cat(sprintf("[manifest] %s not in the session - inheriting from the %s checkpoint that was loaded.\n",
                name, lm$label))
    # For "required", everything the loaded file actually held is the honest
    # inheritance: it is what this session has, regardless of how the file that
    # produced it split required from optional.
    return(if (identical(which, "required")) lm$names else character(0))
  }

  # ── Last resort: the session itself ────────────────────────────────────────
  # No named vector and no checkpoint loaded. That is the ordinary case for a
  # session built by RUNNING chunks rather than by loading - Stage 1 through
  # Stage 3 straight down the document, or an interactive session where the
  # objects were produced rather than read. There is nothing wrong with it, and
  # a save must not refuse.
  #
  # So fall back to what Stages 4 and 5 have always done: take the manifest from
  # the environment. Every non-function, non-dotted object in scope is what this
  # stage inherited, by definition - it is the same rule, just applied later.
  #
  # Only "required" gets this. Optional means "save it if it happens to exist",
  # which is meaningless once the list IS everything that exists.
  if (identical(which, "required")) {
    nm <- setdiff(ls(envir = envir), lsf.str(envir = envir))
    nm <- nm[!startsWith(nm, ".")]
    if (length(nm)) {
      cat(sprintf(paste0("[manifest] %s not found and no checkpoint was loaded - taking the manifest\n",
                         "           from the session instead (%d object(s)). This is the normal path\n",
                         "           when the stage was RUN rather than loaded.\n"), name, length(nm)))
      return(nm)
    }
  } else {
    return(character(0))
  }

  stop(sprintf(paste0("[manifest] %s not found, no checkpoint has been loaded, and the session is\n",
                      "  empty - there is nothing to save. Run this stage's chunks, or load a\n",
                      "  checkpoint, before the save chunk."), name))
}

#' Print the Stage 1 pivot point.
.report_pivot1 <- function() {
  if (exists("pivot1")) {
    cat(sprintf("pivot1 (Stage 1 footprint centre): (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
                pivot1[1], pivot1[2], pivot1[3]))
  } else {
    cat("pivot1 NOT available.\n")
  }
}

# ============================================================
# Stages 2, 4 and 5 deliberately never load point clouds - they work purely on
# fitted ellipse geometry, which is what keeps them cheap to re-run. A handful
# of 3-D figures in those stages genuinely need raw points, so each of those
# chunks carries its own loader at the top, controlled by one toggle.
#
# Stage 3 carries it too, for a different reason: it DOES load the clouds at the
# top, but releases them again part-way through, and resuming from the Stage 3
# post-fit checkpoint skips the load entirely.
#
# Stages 1 and 6 do NOT have this block at all - they load the clouds up front
# and keep them for the whole stage, so nothing there would ever call it.
#
#   vis_load_clouds <- TRUE    read las_1 / las_2 from disk
#   vis_load_clouds <- FALSE   reuse whatever is already resident in memory
#
# Set it FALSE when the clouds are already loaded - you just ran Stage 3 in the
# same session, or an earlier figure in this stage already loaded them. Reading
# a multi-gigabyte LAS once per figure is slow and pointless. Leave it TRUE when
# running the stage standalone from its checkpoint, which is the normal case.
#
# ── FRAMES: why las_1 needs a rotation the moment it comes off disk ────────────
# las_1 sits on disk in the ORIGINAL scan frame. Stage 1A's rough vertical
# alignment (R_align_1 about align_pivot_1) was applied to las_1 IN MEMORY in
# Stage 1 and never written back - there is no writeLAS anywhere in Stage 1. So
# every measurement made downstream of Stage 1A - ellipse centres, per-stem axis
# vectors, pivot1, and the Stage 2 rotation solve R_xyz - live in the ALIGNED
# frame, not the disk frame. A figure that reads las_1 off disk and overlays any
# of that geometry is mixing two frames unless it first reapplies R_align_1.
#
# This loader therefore reconstructs the pipeline frame for las_1 as a stack of
# rigid steps, matching the Stage 2 composition (R_align_xyz_1) exactly:
#
#   x_aligned = R_align_1 (x_raw     - align_pivot_1) + align_pivot_1   (apply_align, Stage 1A)
#   x_final   = R_xyz     (x_aligned - pivot1)        + pivot1          (apply_rot,   Stage 2)
#   x_final  += t_trans_z                                              (apply_zshift, Stage 4)
#   x_final   = R_z-only  about pivot2 in XY                            (apply_zrot,   Stage 5)
#
# apply_align is the default-ON baseline: everything above stacks on the
# aligned frame, so leaving it on is what makes las_1 line up with the ellipses
# and vectors. Turn it OFF only to inspect the raw disk cloud deliberately.
# las_2 is the REFERENCE cloud - Stage 1 never rotates it and its ellipses are in
# the disk frame - so it is never transformed here.
#
# Transforms are applied to the RETURNED point frame, never baked back into the
# LAS object, so repeated calls (or a load = FALSE reuse) can never compound.
# ============================================================

#' Make point clouds available to one visualisation chunk.
#'
#' @param load         TRUE to read from disk; FALSE to reuse las_1 / las_2
#'                     already in the global environment.
#' @param las_1_path,las_2_path
#'                     Optional explicit source paths. When NULL (default) the
#'                     paths are taken from the global environment, so a caller
#'                     can either pass them or rely on the checkpoint. Only used
#'                     when load = TRUE.
#' @param apply_align  reapply the Stage 1A rough vertical alignment to las_1
#'                     (R_align_1 about align_pivot_1). Default TRUE: this is the
#'                     baseline frame every Stage 1/2 measurement lives in, so
#'                     without it the returned las_1 points do NOT match the
#'                     ellipses or axis vectors. Set FALSE only to see the raw
#'                     on-disk cloud. No-op (identity) when rough alignment was
#'                     not run; skipped with a note if the checkpoint lacks the
#'                     objects.
#' @param apply_rot    rebuild the Stage 2 XYZ rotation R_xyz (about pivot1),
#'                     stacked on the aligned frame.
#' @param apply_zshift rebuild the Stage 4 Z-translation.
#' @param apply_zrot   rebuild the Stage 5 Z-only rotation (about pivot2 in XY).
#' @param need_las2    FALSE to skip the reference cloud entirely.
#'
#' @return list(las_1, las_2, pts_1, pts_2, xyz_1, state). pts_* are plain data
#'   frames of X/Y/Z/TreeID with TreeID 0 and NA dropped (figures show stems).
#'   xyz_1 / pts_1 are in the transformed frame; the LAS objects stay on-disk.
.vis_point_clouds <- function(load,
                              las_1_path   = NULL,
                              las_2_path   = NULL,
                              apply_align  = TRUE,
                              apply_rot    = FALSE,
                              apply_zshift = FALSE,
                              apply_zrot   = FALSE,
                              need_las2    = TRUE,
                              quiet        = FALSE,
                              envir        = .stage_env()) {

  .say <- function(...) if (!quiet) cat(...)
  .g   <- function(nm) get(nm, envir = envir)
  .has <- function(nm) exists(nm, envir = envir)

  # Resolve source paths: explicit argument wins, else the global/checkpoint.
  .p1 <- if (!is.null(las_1_path)) las_1_path else
         if (.has("las_1_path")) .g("las_1_path") else NULL
  .p2 <- if (!is.null(las_2_path)) las_2_path else
         if (.has("las_2_path")) .g("las_2_path") else NULL

  if (isTRUE(load)) {

    if (is.null(.p1))
      stop("[vis loader] las_1_path not supplied and not in the environment - ",
           "pass it or load this stage's checkpoint first.")

    .say(sprintf("[vis loader] Reading las_1 from disk: %s\n", basename(.p1)))
    l1 <- lidR::readLAS(.p1)
    if (lidR::is.empty(l1)) stop("[vis loader] las_1 read as empty: ", .p1)
    l1 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(l1, x = seq_len(nrow(l1@data)),
                                 name = "point_id", desc = "Unique ID for las_1 points")
    l2 <- NULL
    if (need_las2) {
      if (is.null(.p2))
        stop("[vis loader] las_2_path not supplied and not in the environment.")
      .say(sprintf("[vis loader] Reading las_2 from disk: %s\n", basename(.p2)))
      l2 <- lidR::readLAS(.p2)
      if (lidR::is.empty(l2)) stop("[vis loader] las_2 read as empty: ", .p2)
      l2 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(l2, x = seq_len(nrow(l2@data)),
                                   name = "point_id", desc = "Unique ID for las_2 points")
    }

    assign("las_1", l1, envir = envir)
    if (!is.null(l2)) assign("las_2", l2, envir = envir)

  } else {

    if (!.has("las_1"))
      stop("[vis loader] vis_load_clouds = FALSE but las_1 is not in memory. Set it TRUE.")
    if (need_las2 && !.has("las_2"))
      stop("[vis loader] vis_load_clouds = FALSE but las_2 is not in memory. Set it TRUE.")

    l1 <- .g("las_1")
    l2 <- if (need_las2) .g("las_2") else NULL
    .say("[vis loader] Reusing the point clouds already in memory (no disk read).\n")
  }

  # ── Rebuild the transform state (las_1 only; las_2 is never transformed) ──────
  # The stack runs in pipeline order on the RETURNED frame: Stage 1A align first,
  # then the Stage 2 rotation, then the Stage 4/5 shifts. Each step is a rigid
  # transform about the pivot the corresponding stage used, matching the Stage 2
  # composition. IDENTICAL in Stages 2, 3, 4 and 5 - if it is edited, edit all four.
  xyz   <- as.matrix(l1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  state <- character(0)

  # ── Stage 1A: rough vertical alignment (raw disk -> aligned frame) ────────────
  if (isTRUE(apply_align)) {
    if (!.has("R_align_1") || !.has("align_pivot_1")) {
      .say("[vis loader] R_align_1 / align_pivot_1 not in the checkpoint - ",
           "las_1 left in the raw disk frame (no Stage 1A alignment).\n")
    } else {
      Ra <- .g("R_align_1"); pa <- as.numeric(.g("align_pivot_1"))
      xyz <- sweep(t(Ra %*% t(sweep(xyz, 2, pa))), 2, -pa)
      # Angle of the rigid rotation, for the log only: acos((tr(R) - 1) / 2).
      .ang_a <- acos(max(-1, min(1, (sum(diag(Ra)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
      state  <- c(state, sprintf("stage-1A align %.4f deg about align_pivot_1", .ang_a))
    }
  }

  # ── Stage 2: XYZ rotation R_xyz about pivot1 (aligned -> final) ───────────────
  if (isTRUE(apply_rot)) {
    if (!.has("R_xyz") || !.has("pivot1"))
      stop("[vis loader] apply_rot = TRUE but R_xyz / pivot1 not found - run the ",
           "Stage 2 rotation solve first, or reload a checkpoint that carries them.")
    R  <- .g("R_xyz"); pv <- as.numeric(.g("pivot1"))
    xyz <- sweep(t(R %*% t(sweep(xyz, 2, pv))), 2, -pv)
    .ang_x <- if (.has("angle_xyz")) .g("angle_xyz") else
              acos(max(-1, min(1, (sum(diag(R)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
    state <- c(state, sprintf("xyz-rot %.4f deg about pivot1", .ang_x))
  }

  if (isTRUE(apply_zshift)) {
    tz <- if (.has("t_trans_z_applied")) .g("t_trans_z_applied") else .g("t_trans_z")
    xyz[, 3] <- xyz[, 3] + tz
    state <- c(state, sprintf("z-shift %+.4f m", tz))
  }

  if (isTRUE(apply_zrot)) {
    # Same sign flip the Stage 5 / Stage 6 builders use: z_rotation_deg is held
    # in the standard CCW-positive convention, the 2x2 fill below evaluates to
    # the matrix for -a, so the angle is negated exactly once here.
    a  <- -.g("z_rotation_deg") * pi / 180
    Rz <- matrix(c(cos(a), -sin(a), sin(a), cos(a)), 2, 2)
    pv <- if (.has("pivot2")) .g("pivot2") else .g("pivot1")
    xc <- xyz[, 1] - pv[1]; yc <- xyz[, 2] - pv[2]
    xyz[, 1] <- Rz[1, 1] * xc + Rz[1, 2] * yc + pv[1]
    xyz[, 2] <- Rz[2, 1] * xc + Rz[2, 2] * yc + pv[2]
    state <- c(state, sprintf("z-rot %+.4f deg", .g("z_rotation_deg")))
  }

  pts_1 <- data.frame(X = xyz[, 1], Y = xyz[, 2], Z = xyz[, 3], TreeID = l1@data$TreeID)
  pts_1 <- pts_1[!is.na(pts_1$TreeID) & pts_1$TreeID != 0L, ]

  pts_2 <- NULL
  if (!is.null(l2)) {
    pts_2 <- data.frame(X = l2@data$X, Y = l2@data$Y, Z = l2@data$Z, TreeID = l2@data$TreeID)
    pts_2 <- pts_2[!is.na(pts_2$TreeID) & pts_2$TreeID != 0L, ]
  }

  .say(sprintf("[vis loader] las_1 state: %s\n",
               if (length(state)) paste(state, collapse = " + ") else "as loaded (no transform)"))
  .say(sprintf("[vis loader] stem points available - las_1: %s | las_2: %s\n",
               format(nrow(pts_1), big.mark = ","),
               if (is.null(pts_2)) "not loaded" else format(nrow(pts_2), big.mark = ",")))

  invisible(list(las_1 = l1, las_2 = l2, pts_1 = pts_1, pts_2 = pts_2,
                 xyz_1 = xyz, state = state))
}

# ============================================================
# Run tally - one cumulative record of how many things survived each filter
#
# Every stage prints its own counts, but those printouts vanish with the render
# and cannot be compared across runs. .tally() writes the same numbers into a
# single named list, `run_counts`, that travels in the checkpoints and is read
# out whole by the Stage 6 error report. A run then answers "how many pairs
# reached the Z-translation" without anyone re-reading five HTML files.
#
# Cumulative and idempotent: each call updates only the keys it names, so
# re-running one chunk refreshes that chunk's numbers and leaves the rest alone.
# It never errors - a tally is bookkeeping, and a missing count must not be able
# to stop a stage from saving.
# ============================================================
.tally <- function(...) {
  vals <- list(...)
  e    <- .stage_env()
  base <- if (exists("run_counts", envir = e, inherits = FALSE))
            get("run_counts", envir = e) else list()
  assign("run_counts", utils::modifyList(base, vals), envir = e)
  invisible(get("run_counts", envir = e))
}


#' TRUE when a cli bar can actually be seen.
#'
#' All four conditions matter: cli absent, output being knitted, a message sink
#' in the way (the batch driver), or a terminal that cannot redraw - any one of
#' them and the bar is invisible, mangled, or both.
.pb_cli_usable <- function() {
  isNamespaceLoaded("cli") || requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)
  requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE) &&
    !isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress")) &&
    sink.number(type = "message") == 0L &&
    isTRUE(try(cli::is_dynamic_tty(), silent = TRUE))
}

.pb_fmt_dur <- function(s) {
  if (!is.finite(s)) return("--")
  if (s < 90) sprintf("%.0fs", s) else if (s < 5400) sprintf("%.1fm", s / 60)
  else sprintf("%.1fh", s / 3600)
}

#' Start a bar. Returns an opaque handle for .pb_tick()/.pb_done(), or NULL.
#'
#' .envir = parent.frame() is load-bearing for the cli branch: cli ties a bar's
#' lifetime to a frame, so a bar created with the default .envir would be torn
#' down the instant this function returned and every later tick would silently
#' do nothing. That was a real bug here once.
.pb_new <- function(total, label) {
  total <- as.integer(total)
  if (!isTRUE(show_progress_bars) || is.na(total) || total < 1L) return(NULL)

  if (.pb_cli_usable()) {
    id <- cli::cli_progress_bar(
      name   = label,
      total  = total,
      format = paste0(label,
                      " {cli::pb_bar} {cli::pb_current}/{cli::pb_total}",
                      " | {cli::pb_elapsed} | {cli::pb_eta} left"),
      .envir = parent.frame())
    return(structure(list(kind = "cli", id = id), class = ".pb"))
  }

  # An ENVIRONMENT, not a list: a tick inside lapply() has to update the
  # caller's counter, and a list passed by value would not.
  st <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  st$i <- 0L; st$total <- total; st$label <- label
  st$t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]; st$last_t <- -Inf; st$last_i <- -1L
  structure(list(kind = "lines", st = st), class = ".pb")
}

.pb_tick <- function(pb, by = 1L) {
  if (is.null(pb)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (identical(pb$kind, "cli")) {
    cli::cli_progress_update(id = pb$id, inc = by)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  st <- pb$st
  st$i <- st$i + by
  now <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  step <- max(1L, as.integer(ceiling(st$total * progress_step_frac)))
  due  <- st$i >= st$total || st$i == 1L ||
          (st$i - st$last_i) >= step ||
          (now - st$last_t) >= progress_min_seconds
  if (!due) return(invisible(NULL))
  st$last_i <- st$i; st$last_t <- now
  el   <- now - st$t0
  frac <- st$i / st$total
  eta  <- if (st$i > 0L) el / st$i * (st$total - st$i) else NA_real_
  nfill <- as.integer(round(20 * frac))
  cat(sprintf("  %s [%s%s] %d/%d %3.0f%% | %s elapsed | ~%s left\n",
              st$label, strrep("#", nfill), strrep("-", 20L - nfill),
              st$i, st$total, 100 * frac, .pb_fmt_dur(el), .pb_fmt_dur(eta)))
  flush.console()
  invisible(NULL)
}

.pb_done <- function(pb) {
  if (is.null(pb)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (identical(pb$kind, "cli")) {
    cli::cli_progress_done(id = pb$id)
  } else if (pb$st$i < pb$st$total) {
    # The loop ended early (an epoch with nothing to do, say). Say so rather
    # than leaving a bar stopped at 12/25 as though something had hung.
    cat(sprintf("  %s: finished after %d of %d | %s\n", pb$st$label, pb$st$i,
                pb$st$total, .pb_fmt_dur(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - pb$st$t0)))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

## 0.3 Load the Stage 1 Checkpoint

This is a **load-only** chunk – Stage 2 never writes to the Stage 1 file. If an
object the stage asks for is absent from the `.rds`, loading continues with
whatever *is* available and raises one warning naming every missing object.

Stage 2 works from the **slice-fate ledger** – the flat frame that lists every
fitted slice, kept or removed, with the verdict that removed it. The raw
per-stem result lists are not carried; the ledger already holds one row per
slice with its geometry and status.

| object | contents |
|---|---|
| `slice_fates_*` / `slice_fates_all` | flat ledger: one row per fitted slice, geometry + verdict (the entry point) |
| `ellipses_zt_*_valid_all` | pass-1 survivors, used where only kept slices are needed |
| `ellipses_zt_*_valid2_all` | the final (pass-2) survivors |
| `ellipses_zt_*_all` / `ellipses_zt_*_refit_all` | raw and post-refit sets, summarised in the load-time inventory |

The ledger is the intended entry point – it is the only object that puts a
kept slice and a removed slice side by side in one frame.

```{r}
#| label: params-load_Stage2
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Load the Stage 1 checkpoint (load only – never saves)"


# Path to the file written by save-load_Stage1
stage1_rds_path <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/SaveLoad/Stage1_BOS_F1_aii_man.rds"

.par_apply("params-load_Stage2")
```

```{r}
#| label: load_Stage2
#| code-summary: "Load the Stage 1 checkpoint (load only – never saves)"
#| code-fold: false

.stage1_required <- c(
  # -- File paths + fit provenance (reported / reloaded by Stage 3) --
  "las_1_path",
  "las_2_path",
  "ransac_ellipse_script",
  "second_run",
  "ransac_seed",
  "ransac_track_history",
  # -- Slice band (slice-height reconstruction) --------------------
  "ransac_slice_bot",
  "ransac_slice_top",
  # -- Cloud summary + pivot ---------------------------------------
  "treeids_1",
  "treeids_2",
  "pivot1",
  # -- Rough vertical alignment (Stage 1A) -------------------------
  # Requested explicitly (Stage 1 saves them) so they load without the
  # "unrequested, loaded anyway" warning AND propagate into the Stage 2
  # checkpoint - Step 2.5 composes R_align_1 with R_xyz below, and Stage 3+
  # needs the rough rotation to reconstruct the raw-cloud -> final frame.
  "run_rough_alignment",
  "R_align_1",
  "align_pivot_1",
  "forest_axis_vec_1",
  "align_upside_down",
  # -- RANSAC fit products -----------------------------------------
  # ellipses_zt_*_all is the UNCLEANED fit: every slice, including the ones
  # later removed. It is the widest ellipse set in the checkpoint.
  "fp",
  "ellipses_zt_1_all",
  "ellipses_zt_2_all",
  # -- Cleaning: MAD multipliers + params record + pass-1 survivors -
  "mad_minor_mult",
  "mad_major_mult",
  "cp",
  "ellipses_zt_1_valid_all",
  "ellipses_zt_2_valid_all",
  # -- Temporal pairing --------------------------------------------
  "pairs_stage1"
)

.stage1_optional <- c(
  # Post-refit and pass-2 survivor sets plus the slice-fate ledger.
  # slice_fates_* is the ledger Stage 2 actually analyses (and hard-requires
  # at run time); the ellipse sets feed the load-time inventory report. They
  # are optional in the checkpoint because a Stage 1 run may skip the
  # ledger / second-pass chunks, but Stage 2 stops if the ledger is absent.
  # Stage 1A rotation ledger: the individual legs (bounding-box sideways yaw and
  # 90 deg tip, and the residual verticalisation) behind R_align_1, plus the
  # verified round-trip error. R_align_1 alone is what every composition uses;
  # these travel so Stage 6 can report WHICH rotations produced it. Optional, so
  # a checkpoint written before the 1A.0 rework still loads.
  "R_sideways_yaw",
  "R_sideways_90",
  "R_sideways_pre",
  "R_residual",
  "align_rotations",
  "align_check_max_err",
  "align_sideways",
  "align_sideways_rotated",
  "align_sw_probed",
  "align_orientation",
  "align_ud_confident",
  "ellipses_zt_1_refit_all",
  "ellipses_zt_2_refit_all",
  "ellipses_zt_1_valid2_all",
  "ellipses_zt_2_valid2_all",
  "slice_fates_1",
  "slice_fates_2",
  "slice_fates_all",
  "slice_fate_summary_1",
  "slice_fate_summary_2",
  # Stage 1A.1b density probe. Stage 2 fits nothing, so it only carries these -
  # Stage 3 reads density_slice_width_reco / density_distance_threshold_reco to
  # fit its axis-aligned ellipses on the same settings Step 1.1 used. Optional,
  # so a checkpoint written before the probe existed still loads.
  "density_stats",
  "density_stats_by_tree",
  "density_probe_width",
  "density_probe_step",
  "density_regime",
  "density_scarcity",
  "density_centre_scatter",
  "density_max_frac_centre",
  "density_max_frac_minor",
  "density_max_frac_major",
  "density_apply_regime",
  "density_slice_width_reco",
  "density_distance_threshold_reco"
)

.stage_load(stage1_rds_path, .stage1_required, .stage1_optional, label = "Stage 1")

# ── Ellipse set inventory ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reports what actually arrived, so a truncated checkpoint is obvious here
# rather than three chunks later.
.n_slices <- function(nm) {
  if (!exists(nm)) return(NA_integer_)
  x <- get(nm)
  if (is.null(x)) return(NA_integer_)
  sum(vapply(x, function(d) if (is.null(d)) 0L else nrow(d), integer(1)))
}

.fmt_n <- function(n) if (is.na(n)) "absent" else format(n, big.mark = ",")

.report_ellipse_sets <- function() {
  sets <- list(
    c("raw fit (all slices)",        "ellipses_zt_1_all",       "ellipses_zt_2_all"),
    c("pass-1 survivors",            "ellipses_zt_1_valid_all",  "ellipses_zt_2_valid_all"),
    c("post-refit set",              "ellipses_zt_1_refit_all",  "ellipses_zt_2_refit_all"),
    c("pass-2 survivors (final)",    "ellipses_zt_1_valid2_all", "ellipses_zt_2_valid2_all")
  )
  cat("Ellipse sets (slice counts):\n")
  for (s in sets)
    cat(sprintf("  %-26s las_1 %10s | las_2 %10s\n",
                s[1], .fmt_n(.n_slices(s[2])), .fmt_n(.n_slices(s[3]))))
}

.report_slice_fates <- function() {
  if (!exists("slice_fates_all") || is.null(slice_fates_all)) {
    cat("Slice fate ledger: NOT available - re-run the Stage 1 slice-fate-ledger chunk.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  tb <- table(factor(slice_fates_all$status,
                     levels = c("kept", "mad1", "consensus1", "consensus2", "mad2")),
              slice_fates_all$epoch)
  cat(sprintf("Slice fate ledger: %s fitted slice(s) across %d stem(s)\n",
              format(nrow(slice_fates_all), big.mark = ","),
              length(unique(paste(slice_fates_all$epoch, slice_fates_all$TreeID)))))
  print(tb)
  cat("  kept = survived both passes | mad1 / mad2 = MAD removal, pass 1 / pass 2\n",
      "  consensus1 = pass-1 consensus removal the refit did not recover\n",
      "  consensus2 = pass-2 consensus removal\n", sep = "")
}

cat("\n── Carried in from Stage 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
.report_pivot1()
cat(sprintf("Temporal pairs available (pairs_stage1): %d\n", nrow(pairs_stage1)))
cat("\n")
.report_ellipse_sets()
cat("\n")
.report_slice_fates()
cat("\nNo point-cloud data is loaded in this stage.\n")
```


# Stage 2 - XYZ Rotation from Stem Axis Vectors
This step estimates the global XYZ (full 3D, yaw retained) rotation between las_1
and las_2 using stem axis vectors derived from the brute-force RANSAC ellipses
fitted in Step 1.1 to all paired trees. All valid (post-cleaning) ellipses from
the full Step 1.1 RANSAC fitting range (`ransac_slice_bot`–`ransac_slice_top`)
are used for PCA stem-axis fitting and the IRLS + SVD rotation solve – Step 2.1
subsets those ellipses down to the paired trees only, but applies no additional
height sub-window on top of that. Stage 2 reuses the ellipses produced in
Step 1.1 for PCA stem-axis fitting and the IRLS + SVD rotation solve.

## 2.0 Helpers
```{r}
#| label: step2-helpers
#| code-summary: "Step 2 helper functions"

# ============================================================
# 2.0.1  Tilt-only angular difference between two unit vectors (degrees)
# Reports |tilt_a - tilt_b| where tilt = deviation from vertical.
# Used for the pre/post diagnostic table only (not the IRLS loss).
# ============================================================
compute_tilt_angle <- function(a, b) {
  a <- a / sqrt(sum(a^2))
  b <- b / sqrt(sum(b^2))
  tilt_a <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, abs(a[3])))) * 180 / pi
  tilt_b <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, abs(b[3])))) * 180 / pi
  abs(tilt_a - tilt_b)
}

# ============================================================
# 2.0.2  Axis-vector segment builder for 3-D visualisation
# Projects each stem's regression axis vector through its
# point-cloud centroid and returns endpoint pairs
# (x0/y0/z0 -> x1/y1/z1) ready for plotly line traces.
# half_len_xy must be defined in the calling scope.
# ============================================================
make_vec_segs_xy <- function(vecs_df, pts_df, local_cx, local_cy) {
  centroids <- pts_df |>
    dplyr::group_by(TreeID) |>
    dplyr::summarise(cx = mean(X), cy = mean(Y), cz = mean(Z), .groups = "drop")
  dplyr::inner_join(vecs_df, centroids, by = "TreeID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      x0 = (cx - vx * half_len_xy) - local_cx,
      y0 = (cy - vy * half_len_xy) - local_cy,
      z0 =  cz - vz * half_len_xy,
      x1 = (cx + vx * half_len_xy) - local_cx,
      y1 = (cy + vy * half_len_xy) - local_cy,
      z1 =  cz + vz * half_len_xy
    )
}

# ============================================================
# Weighted Kabsch rotation (SVD)
# ============================================================
solve_rotation_weighted <- function(src, tgt, w) {
  w_sum <- sum(w)
  if (!is.finite(w_sum) || w_sum < 1e-10) {
    warning("solve_rotation_weighted: weights sum to ~0 or non-finite; falling back to uniform weights.")
    w <- rep(1, length(w))
    w_sum <- sum(w)
  }
  w  <- w / w_sum
  H  <- t(src * w) %*% tgt
  sv <- svd(H)
  d  <- det(sv$v %*% t(sv$u))
  D  <- diag(c(1, 1, sign(d)))
  sv$v %*% D %*% t(sv$u)
}
```

### Vis - Ellipse area vs height – kept and MAD-removed slices

Area is recomputed here as `pi * semi_a * semi_b`; nothing upstream stores it,
since the cleaning stages score the semi-minor and semi-major axes separately
rather than their product. The product is invariant to the `sort_axes` swap, so
`semi_a`/`semi_b` are used directly rather than `major_len`/`minor_len`.

Only three verdicts appear: `kept`, `mad1` and `mad2`. Consensus removals are
excluded by design – `consensus1` slices were never recovered by the refit and
`consensus2` slices failed neighbour agreement, so neither belongs on a plot
about axis-magnitude outliers.

Pagination follows `pairs_stage1`: each page holds one temporal pair, the las_1
stem on the left and the las_2 stem it was matched to on the right, sharing
their axes so the two epochs can be read against each other. A stem with no
partner still gets a page, unless `area_drop_unpaired` is set.

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-ellipse-area-vs-height
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Ellipse area against slice height, one temporal pair per page; circle = kept, x = removed by MAD"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
area_epochs      <- c("las_1", "las_2")   # which epochs to draw
area_treeids     <- NULL                  # NULL = every stem in the ledger
area_pairs_page  <- 1L                    # temporal pairs per page; NULL = all in one grid
area_facet_ncol  <- 2L                    # 2 = las_1 left, its las_2 partner right
area_drop_unpaired <- FALSE                # TRUE = show only stems with a partner
# Scales are fixed WITHIN a page, so a pair shares its axes and the two epochs
# can be read against each other. Each page still gets its own range.
area_free_y      <- FALSE                 # TRUE = every panel scaled independently
area_flip        <- FALSE                 # TRUE = height on y, area on x
area_use_abs_z   <- FALSE                 # TRUE = absolute slice_z instead of h
area_units_cm2   <- FALSE                 # TRUE = cm^2 instead of m^2

# Matches fig-refit-clean2-slice-status, so the two figures read consistently.
area_col_kept <- "#2C3E50"
area_col_mad1 <- "purple"
area_col_mad2 <- "#F07C10"

.par_apply("params-fig-ellipse-area-vs-height")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ellipse-area-vs-height
#| code-summary: "Ellipse area against slice height, one temporal pair per page; circle = kept, x = removed by MAD"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| results: asis

# ── Source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!exists("slice_fates_all") || is.null(slice_fates_all))
  stop("slice_fates_all not found - it travels in the Stage 1 checkpoint.")

area_df <- slice_fates_all[slice_fates_all$epoch %in% area_epochs &
                           slice_fates_all$status %in% c("kept", "mad1", "mad2"), ,
                           drop = FALSE]

if (!is.null(area_treeids))
  area_df <- area_df[area_df$TreeID %in% as.character(area_treeids), , drop = FALSE]

if (nrow(area_df) == 0L)
  stop("No kept or MAD-removed slices match the current area_* filters.")

# ── Resolve temporal pairs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each page holds one pair: the las_1 stem and the las_2 stem it was matched to
# in Stage 1. A stem with no partner still gets a page of its own rather than
# being dropped silently.
if (!exists("pairs_stage1") || is.null(pairs_stage1) || nrow(pairs_stage1) == 0L)
  stop("pairs_stage1 not found - it travels in the Stage 1 checkpoint.")

.pl <- data.frame(
  TreeID_1 = as.character(pairs_stage1$TreeID_1),
  TreeID_2 = as.character(pairs_stage1$TreeID_2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
.pl <- unique(.pl[!is.na(.pl$TreeID_1) & !is.na(.pl$TreeID_2), , drop = FALSE])
.pl$pair_id  <- sprintf("las_1 %s \u2194 las_2 %s", .pl$TreeID_1, .pl$TreeID_2)
.pl$pair_ord <- seq_len(nrow(.pl))

# A TreeID is matched against the column for its own epoch, so an ID that
# happens to exist in both clouds is never cross-assigned.
.hit <- ifelse(area_df$epoch == "las_1",
               match(area_df$TreeID, .pl$TreeID_1),
               match(area_df$TreeID, .pl$TreeID_2))

area_df$pair_id  <- .pl$pair_id[.hit]
area_df$pair_ord <- .pl$pair_ord[.hit]

.orphan <- is.na(area_df$pair_ord)
if (any(.orphan)) {
  if (area_drop_unpaired) {
    cat(sprintf("Dropping %d slice(s) from %d stem(s) with no temporal partner.\n",
                sum(.orphan), length(unique(area_df$TreeID[.orphan]))))
    area_df <- area_df[!.orphan, , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    area_df$pair_id[.orphan] <- sprintf("unpaired - %s TreeID %s",
                                        area_df$epoch[.orphan],
                                        area_df$TreeID[.orphan])
    # Orphans sort after every real pair, in a stable order.
    area_df$pair_ord[.orphan] <- nrow(.pl) +
      as.integer(factor(area_df$pair_id[.orphan]))
    cat(sprintf("%d stem(s) have no temporal partner and get a page each.\n",
                length(unique(area_df$pair_id[.orphan]))))
  }
}

if (nrow(area_df) == 0L) stop("Nothing left to plot after pair resolution.")

# ── Derived columns ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
area_df$area <- pi * area_df$semi_a * area_df$semi_b
if (area_units_cm2) area_df$area <- area_df$area * 1e4

area_df$height <- if (area_use_abs_z) area_df$slice_z else area_df$h

# Verdict as a factor, so the legend order is fixed even when a stem has no
# removals of one kind.
area_df$verdict <- factor(
  area_df$status,
  levels = c("kept", "mad1", "mad2"),
  labels = c("kept", "MAD pass 1", "MAD pass 2")
)

area_df$stem <- sprintf("%s | TreeID %s", area_df$epoch, area_df$TreeID)

# Panels are ordered by pair, then epoch within the pair - so with ncol = 2 the
# las_1 stem lands on the left and its las_2 partner on the right.
.stem_key <- unique(data.frame(stem     = area_df$stem,
                               pair_ord = area_df$pair_ord,
                               epoch    = area_df$epoch,
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
.stem_key <- .stem_key[order(.stem_key$pair_ord, .stem_key$epoch), ]
area_df$stem <- factor(area_df$stem, levels = .stem_key$stem)

.pair_key <- unique(area_df[, c("pair_id", "pair_ord")])
.pair_key <- .pair_key[order(.pair_key$pair_ord), ]
area_df$pair_id <- factor(area_df$pair_id, levels = .pair_key$pair_id)

.area_lab <- if (area_units_cm2) expression(Ellipse~area~(cm^2)) else
                                 expression(Ellipse~area~(m^2))
.h_lab    <- if (area_use_abs_z) "Slice centre height, absolute z (m)" else
                                 "Slice centre height above stem base (m)"

# ── Plot builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.area_plot <- function(d, page_lab = NULL) {

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = height, y = area,
                     colour = verdict, shape = verdict)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = verdict, stroke = ifelse(verdict == "kept", 0.4, 0.9)),
               alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("kept" = 16, "MAD pass 1" = 4, "MAD pass 2" = 4),
                       drop = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("kept"       = area_col_kept,
                                   "MAD pass 1" = area_col_mad1,
                                   "MAD pass 2" = area_col_mad2),
                        drop = FALSE) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c("kept" = 1.5, "MAD pass 1" = 2.4, "MAD pass 2" = 2.4),
                      drop = FALSE, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~ stem, ncol = area_facet_ncol,
               scales = if (area_free_y) "free" else "fixed") +
    labs(
      title    = paste0("Ellipse area against slice height",
                        if (is.null(page_lab)) "" else paste0(" - ", page_lab)),
      subtitle = "Circle = kept by both cleaning passes | x = removed by a MAD filter (consensus removals excluded)",
      x = .h_lab, y = .area_lab, colour = NULL, shape = NULL
    ) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  if (area_flip) p <- p + coord_flip()
  p
}

# ── Draw ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.area_stems <- levels(droplevels(area_df$stem))
.area_pairs <- levels(droplevels(area_df$pair_id))

area_plots <- if (is.null(area_pairs_page) || length(.area_pairs) <= area_pairs_page) {
  list(.area_plot(area_df))
} else {
  pages <- split(.area_pairs, ceiling(seq_along(.area_pairs) / area_pairs_page))
  lapply(seq_along(pages), function(i)
    .area_plot(area_df[area_df$pair_id %in% pages[[i]], , drop = FALSE],
               if (length(pages[[i]]) == 1L)
                 sprintf("%s (%d of %d)", pages[[i]], i, length(pages))
               else sprintf("page %d of %d", i, length(pages))))
}

# One plot per page. The break is emitted between plots, never after the last
# one, so no trailing blank page is produced. HTML has no pages, so it gets a
# CSS print-break that only takes effect when the document is printed to PDF.
.page_break <- function() {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    cat("\n\\newpage\n")
  } else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    cat('\n<div style="page-break-after:always;break-after:page;"></div>\n')
  } else {
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}

for (i in seq_along(area_plots)) {
  print(area_plots[[i]])
  if (i < length(area_plots)) .page_break()
}

# ── Counts behind the figure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
area_plot_summary <- as.data.frame(
  table(stem = droplevels(area_df$stem), verdict = area_df$verdict)
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = verdict, values_from = Freq)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nPlotted %d slice(s) across %d stem(s) in %d pair page(s): %d kept | %d MAD pass 1 | %d MAD pass 2\n",
  nrow(area_df), length(.area_stems), length(.area_pairs),
  sum(area_df$verdict == "kept"),
  sum(area_df$verdict == "MAD pass 1"),
  sum(area_df$verdict == "MAD pass 2")))
```

### Vis - Inliers

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-ellipse-area-vs-height-kept
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Ellipse area against slice height, kept ellipses only, so the y axis is scaled by the inliers"


# ── Parameters ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything else - epochs, pairing, pagination, units, flip - is inherited from
# the chunk above, so the two figures stay in step. Changing a parameter there
# changes it here.
areak_zoom  <- "data"        # "data"     = fit the kept points exactly
                             # "quantile" = clip to a quantile band, for stems
                             #              whose kept set still holds a flier
                             # "manual"   = use areak_ylim
areak_qlo   <- 0.00          # lower quantile when areak_zoom = "quantile"
areak_qhi   <- 0.99          # upper quantile
areak_pad   <- 0.04          # padding as a fraction of the band
areak_ylim  <- NULL          # c(lo, hi) in the plot's area units, for "manual"

.par_apply("params-fig-ellipse-area-vs-height-kept")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ellipse-area-vs-height-kept
#| code-summary: "Ellipse area against slice height, kept ellipses only, so the y axis is scaled by the inliers"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| results: asis

if (!exists("area_df") || is.null(area_df))
  stop("Run fig-ellipse-area-vs-height first - this chunk reuses its area_df.")

# ── Kept only ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
areak_df <- area_df[area_df$verdict == "kept", , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(areak_df) == 0L) stop("No kept ellipses to draw.")

# A stem whose every slice was MAD-removed has no panel here. That is a real
# finding rather than a plotting gap, so it is named instead of dropped quietly.
.gone_stems <- setdiff(levels(droplevels(area_df$stem)),
                       levels(droplevels(areak_df$stem)))
if (length(.gone_stems) > 0L)
  cat(sprintf("%d stem(s) have no kept ellipses and so no panel below: %s\n",
              length(.gone_stems), paste(.gone_stems, collapse = ", ")))

areak_df$stem    <- droplevels(areak_df$stem)
areak_df$pair_id <- droplevels(areak_df$pair_id)

# ── Zoom band ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Computed per page, because scales are fixed within a page and a band taken
# across every stem at once would defeat the point of zooming. The band is
# applied through coord_*, never through scale limits: coord zooms the view,
# scale limits DELETE the points outside it, which would silently change what
# the panel is showing.
.areak_band <- function(d) {
  if (identical(areak_zoom, "manual")) return(areak_ylim)
  if (!identical(areak_zoom, "quantile")) return(NULL)
  v <- d$area[is.finite(d$area)]
  if (length(v) < 2L) return(NULL)
  q <- unname(quantile(v, c(areak_qlo, areak_qhi), na.rm = TRUE))
  pad <- diff(q) * areak_pad
  if (!is.finite(pad) || pad <= 0) pad <- abs(q[2]) * 0.05
  c(q[1] - pad, q[2] + pad)
}

# ── Plot builder ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.areak_plot <- function(d, page_lab = NULL) {

  lim <- .areak_band(d)
  n_out <- if (is.null(lim)) 0L else
             sum(d$area < lim[1] | d$area > lim[2], na.rm = TRUE)

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = height, y = area)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = stem), colour = area_col_kept,
              linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.45) +
    geom_point(colour = area_col_kept, shape = 16, size = 1.5,
               stroke = 0.4, alpha = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ stem, ncol = area_facet_ncol,
               scales = if (area_free_y) "free" else "fixed") +
    labs(
      title    = paste0("Ellipse area against slice height, kept ellipses only",
                        if (is.null(page_lab)) "" else paste0(" - ", page_lab)),
      subtitle = paste0(
        "MAD-removed slices withheld so the y range is set by the inliers",
        if (is.null(lim)) "" else
          sprintf(" | view clipped to %.4g - %.4g%s", lim[1], lim[2],
                  if (n_out > 0L) sprintf(", %d point(s) outside the view", n_out) else "")),
      x = .h_lab, y = .area_lab
    ) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  # coord_flip takes its own ylim, so the two branches cannot be merged.
  if (area_flip) {
    p <- p + coord_flip(ylim = lim)
  } else if (!is.null(lim)) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = lim)
  }
  p
}

# ── Draw ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Paginated on the same rule as the chunk above, so page i here is page i there
# - except where a pair lost every one of its slices, which is why the page
# count is reported rather than assumed to match.
.areak_pairs <- levels(areak_df$pair_id)

areak_plots <- if (is.null(area_pairs_page) || length(.areak_pairs) <= area_pairs_page) {
  list(.areak_plot(areak_df))
} else {
  pages <- split(.areak_pairs, ceiling(seq_along(.areak_pairs) / area_pairs_page))
  lapply(seq_along(pages), function(i)
    .areak_plot(areak_df[areak_df$pair_id %in% pages[[i]], , drop = FALSE],
                if (length(pages[[i]]) == 1L)
                  sprintf("%s (%d of %d)", pages[[i]], i, length(pages))
                else sprintf("page %d of %d", i, length(pages))))
}

for (i in seq_along(areak_plots)) {
  print(areak_plots[[i]])
  if (i < length(areak_plots)) .page_break()
}

# ── Counts behind the figure ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# The range comparison is the point of the chunk: it says how much of the
# previous figure's y extent was being spent on slices already thrown away.
.rng_all  <- range(area_df$area,  na.rm = TRUE)
.rng_keep <- range(areak_df$area, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nKept-only figure: %d slice(s) across %d stem(s) in %d pair page(s)\n",
  nrow(areak_df), nlevels(areak_df$stem), length(.areak_pairs)))
cat(sprintf("  y range with removals: %.4g - %.4g | kept only: %.4g - %.4g",
            .rng_all[1], .rng_all[2], .rng_keep[1], .rng_keep[2]))
cat(if (diff(.rng_keep) > 0)
      sprintf(" (%.1fx tighter)\n", diff(.rng_all) / diff(.rng_keep)) else "\n")

areak_plot_summary <- as.data.frame(table(stem = areak_df$stem))
names(areak_plot_summary) <- c("stem", "n_kept")
```

## 2.1 Stem filtering and straightness gate

Three filters run in sequence, each narrowing the stem set the next one
scores. The pre-filter removes stems that are unusable in absolute terms; the
MAD filter removes stems that are usable but unusually sparse for their own
epoch; the straightness gate removes stems that are well-reconstructed but
geometrically bent. All three propagate across temporal pairs – a pair needs
two usable, sufficiently-dense, sufficiently-straight stems, so a failure on
either side removes both.

### 2.1.1 Vertical-span and kept-ellipse pre-filter

Two absolute gates, applied before the MAD filter. Both are fixed thresholds
rather than distribution-relative: a stem that fails either is unusable in its
own right, regardless of how the rest of the epoch looks.

1. **Vertical span** – the stem must have at least two kept ellipses separated
   by `prefilter_min_span` metres in height. A stem whose survivors are all
   bunched into one short section has no lever arm for an axis fit, even if it
   has plenty of them.
2. **Kept count** – the stem must have at least `prefilter_min_kept` kept
   ellipses.

**Pair propagation**: a temporal pair needs two usable stems, so when either
side fails, both are removed. This runs after both gates, so a stem that passes
everything on its own merits can still be removed for its partner's failure –
that is the intended behaviour, and the reason column records it as such.

Running this before the MAD filter matters: the removals here change the
kept-count distribution the MAD stage scores against, so the median and MAD are
computed over usable stems only rather than being dragged down by stems that
were never viable.

```{r}
#| label: params-stem-prefilter-span-count
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Absolute stem gates: >= 2 kept ellipses >= 5 m apart, and a kept-ellipse count floor; failures propagate across the pair"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
run_stem_prefilter   <- TRUE
prefilter_min_span   <- 4.0    # m between the lowest and highest kept ellipse
prefilter_min_kept   <- 20L    # kept ellipses required (dense regime)

# ── Sparse regime ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# When Stage 1A.1b put the pair in the SPARSE regime, Step 1.1 fitted 10 cm
# slices instead of 5 cm - which is half as many slices over the same stem, so
# the same stem can only ever reach about half the kept-ellipse count. Holding
# the count gate at 20 would therefore fail stems for the slice thickness rather
# than for their reconstruction. The SPAN gate is left alone: it is measured in
# metres and does not move with slice thickness.
#
# NULL = keep prefilter_min_kept whatever the regime.
prefilter_min_kept_sparse <- 10L
prefilter_span_on    <- "kept" # "kept" = span over kept slices only
                               # "fitted" = span over every fitted slice
prefilter_drop_unpaired <- TRUE  # TRUE = a stem with no temporal partner is removed

.par_apply("params-stem-prefilter-span-count")
```

```{r}
#| label: stem-prefilter-span-count
#| code-summary: "Absolute stem gates: >= 2 kept ellipses >= 5 m apart, and a kept-ellipse count floor; failures propagate across the pair"

# ── Count gate from the Stage 1A.1b density regime ───────────────────────────
# A NO-OP outside the sparse regime, or when the probe did not run. Applied here
# rather than in the params chunk so the gate that is actually used is visible
# beside the gate that uses it.
if (exists("density_scarcity") && isTRUE(density_scarcity > 0) &&
    exists("prefilter_min_kept_sparse") && !is.null(prefilter_min_kept_sparse)) {
  cat(sprintf("[2.1] scarce cloud (t = %.2f): kept-ellipse gate %d -> %d\n",
              density_scarcity, prefilter_min_kept, as.integer(prefilter_min_kept_sparse)))
  prefilter_min_kept <- as.integer(prefilter_min_kept_sparse)
}

# ── Per-stem measurements ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The universe is the fate SUMMARY, not the ledger: a stem with zero kept
# ellipses has no rows in the ledger and would otherwise vanish rather than
# fail, which is the exact case these gates exist to catch.
.pre_table <- function(fate_summary, fates, label) {

  if (is.null(fate_summary) || nrow(fate_summary) == 0L) return(NULL)

  d <- data.frame(
    epoch    = label,
    TreeID   = as.character(fate_summary$TreeID),
    n_fitted = as.integer(fate_summary$n_fitted),
    n_kept   = as.integer(fate_summary$n_kept),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # The ledger summary already carries the kept z-range; recompute only if an
  # older checkpoint predates those columns.
  if (all(c("z_min_kept", "z_max_kept") %in% names(fate_summary)) &&
      prefilter_span_on == "kept") {
    d$z_lo <- as.numeric(fate_summary$z_min_kept)
    d$z_hi <- as.numeric(fate_summary$z_max_kept)
  } else {
    d$z_lo <- NA_real_
    d$z_hi <- NA_real_
    if (!is.null(fates) && nrow(fates) > 0L) {
      src <- if (prefilter_span_on == "kept")
               fates[fates$status == "kept", , drop = FALSE] else fates
      if (nrow(src) > 0L) {
        rng <- tapply(src$slice_z, as.character(src$TreeID),
                      function(z) range(z, na.rm = TRUE))
        m <- match(d$TreeID, names(rng))
        d$z_lo <- vapply(seq_along(m), function(i)
          if (is.na(m[i])) NA_real_ else rng[[m[i]]][1], numeric(1))
        d$z_hi <- vapply(seq_along(m), function(i)
          if (is.na(m[i])) NA_real_ else rng[[m[i]]][2], numeric(1))
      }
    }
  }

  # Span is a difference of slice_z, so it is identical whether measured on
  # absolute z or on the ledger's h - the offset cancels.
  d$span <- d$z_hi - d$z_lo
  d
}

.fs_1 <- if (exists("slice_fate_summary_1")) slice_fate_summary_1 else NULL
.fs_2 <- if (exists("slice_fate_summary_2")) slice_fate_summary_2 else NULL
.sf_1 <- if (exists("slice_fates_1"))        slice_fates_1        else NULL
.sf_2 <- if (exists("slice_fates_2"))        slice_fates_2        else NULL

if (is.null(.fs_1) && is.null(.fs_2))
  stop("slice_fate_summary_1/2 not found - they travel in the Stage 1 checkpoint.")

pre_1 <- .pre_table(.fs_1, .sf_1, "las_1")
pre_2 <- .pre_table(.fs_2, .sf_2, "las_2")

if (run_stem_prefilter) {

  # ── Gate 1 and Gate 2, evaluated independently ──────────────────────────────
  # A stem with fewer than 2 kept ellipses has an NA span; treat that as a span
  # failure rather than letting NA propagate into the logical result.
  .apply_gates <- function(d) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    d$fail_span  <- is.na(d$span) | d$span < prefilter_min_span
    d$fail_count <- is.na(d$n_kept) | d$n_kept < prefilter_min_kept
    d$fail_self  <- d$fail_span | d$fail_count
    d
  }

  pre_1 <- .apply_gates(pre_1)
  pre_2 <- .apply_gates(pre_2)

  # ── Pair propagation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (!exists("pairs_stage1") || is.null(pairs_stage1) || nrow(pairs_stage1) == 0L)
    stop("pairs_stage1 not found - it travels in the Stage 1 checkpoint.")

  .pl <- data.frame(
    TreeID_1 = as.character(pairs_stage1$TreeID_1),
    TreeID_2 = as.character(pairs_stage1$TreeID_2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  .pl <- unique(.pl[!is.na(.pl$TreeID_1) & !is.na(.pl$TreeID_2), , drop = FALSE])

  .fail_of <- function(d, ids) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(rep(TRUE, length(ids)))
    hit <- match(ids, d$TreeID)
    # A paired ID with no row here was never fitted at all, so it fails.
    ifelse(is.na(hit), TRUE, d$fail_self[hit])
  }

  .pl$fail_1    <- .fail_of(pre_1, .pl$TreeID_1)
  .pl$fail_2    <- .fail_of(pre_2, .pl$TreeID_2)
  .pl$pair_fail <- .pl$fail_1 | .pl$fail_2

  # A stem is removed if it failed itself, OR its partner failed, OR (when
  # required) it has no partner at all.
  .mark <- function(d, side) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    own  <- if (side == 1L) .pl$TreeID_1 else .pl$TreeID_2
    hit  <- match(d$TreeID, own)
    d$paired       <- !is.na(hit)
    d$fail_partner <- !is.na(hit) & .pl$pair_fail[hit] & !d$fail_self
    d$fail_unpaired <- prefilter_drop_unpaired & !d$paired
    d$removed      <- d$fail_self | d$fail_partner | d$fail_unpaired

    d$reason <- ifelse(!d$removed, "pass",
                mapply(function(sp, ct, pa, up) {
                  r <- c(if (sp) "span", if (ct) "count",
                         if (pa) "partner", if (up) "unpaired")
                  paste(r, collapse = "+")
                }, d$fail_span, d$fail_count, d$fail_partner, d$fail_unpaired))
    d
  }

  pre_1 <- .mark(pre_1, 1L)
  pre_2 <- .mark(pre_2, 2L)

  prefilter_scores <- rbind(pre_1, pre_2)

  # ── Report ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cat(sprintf(paste0("\n\u2500\u2500 Stem pre-filter \u2500\u2500\n",
                     "Gate 1: >= 2 kept ellipses spanning >= %.1f m (measured on %s slices)\n",
                     "Gate 2: >= %d kept ellipses\n",
                     "Failures propagate to the partner stem; unpaired stems %s\n\n"),
              prefilter_min_span, prefilter_span_on, prefilter_min_kept,
              if (prefilter_drop_unpaired) "are removed" else "are kept"))

  .report <- function(d, label) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) {
      cat(sprintf("[%s] no stems.\n", label)); return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    cat(sprintf("[%s] %d stem(s) in -> %d kept, %d removed",
                label, nrow(d), sum(!d$removed), sum(d$removed)))
    cat(sprintf("  (span %d | count %d | partner %d | unpaired %d)\n",
                sum(d$fail_span), sum(d$fail_count),
                sum(d$fail_partner), sum(d$fail_unpaired)))
    if (any(d$removed)) {
      sub <- d[d$removed, c("TreeID", "n_fitted", "n_kept", "span", "reason")]
      sub$span <- round(sub$span, 2)
      print(sub[order(sub$reason, sub$n_kept), ], row.names = FALSE)
    }
    invisible(NULL)
  }

  .report(pre_1, "las_1")
  cat("\n")
  .report(pre_2, "las_2")

  cat(sprintf("\nTemporal pairs: %d -> %d (%d lost)\n",
              nrow(.pl), sum(!.pl$pair_fail), sum(.pl$pair_fail)))

  # ── Surviving stem lists ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  stems_pre_kept_1    <- if (is.null(pre_1)) character(0) else pre_1$TreeID[!pre_1$removed]
```
