```{r}
  stems_pre_kept_2    <- if (is.null(pre_2)) character(0) else pre_2$TreeID[!pre_2$removed]
  stems_pre_removed_1 <- if (is.null(pre_1)) character(0) else pre_1$TreeID[pre_1$removed]
  stems_pre_removed_2 <- if (is.null(pre_2)) character(0) else pre_2$TreeID[pre_2$removed]

  pairs_prefilter <- pairs_stage1[
    as.character(pairs_stage1$TreeID_1) %in% stems_pre_kept_1 &
    as.character(pairs_stage1$TreeID_2) %in% stems_pre_kept_2, , drop = FALSE]

  # ── Filtered views for the downstream MAD filter ────────────────────────────
  # The MAD stage must score the SURVIVORS only, so it is handed these rather
  # than the full Stage 1 objects.
  slice_fate_summary_1_pre <- if (is.null(.fs_1)) NULL else
    .fs_1[as.character(.fs_1$TreeID) %in% stems_pre_kept_1, , drop = FALSE]
  slice_fate_summary_2_pre <- if (is.null(.fs_2)) NULL else
    .fs_2[as.character(.fs_2$TreeID) %in% stems_pre_kept_2, , drop = FALSE]

  slice_fates_1_pre <- if (is.null(.sf_1)) NULL else
    .sf_1[as.character(.sf_1$TreeID) %in% stems_pre_kept_1, , drop = FALSE]
  slice_fates_2_pre <- if (is.null(.sf_2)) NULL else
    .sf_2[as.character(.sf_2$TreeID) %in% stems_pre_kept_2, , drop = FALSE]

} else {

  cat("\nStem pre-filter SKIPPED (run_stem_prefilter = FALSE).\n")
  prefilter_scores <- NULL
  stems_pre_kept_1 <- if (is.null(pre_1)) character(0) else pre_1$TreeID
  stems_pre_kept_2 <- if (is.null(pre_2)) character(0) else pre_2$TreeID
  stems_pre_removed_1 <- stems_pre_removed_2 <- character(0)
  pairs_prefilter <- if (exists("pairs_stage1")) pairs_stage1 else NULL
  slice_fate_summary_1_pre <- .fs_1; slice_fate_summary_2_pre <- .fs_2
  slice_fates_1_pre        <- .sf_1; slice_fates_2_pre        <- .sf_2
}

# ── Parameter record ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pf <- list(
  method        = "absolute_span_and_kept_count_with_pair_propagation",
  min_span_m    = prefilter_min_span,
  min_kept      = prefilter_min_kept,
  span_measured_on = prefilter_span_on,
  drop_unpaired = prefilter_drop_unpaired,
  run           = run_stem_prefilter
)
```

### 2.1.2 Stem-level MAD filter on kept-ellipse count

The pre-filter removed stems that fail in absolute terms. This one removes
stems that fail *relative to their own epoch*: a stem whose surviving ellipse
count sits far below its epoch's median has too little of its profile
reconstructed to carry a reliable axis, however good the few remaining fits
are.

Three things this chunk depends on:

**It scores the pre-filter survivors**, not the full Stage 1 population. It
picks up `slice_fate_summary_*_pre` automatically when the pre-filter has run
and falls back to the unfiltered objects when it hasn't, reporting which it
used. Scoring the full population would let stems the pre-filter already
condemned drag the median down and mask the marginal cases this stage exists
to find.

**It scores paired stems only.** Whatever set arrives from the pre-filter, an
unpaired stem is removed from the scored distribution before the median and MAD
are taken. An unpaired stem is dropped ahead of the rotation solve regardless of
its count, so including it would only shift the median/MAD that every paired
stem is then judged against. This is enforced in the MAD stage itself, so it
holds even when the pre-filter is skipped or run with
`prefilter_drop_unpaired = FALSE`.

**The test is one-sided.** Only `z < -mult` removes a stem. An unusually high
count is a densely scanned stem, which is the good case, so the upper tail is
never cut.

**Each epoch is scored separately.** las_1 and las_2 are different scans with
different point densities, so a shared threshold would silently penalise the
sparser epoch.

Removals propagate across temporal pairs, matching the pre-filter: a pair needs
two usable stems, so when either side is cut, both go.

```{r}
#| label: params-stem-mad-kept-count
#| code-summary: "Parameters - One-sided MAD filter on kept-ellipse count per stem; z left, counts right, stems ordered by count"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
run_stem_mad       <- TRUE

stem_mad_mult      <- 3.0                 # chosen multiplier (the red line)
stem_mad_min_n     <- 5L                  # need this many stems in an epoch to run
stem_mad_grid      <- c(2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5)  # multipliers compared in the sweep table
stem_mad_ref_lines <- c(2, 4)             # extra grey guides on the plot
stem_mad_pad       <- 0.4                 # y padding beyond the observed z range
stem_mad_plot      <- TRUE
stem_mad_label_rotate <- 90               # x tick label angle
stem_mad_propagate_pairs <- TRUE          # a cut stem takes its partner with it

.par_apply("params-stem-mad-kept-count")
```

```{r}
#| label: stem-mad-kept-count
#| code-summary: "One-sided MAD filter on kept-ellipse count per stem; z left, counts right, stems ordered by count"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5


.col_1   <- if (exists("COL_1")) COL_1 else "#2C7FB8"
.col_2   <- if (exists("COL_2")) COL_2 else "#31A354"
.col_cut <- "#D7263D"
.col_par <- "grey45"

# ── Source: pre-filter survivors when available ───────────────────────────────
# The `_pre` objects are written by stem-prefilter-span-count. Falling back to
# the unfiltered objects keeps this chunk runnable on its own, but the fallback
# is announced rather than silent, because the two give different medians.
.have_pre <- exists("slice_fate_summary_1_pre") || exists("slice_fate_summary_2_pre")

.fs_1 <- if (exists("slice_fate_summary_1_pre")) slice_fate_summary_1_pre else
         if (exists("slice_fate_summary_1"))     slice_fate_summary_1     else NULL
.fs_2 <- if (exists("slice_fate_summary_2_pre")) slice_fate_summary_2_pre else
         if (exists("slice_fate_summary_2"))     slice_fate_summary_2     else NULL
.sf_1 <- if (exists("slice_fates_1_pre"))        slice_fates_1_pre        else
         if (exists("slice_fates_1"))            slice_fates_1            else NULL
.sf_2 <- if (exists("slice_fates_2_pre"))        slice_fates_2_pre        else
         if (exists("slice_fates_2"))            slice_fates_2            else NULL

if (is.null(.fs_1) && is.null(.sf_1) && is.null(.fs_2) && is.null(.sf_2))
  stop("No slice fate data found - it travels in the Stage 1 checkpoint.")

cat(sprintf("Scoring the %s stem set.\n",
            if (.have_pre) "PRE-FILTERED" else "UNFILTERED (pre-filter not run)"))

# The pair table follows the same rule: use the pre-filtered pairs if present.
.pairs_in <- if (exists("pairs_prefilter") && !is.null(pairs_prefilter)) pairs_prefilter else
             if (exists("pairs_stage1"))                                 pairs_stage1   else NULL

# ── Kept-ellipse count per stem ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Preferred source is the fate summary, which lists every stem that had at least
# one FITTED slice – including stems whose kept count is zero. Counting from the
# ledger alone would make those stems vanish rather than score as the worst
# case, which is the opposite of what this filter is for.
.stem_counts <- function(fate_summary, fates, label) {

  if (!is.null(fate_summary) && nrow(fate_summary) > 0L) {
    return(data.frame(
      epoch    = label,
      TreeID   = as.character(fate_summary$TreeID),
      n_kept   = as.integer(fate_summary$n_kept),
      n_fitted = as.integer(fate_summary$n_fitted),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }

  if (is.null(fates) || nrow(fates) == 0L) return(NULL)
  tid  <- unique(as.character(fates$TreeID))
  kept <- table(factor(as.character(fates$TreeID)[fates$status == "kept"], levels = tid))
  fit  <- table(factor(as.character(fates$TreeID),                          levels = tid))
  data.frame(epoch = label, TreeID = tid,
             n_kept = as.integer(kept), n_fitted = as.integer(fit),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

stem_counts_1 <- .stem_counts(.fs_1, .sf_1, "las_1")
stem_counts_2 <- .stem_counts(.fs_2, .sf_2, "las_2")

# ── Restrict the scored set to PAIRED stems ───────────────────────────────────
# The median and MAD must be computed over the stems this stage can actually
# use - the ones with a temporal partner. An unpaired stem is dropped before the
# rotation solve regardless of its count, so letting it sit in the distribution
# only shifts the median/MAD that every paired stem is then judged against.
#
# This is enforced here, in the MAD stage itself, rather than relying on the
# pre-filter having removed unpaired stems: the pre-filter only drops them when
# prefilter_drop_unpaired = TRUE, and it may be skipped entirely, in which case
# the fallback to the unfiltered Stage 1 summary would otherwise carry every
# unpaired stem into the median. Scoring paired stems only makes the filter
# invariant to both toggles.
.paired_ids <- function(pairs, col) {
  if (is.null(pairs) || nrow(pairs) == 0L) return(character(0))
  unique(as.character(pairs[[col]])[!is.na(pairs[[col]])])
}
.keep_paired <- function(d, ids, label) {
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(d)
  if (length(ids) == 0L) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] No pair table available - scoring all %d stem(s).\n",
                label, nrow(d)))
    return(d)
  }
  keep <- d$TreeID %in% ids
  n_drop <- sum(!keep)
  if (n_drop > 0L)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] Excluded %d unpaired stem(s) from the MAD distribution (paired: %d).\n",
                label, n_drop, sum(keep)))
  d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}
stem_counts_1 <- .keep_paired(stem_counts_1, .paired_ids(.pairs_in, "TreeID_1"), "las_1")
stem_counts_2 <- .keep_paired(stem_counts_2, .paired_ids(.pairs_in, "TreeID_2"), "las_2")

# ── Score one epoch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MAD carries the 1.4826 constant, so z is on a sigma-like scale and the
# multiplier means the same thing as it does in the slice-level filters.
.stem_mad_score <- function(d, mult, min_n, label) {

  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)

  med  <- median(d$n_kept, na.rm = TRUE)
  madr <- mad(d$n_kept, center = med, na.rm = TRUE)

  d$med      <- med
  d$madr     <- madr
  d$z        <- NA_real_
  d$cutoff   <- NA_real_
  d$fail_mad <- FALSE

  if (nrow(d) < min_n) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] Only %d stem(s) - fewer than stem_mad_min_n (%d). No stem removed.\n",
                label, nrow(d), min_n))
    return(d)
  }

  # A zero MAD means over half the stems share one count. Scaling by it would
  # send every other stem to +/-Inf, so the test is skipped rather than allowed
  # to remove stems on a degenerate scale.
  if (is.na(madr) || madr < 1e-12) {
    cat(sprintf(paste0("[%s] MAD of the kept-count distribution is zero (median = %.0f).\n",
                       "      The test is skipped - counts are too uniform to score.\n"),
                label, med))
    return(d)
  }

  d$z        <- (d$n_kept - med) / madr
  d$cutoff   <- med - mult * madr          # counts strictly below this go
  d$fail_mad <- d$z < -mult                # ONE-SIDED: the high tail is kept
  d
}

# ── Pair propagation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Adds `fail_partner` (this stem passed, its partner did not) and `removed`.
# Kept separate from `fail_mad` so the plot and the report can distinguish a
# stem cut on its own count from one cut by association.
.propagate <- function(d1, d2, pairs, on) {

  .init <- function(d) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    d$fail_partner <- FALSE
    d$removed      <- d$fail_mad
    d
  }
  d1 <- .init(d1); d2 <- .init(d2)

  if (!on || is.null(pairs) || nrow(pairs) == 0L) return(list(d1 = d1, d2 = d2, pl = NULL))

  pl <- unique(data.frame(
    TreeID_1 = as.character(pairs$TreeID_1),
    TreeID_2 = as.character(pairs$TreeID_2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))

  # An ID absent from its epoch's score table was never scored, so it cannot
  # fail here – FALSE, not NA, keeps the OR below well defined.
  .fail <- function(d, ids) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(rep(FALSE, length(ids)))
    hit <- match(ids, d$TreeID)
    ifelse(is.na(hit), FALSE, d$fail_mad[hit])
  }

  pl$pair_fail <- .fail(d1, pl$TreeID_1) | .fail(d2, pl$TreeID_2)

  .mark <- function(d, own_ids) {
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    hit <- match(d$TreeID, own_ids)
    d$fail_partner <- !is.na(hit) & pl$pair_fail[hit] & !d$fail_mad
    d$removed      <- d$fail_mad | d$fail_partner
    d
  }

  list(d1 = .mark(d1, pl$TreeID_1), d2 = .mark(d2, pl$TreeID_2), pl = pl)
}

# ── Multiplier sweep ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# n_removed is the direct MAD hit; n_removed_prop adds the partners that go
# with them, which is the number that actually matters downstream.
.stem_mad_sweep <- function(d1, d2, grid, pairs, on) {

  .one <- function(d, label, k, extra) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || all(is.na(d$z))) return(NULL)
    med <- d$med[1]; madr <- d$madr[1]
    rm  <- d$z < -k & !is.na(d$z)
    data.frame(
      epoch           = label,
      mult            = k,
      cutoff_n        = round(med - k * madr, 1),
      n_stems         = nrow(d),
      n_removed       = sum(rm),
      n_removed_prop  = sum(rm | extra),
      pct_removed_prop = round(100 * mean(rm | extra), 1),
      max_kept_rm     = if (any(rm)) max(d$n_kept[rm]) else NA_integer_,
      min_kept_ok     = if (any(!rm)) min(d$n_kept[!rm]) else NA_integer_,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }

  do.call(rbind, lapply(grid, function(k) {
    tmp1 <- d1; tmp2 <- d2
    if (!is.null(tmp1)) tmp1$fail_mad <- !is.na(tmp1$z) & tmp1$z < -k
    if (!is.null(tmp2)) tmp2$fail_mad <- !is.na(tmp2$z) & tmp2$z < -k
    pr <- .propagate(tmp1, tmp2, pairs, on)
    rbind(
      .one(d1, "las_1", k, if (is.null(pr$d1)) FALSE else pr$d1$fail_partner),
      .one(d2, "las_2", k, if (is.null(pr$d2)) FALSE else pr$d2$fail_partner)
    )
  }))
}

# ── Plot one epoch ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Left axis  : MAD z-score of the stem's kept count.
# Right axis : the count itself. Because z = (n - med) / MAD is linear, the two
#              axes are exact rescalings of each other - one series, two
#              readings, same as the slice-level diagnostics.
# X axis     : stems in ascending count order, so the curve rises left to right
#              and the removal boundary is a single crossing rather than a
#              scatter. Direct MAD removals are the run at the far left.
# Marks      : x = cut on its own count | hollow = cut because its partner was.
#              Partner removals sit anywhere on the curve, including well above
#              the line, which is why they need their own mark.
.stem_mad_plot <- function(d, label, colour, mult) {

  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || all(is.na(d$z))) return(NULL)

  d <- d[order(d$n_kept, d$TreeID), ]
  d$TreeID <- factor(d$TreeID, levels = d$TreeID)
  med <- d$med[1]; madr <- d$madr[1]

  d$state <- ifelse(d$fail_mad, "mad",
              ifelse(d$fail_partner, "partner", "kept"))
  d$state <- factor(d$state, levels = c("kept", "mad", "partner"))

  z_lo <- min(c(d$z, -mult), na.rm = TRUE) - stem_mad_pad
  z_hi <- max(d$z, na.rm = TRUE) + stem_mad_pad

  ggplot(d, aes(TreeID, z, group = 1)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -stem_mad_ref_lines,
               linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -mult,
               linetype = "dotted", colour = .col_cut, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_line(colour = colour, alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = state, size = state, colour = state), stroke = 1.0) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(kept = 16, mad = 4, partner = 1), drop = FALSE,
                       guide = "none") +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(kept = 2.2, mad = 3.6, partner = 2.8), drop = FALSE,
                      guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(kept = colour, mad = .col_cut, partner = .col_par),
                        drop = FALSE, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name     = "MAD z-score of kept-ellipse count",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * madr + med, name = "Kept ellipses per stem")
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(z_lo, z_hi)) +
    labs(
      title    = sprintf("[%s] Stem kept-ellipse count \u2014 one-sided MAD filter", label),
      subtitle = sprintf("median %.0f kept | MAD %.2f | cutoff < %.1f kept | %d cut on count, %d on partner, of %d stem(s) at mult %.1f",
                         med, madr, med - mult * madr,
                         sum(d$fail_mad), sum(d$fail_partner), nrow(d), mult),
      x        = "Stem (TreeID), ordered by kept-ellipse count",
      caption  = sprintf("red dotted = chosen multiplier (-%.1f) | grey dotted = -%s | \u2715 = cut on count | hollow = cut with partner | high tail never cut",
                         mult, paste(stem_mad_ref_lines, collapse = ", -"))
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = stem_mad_label_rotate,
                                     vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

# ── Run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (run_stem_mad) {

  stem_mad_1 <- .stem_mad_score(stem_counts_1, stem_mad_mult, stem_mad_min_n, "las_1")
  stem_mad_2 <- .stem_mad_score(stem_counts_2, stem_mad_mult, stem_mad_min_n, "las_2")

  .prop      <- .propagate(stem_mad_1, stem_mad_2, .pairs_in, stem_mad_propagate_pairs)
  stem_mad_1 <- .prop$d1
  stem_mad_2 <- .prop$d2

  stem_mad_scores <- rbind(stem_mad_1, stem_mad_2)

  cat("\n\u2500\u2500 Stem-level MAD sweep on kept-ellipse count (one-sided, low tail only) \u2500\u2500\n")
  cat("z = (n_kept - median(n_kept)) / MAD  [MAD includes the 1.4826 constant]\n")
  cat("cutoff_n       = the kept count below which a stem is cut at that multiplier\n")
  cat("n_removed_prop = that count plus the partners removed alongside them\n\n")

  stem_mad_sweep <- .stem_mad_sweep(stem_mad_1, stem_mad_2, stem_mad_grid,
                                    .pairs_in, stem_mad_propagate_pairs)
  if (!is.null(stem_mad_sweep))
    print(stem_mad_sweep[order(stem_mad_sweep$epoch, stem_mad_sweep$mult), ],
          row.names = FALSE)

  # ── Surviving stem lists ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  .ids <- function(d, col) if (is.null(d)) character(0) else d$TreeID[d[[col]] %in% TRUE]

  stems_mad_removed_1 <- .ids(stem_mad_1, "removed")
  stems_mad_removed_2 <- .ids(stem_mad_2, "removed")
  stems_kept_1 <- setdiff(if (is.null(stem_counts_1)) character(0) else stem_counts_1$TreeID,
                          stems_mad_removed_1)
  stems_kept_2 <- setdiff(if (is.null(stem_counts_2)) character(0) else stem_counts_2$TreeID,
                          stems_mad_removed_2)

  .rm_line <- function(d, label) {
    if (is.null(d) || !any(d$removed)) {
      cat(sprintf("\n[%s] No stem removed.\n", label)); return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    sub <- d[d$removed, c("TreeID", "n_kept", "n_fitted", "z")]
    sub$reason <- ifelse(d$fail_mad[d$removed], "count", "partner")
    sub$z <- round(sub$z, 2)
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] %d stem(s) removed:\n", label, nrow(sub)))
    print(sub[order(sub$reason, sub$n_kept), ], row.names = FALSE)
  }

  .rm_line(stem_mad_1, "las_1")
  .rm_line(stem_mad_2, "las_2")

  # ── Pairs surviving both this stage and the pre-filter ──────────────────────
  if (!is.null(.pairs_in)) {
    .ok <- as.character(.pairs_in$TreeID_1) %in% stems_kept_1 &
           as.character(.pairs_in$TreeID_2) %in% stems_kept_2
    pairs_stem_mad <- .pairs_in[.ok, , drop = FALSE]
    cat(sprintf("\nTemporal pairs: %d -> %d (%d lost at this stage)\n",
                nrow(.pairs_in), nrow(pairs_stem_mad), sum(!.ok)))
  } else {
    pairs_stem_mad <- NULL
  }

  # ── Plots ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (stem_mad_plot) {
    p1 <- .stem_mad_plot(stem_mad_1, "las_1", .col_1, stem_mad_mult)
    p2 <- .stem_mad_plot(stem_mad_2, "las_2", .col_2, stem_mad_mult)
    if (!is.null(p1)) print(p1)
    if (!is.null(p2)) print(p2)
  }

} else {
  cat("\nStem-level MAD filter SKIPPED (run_stem_mad = FALSE).\n")
  stem_mad_scores <- NULL
  stems_mad_removed_1 <- stems_mad_removed_2 <- character(0)
  stems_kept_1 <- if (is.null(stem_counts_1)) character(0) else stem_counts_1$TreeID
  stems_kept_2 <- if (is.null(stem_counts_2)) character(0) else stem_counts_2$TreeID
  pairs_stem_mad <- .pairs_in
}

# ── Parameter record ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sp <- list(
  method          = "stem_level_mad_on_kept_ellipse_count_one_sided_low",
  mult            = stem_mad_mult,
  min_n           = stem_mad_min_n,
  per_epoch       = TRUE,
  propagate_pairs = stem_mad_propagate_pairs,
  scored_prefiltered_set = .have_pre,
  run             = run_stem_mad
)
```


### 2.1.3 Straightness gate: gold length, with a silver fallback

A stem is judged over a defined vertical window rather than over whatever
survived cleaning, so stems are compared on equal footing. Straightness means
a **consistent lean angle** – leaning is fine, the angle just has to hold up the
stem – so the gate must separate deviation that is *directionally consistent*
(a bend) from deviation that merely scatters (RANSAC centre error). Raw RMS
distance from a fitted line cannot tell those apart: a stem with noisy centres
and a stem with a real bend score the same.

The line is fitted as two independent regressions, `x ~ z` and `y ~ z`. Slice
heights are a design parameter rather than a measurement, so there is no error
in `z` and orthogonal regression or PCA would buy nothing. Theil–Sen by default:
a least-squares line is pulled *towards* surviving bad ellipses and so shrinks
the very deviation this gate depends on.

The window is cut into four sub-windows

Each scoring window is divided into `gold_n_blocks = 4` equal-height
sub-windows. Equal height, not equal count, so a sub-window is a physical
section of stem rather than a variable slab of whatever happened to survive
cleaning. One partition serves both tests below, which keeps the two scores
commensurable: they read the same four sections of the same stem.

**Every sub-window must carry at least `gold_min_n_block = 3` kept centres.**
A window that fails this is dropped unscored, and so fails the gate. This is a
coverage requirement rather than a sample-size one: equal-height blocks mean an
empty or near-empty block is a *vertical gap* in the reconstruction, and a stem
measured over four sections where one section is missing has not been measured
over four sections at all. Both scores would degrade quietly rather than
loudly – the bend angle would compare three directions while claiming four, and
the bias correction would rest on a median of one or two points, whose variance
is several times that of a median of five. Requiring the coverage up front is
cheaper than trying to model the damage. This rule is also the *only* count
floor on a window: it implies `gold_n_blocks × gold_min_n_block` centres, and a
separate window-wide minimum would either sit below that and never bind or
above it and overrule it, so there is no second parameter to keep in step.

**`bend_deg` – direction change from base to top (reported, not gated).** Note
this is a *bend*, not a lean: it is the angle *between* local axis directions,
so the tilt they share cancels out of every comparison and a stem leaning 25°
all the way up scores zero.

A sub-window direction is itself an estimate, so two noise-only directions
disagree by a non-zero angle and `bend_deg` has a floor of its own. That floor
is estimated per stem and removed, giving `bend_adj_deg`, which is what the gate
reads. The floor is dominated by the sub-window **lever arm** rather than its
count – per block the slope variance is $s^2 / S_{zz}$ – so halving the rung
length roughly doubles it, and three short sub-windows are worse than three long
ones. It is simulated from fixed draws rather than derived, because `bend_deg`
shares block errors with the simulated floor draws and has no tidy closed form.
`bend_f` is the raw-to-floor ratio for reading the two apart.

Theil–Sen is run inside each sub-window, giving four local axis directions
$u_b = (b_x, b_y, 1)/\lVert\cdot\rVert$, and the score is the angle between the
**bottom** sub-window's direction and the **top** sub-window's – end to end,
not the largest angle among all pairs of the four. This is deliberate: it
measures a single physical quantity, how far the stem has turned between its
ends, so it does not inflate just because more sub-windows are used, and it
needs no reference axis, which removes a correlation between the score and the
window-wide fit that a widest-departure form would otherwise have to model.
Noise averages down inside each sub-window fit, since Theil–Sen slope error
falls as $1/\sqrt{k}$, while a real end-to-end bend appears at full strength.
The cost is shape-blindness: a symmetric S-bend returns to its starting
direction and scores near zero here. That trade is acceptable only because
`bend_deg`/`bend_adj_deg` is reported rather than gated on – `curv_cm` below
still sees an S-bend, as deviation between the four block medians, so the vote
as a whole does not miss it.

**`curv_cm` – between/within block decomposition (the gate).** Residuals
from the *window-wide* line are reduced to one median vector per sub-window.
The RMS of those four block medians is the structured deviation; the scatter
around them is noise. Block medians of $k$ points still carry residual noise,
so the between term is bias-corrected before the square root:

$$\widehat{\text{curv}}^2 = \overline{\lVert m_b \rVert^2} - 2\hat\sigma^2\,\overline{c_{k_b}}$$

where $c_k$ is the normal-theory variance of a median of $k$ points relative to
$\sigma^2$ ($c_1 = 1$, $c_2 = 0.50$, $c_3 = 0.45$, …, $c_k \to \pi/2k$) and
$\hat\sigma$ is a pooled MAD of the within-block residuals. `curv_f` is the
ratio of the raw between term to its null expectation, so it sits near 1 on a
straight noisy stem and climbs with real structure. This assumes nothing about
the *shape* of the bend, so it catches S-bends and localised crooks that a
parabola misses. `noise_cm` is reported alongside: it is the RANSAC centre
precision floor for that stem, measured on that stem, and it is the number to
read before concluding a threshold is too tight.

**`kappa`, `R_curv` – quadratic curvature (reported, not gated).** A quadratic
$x = a + bz + cz^2$ is fitted per axis by ordinary least squares on the window's
centres, giving a radius of curvature. Least squares rather than Theil–Sen
because Theil–Sen does not extend cleanly to a quadratic term, and by this point
in the pipeline both cleaning passes have run, so the worst centres are gone.
The lean correction matters here, since stems may lean substantially:

$$\kappa = \frac{2\sqrt{c_x^2 + c_y^2 + (b_x c_y - b_y c_x)^2}}{(1 + b_x^2 + b_y^2)^{3/2}},
\qquad R = 1/\kappa$$

This column exists because a radius of curvature in metres is the quantity a
reader expects; it is not part of the verdict, and a stem that fails on
`bend_deg` while showing a large `R_curv` is a stem whose bend is not parabolic
rather than a contradiction.

`rms_cm` is still computed and reported, so the gate's behaviour can be compared
against the previous criterion, but it no longer decides anything. Section 2.3
continues to weight on it.

The **gold length** is a single fixed window, `gold_length = 8` m – the
longest window most stems support, so it is the strongest claim available and
the bend noise floor is smallest there. Pairs split two ways within it:

- **Group A** – both stems span at least the gold length. Each is measured over
  the bottom gold length only. This rests on the program's standing assumption
  that a ULS cloud may not contain the whole stem, so the lower section is the
  part reliably present; if it is straight, the stem is treated as straight.
- **Group B** – either stem falls short. Each is measured over its full kept
  range **capped at the gold length**, against a threshold scaled to that
  range. The cap matters when only one side of a pair falls short: the other
  side may well have plenty of kept range beyond the gold length, and letting
  its window run past the gold length would score curvature the gate was
  never meant to look at, using a threshold that goes flat past that same
  point.

Because `gold_length` no longer descends to chase a count, it is possible for
too few stems to reach it, or for too few of the ones that do to pass the vote
– a forest of short or genuinely crooked trees is a real outcome, not a tuning
failure. When the number of straight units at 8 m falls below
`gold_crit_straight`, the gate does not fail the run: it assumes either that
there are very few genuinely straight stems, or that the forest is largely
short trees the 8 m window can't reach, and falls back to a **silver-length**
pass – the same estimators, evaluated over the shorter `silver_length`
(`= prefilter_min_span`) window on whichever stems reach it, with `3` sub-blocks
instead of `4` since the shorter window has less room to partition. The silver
scores are used **only downstream, as weighting inputs** – they never filter a
pair. When `gold_crit_straight` is met, the silver pass does not run at all and
every pair is filtered on the gold-length vote as before.

**Every stem is also SCORED, pass or fail.** The vote returns a verdict, and a
verdict cannot rank: two stems that both fail 2-of-3 are not equally bent, and
when clean pairs are scarce the useful question stops being *which stems pass*
and becomes *which stems are least bad*. So alongside the vote, each stem gets a
continuous `straight_score` – the geometric mean of `curv_cm`, `sag_cm` and
`bend_adj_deg` each divided by **its own threshold**, mapped to $(0, 1]$ with
higher meaning straighter. Ratios rather than raw values, because the three are
in different units and cannot otherwise be combined, and because the thresholds
already carry each stem's measured noise floor *and* the group-B $L^p$ length
scaling – so stem length is inside the denominator, and a short window cannot
look straight merely by having had less stem to bend over. A mild
$(\text{win\_len}/\text{gold})^{0.5}$ factor then breaks ties in favour of the
stem that demonstrated it over more of itself. A pair's score is the **lower** of
its two stems, for the same reason the gate requires both sides to pass.

That ranking is what Step 2.4 uses to top up the Z-translation pair set when the
gate leaves too few – see there for why the rotation solve is deliberately *not*
topped up the same way.

The line is refitted **inside each window**. Whether the bottom 8 m is straight
is a different question from whether the whole stem is, and the answer must not
carry geometry from above the window.

Group-B thresholds scale as $t(L) = t_{\text{gold}} \cdot (L/\text{gold})^{p}$,
with a different exponent per score because the two grow differently with
window length at constant curvature. Lateral deviation from a fitted line grows
as $L^2$, so `curv_cm` uses $p = 2$ as `rms_cm` did. Total direction change
grows as $L$ – for a circular arc it is exactly $\kappa L$ – so `bend_deg` uses
$p = 1$. Both hold curvature – not raw deviation –
constant across window lengths. Group-B windows are shorter than gold by
construction, so their thresholds come out tighter.

```{r}
#| label: params-gold-length-straightness
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Fit a line per window and gate pairs on straightness at a single gold length, with a silver-length weighting-only fallback"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A SINGLE fixed window. A descending ladder previously chased a straight-unit
# count by re-running at shorter lengths; that bought stems only by measuring
# less of them, and is gone. 8 m is the longest window most stems support, so
# it is the strongest claim available - and the bend noise floor is smallest
# there. If too few stems clear that bar, the fallback below (silver_length)
# produces weighting-only scores instead of retrying the gate at a shorter
# length.
gold_length        <- 8           # the one gold window, metres
gold_crit_straight <- 3L          # below this many straight units at gold_length,
                                  # assume a short/crooked forest and fall back
                                  # to the silver-length weighting-only pass
gold_count_basis   <- "pairs"     # "pairs" = pairs with BOTH sides straight
                                  # "stems" = straight stems, groups A and B pooled
groupB_window      <- "full"      # "full" or "pair_min" - both capped at gold length
gold_plot          <- TRUE

# ── Silver fallback parameters (weighting only, never filtering) ──────────────
silver_length      <- prefilter_min_span  # shorter window used only when the
                                  # gold-length gate is critically short
silver_n_blocks    <- 3L          # fewer sub-windows than gold - less room to
                                  # partition inside a shorter length
silver_min_n_block <- 3L
silver_min_stems   <- 10L         # if fewer stems reach silver_length, the
                                  # stem pre-filter is re-run at half its span

# ── The gate is a VOTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Three scores, each a different estimator of the same claim, each with its own
# noise floor removed:
#   curv_cm   - deviation of the four sub-window median centres from the
#               window-wide line. Robust (medians), undirected, needs the
#               partition.
#   sag_cm    - kappa L^2 / 8 from the quadratic through every centre. Uses all
#               the data and no partition, but OLS, so one wild centre moves it.
#   bend_adj  - angle between the base and top sub-window directions. Reads
#               direction rather than position, so it is sensitive to a kink
#               that leaves the ends aligned in neither position nor slope.
# They fail differently, which is the point of voting: a stem is kept when
# gate_min_votes of them agree it is straight, so no single flaky estimator
# decides alone. Set gate_min_votes to 3 for AND, 1 for OR.
gate_tests         <- c("curv", "sag", "bend")
gate_min_votes     <- 2L          # of length(gate_tests)

# ── Continuous straightness score (ALWAYS computed, gate or no gate) ────────
# The vote is a verdict; it cannot rank. Two stems that both fail 2-of-3 are not
# equally bent, and when there are too few clean pairs to work with, the useful
# question stops being "which stems pass" and becomes "which stems are the least
# bad". So every stem also gets a continuous score, on every run, whether or not
# it passes the vote.
#
# Each test is expressed as a RATIO to that stem's own threshold:
#     r_curv = curv_cm / thresh_curv,  r_sag = sag_cm / thresh_sag,
#     r_bend = bend_adj_deg / thresh_bend
# Ratios rather than raw values because the three are in different units (cm, cm,
# degrees) and cannot otherwise be combined, and because the thresholds already
# carry the two corrections that matter: each stem's OWN measured noise floor,
# and - for group B - the measured L^p scaling. Stem length is therefore already
# inside the denominator, which is what keeps a 4 m window from looking straighter
# than an 8 m one purely by having had less stem to bend over. r = 1 is exactly at
# threshold, so the three are commensurable by construction.
#
# They are combined as a GEOMETRIC mean, matching how 2.3 combines its two shape
# estimators: a stem is penalised when the tests AGREE it is bent, rather than
# whenever the harshest one says so, and no single test can dominate the product
# the way it would dominate a sum.
score_unscorable_r <- 3.0         # ratio assigned to a test that could not be
                                  # scored. Matches the vote's treatment of an
                                  # unscorable test as a vote AGAINST: a window
                                  # too sparse to decompose does not get to be
                                  # ranked as though it were clean. 3.0 is three
                                  # times its own threshold - decisively bad, but
                                  # finite, so a stem with two good tests and one
                                  # missing still outranks one that is bent on all
                                  # three.

# Length still earns a bonus BEYOND the threshold scaling. Two stems can post the
# same ratio over 4 m and 8 m windows, but the 8 m stem has demonstrated it over
# twice the stem, and it is the one whose axis vector the later stages can trust.
# The exponent is deliberately mild - this breaks ties, it does not reorder the
# shape verdict. 0 disables it.
score_len_exp      <- 0.5

# ── How many pairs the Stage 3 Z-translation wants ────────────────────────
# The rotation solve and the Z-translation have different appetites. The rotation
# is a 3-parameter fit over unit vectors and is well determined by a handful of
# genuinely straight pairs, so it stays on the gate survivors and nothing else.
# The Z-translation is a per-pair feature match averaged across pairs, so its
# precision falls off directly with the pair count - and a slightly bent stem
# still carries perfectly matchable bumps and hollows up its length.
#
# So when the gate leaves fewer than this many pairs, the Z-translation set is
# TOPPED UP from the best-ranked pairs that did not pass, while the rotation set
# is left exactly as the gate decided it. See Step 2.4.
ztrans_target_pairs <- 10L

# NOTE on shape. An arc fitted with a straight line has residuals that cross
# that line TWICE - out, through, back - so leaving the line and returning is
# what a real curve looks like, not evidence against one. The gate is
# therefore undirected again. curv_dir_cm (the quadratic component of the
# block pattern) and sbend_cm (the cubic component, a true reversal of
# curvature) are still computed and reported, but neither decides anything: an
# S over 8 m of stem is rare enough that failing it as "curved" is the right
# error to make.

# Sub-windows: one equal-height partition drives both tests
gold_n_blocks      <- 4L          # sub-windows per scoring window
gold_min_n_block   <- 3L          # centres EVERY sub-window must carry, or the
                                  # window is dropped unscored and fails the gate

# Noise floors. Two of the three scores have a floor that has to be estimated
# by simulation rather than derived; both use fixed draws so the result is
# deterministic.
gold_floor_sims    <- 200L        # draws used to estimate the bend noise floor

# Theil-Sen slope efficiency against least squares. NOT a parameter any more:
# 3/pi = 0.955 is the ASYMPTOTIC value, and sub-windows here carry three to
# twenty-odd centres, where the small-sample efficiency is a different number.
# The bend floor is directly proportional to it, so quoting the asymptote
# misstates the floor on exactly the smallest blocks - which are the ones whose
# floors dominate. It is measured below, per block size, the same way .g_cmed
# tabulates the small-k variance of a median instead of trusting pi/(2k).
gold_ts_eff_sims   <- 1000L       # draws per block size
gold_ts_eff_kmax   <- 24L         # sizes tabulated; above this, the asymptote

# Bend behaviour checks. bend_adj_deg now carries a vote; bend_trust is a
# separate diagnostic that says whether that vote is being cast on geometry.
# A bend at roughly constant curvature must (a) grow in proportion to window
# length and (b) agree with the quadratic fit's own kappa. bend_trust records
# whether each stem manages both. It is reported, never applied.
bend_ref_long   <- 8.0            # long reference window, metres
bend_ref_short  <- 4.0            # short reference window

# The expected ratio is DERIVED, not chosen. A bend at constant curvature turns
# in proportion to the length it is measured over, so bend_long / bend_short
# must come out at bend_ref_long / bend_ref_short - 2.0 for these references -
# and hard-coding a band risks it drifting out of step with the windows above,
# which is exactly what happened once already. Only the WIDTH is a judgement,
# and it is multiplicative so the band sits symmetrically around the
# expectation in log terms.
#
# The width is not derived because it cannot honestly be: a tolerance built
# from the simulated bend floors comes out near 1.1, which the observed spread
# of this ratio exceeds on nearly every stem. That would be a check that fails
# everything and tells you nothing.
bend_scale_tol  <- 1.5            # band is the expected ratio times/divided by this
bend_scale_expected <- bend_ref_long / bend_ref_short
bend_scale_min  <- bend_scale_expected / bend_scale_tol
bend_scale_max  <- bend_scale_expected * bend_scale_tol
bend_pred_tol   <- 2.0            # max bend_deg / (kappa * lever) before distrust

# Threshold sweep and worst-window report
curv_sweep       <- TRUE          # print straight counts across a grid of curv thresholds
curv_sweep_n     <- 12L           # grid points, spanning the observed distribution
worst_report_n   <- 8L            # windows listed in the worst-deviation report
# Every threshold is ADAPTIVE, and all three take the same shape:
#     clamp(mult * that stem's own floor, absolute floor, absolute ceiling)
# A stem can never demonstrate less deviation than its own centres can resolve,
# so a single absolute number either lets noisy stems through on a low
# floor-subtracted score or rejects clean ones for structure they genuinely
# have. The multiple tracks each stem's measured precision; the floor stops a
# very quiet stem being held to an unreachable standard, and the ceiling stops
# a very noisy one buying an arbitrarily loose pass.
#
# SETTING THE THREE. There are two defensible ways to choose them, and they do
# not give the same numbers.
#
#   (a) One physical claim, three units. Over an 8 m window a 2 degree turn is
#       kappa ~ 0.006 /m, a radius near 170 m, a sag near 4.7 cm, and - at the
#       observed sag/curv ratio of about 1.5 - some 3.1 cm of block deviation.
#       Coherent, and the version to use if the threshold has to mean one
#       stated thing about stem shape.
#   (b) Comparable strictness, so the VOTE does the work. This is what is set
#       below. Under (a) the bend test passes under a tenth of the stems while
#       curv and sag pass a third or more, so bend never joins a majority and
#       2-of-3 quietly collapses into curv AND sag - stricter than a single
#       test, and decided by two estimators rather than three. A vote only
#       means anything when its members reject comparable shares and are
#       therefore free to disagree; a test that almost nobody passes is not a
#       voter, it is a constant.
#
# So each threshold sits near the median of its own group-A distribution
# (curv 3.63, sag 5.53, bend_adj 4.13 on the 8 m run). The cost is that the
# absolute claim is looser than 2 degrees - about 4 degrees of turn, a radius
# near 85 m. Read the sweep before accepting that: it scales all three
# together, so the row at mult 0.5 is roughly the (a) setting above.
curv_thresh_cm     <- 3.5         # absolute floor on the per-stem threshold
curv_noise_mult    <- 1.2         # threshold as a multiple of that stem's noise_cm
curv_thresh_max    <- 5.5         # absolute ceiling on the per-stem threshold

sag_thresh_cm      <- 5.5         # near the group-A median, as curv is
sag_noise_mult     <- 4.0         # multiple of that stem's sag_floor_cm
sag_thresh_max     <- 8.0

# Compared against bend_adj_deg, which already has its floor removed. The
# multiple of bend_floor_deg is what keeps a stem with short, sparse
# sub-windows - whose direction estimates are genuinely poor - from being
# judged on an angle it cannot resolve.
# 4.0 is bend's own group-A median. At the physically equivalent 2.0 it passes
# fewer than a tenth of stems and stops being a voter - see (b) above.
bend_thresh_deg    <- 4.0         # absolute floor on the per-stem threshold
bend_noise_mult    <- 3.0         # multiple of that stem's bend_floor_deg
bend_thresh_max    <- 6.0
# The group-B exponent is MEASURED from the data further down, not assumed.
# The assumed value was 2.0 (deviation ~ L^2, a constant-curvature arc); the
# stems do not behave that way, so a fixed exponent here would mis-scale every
# short window. gold_scale_exp is set from gold_exp_curv once it is known.
curv_exp_fallback  <- 1.0         # used only if too few stems span both references

# Line fitting
gold_fit_method <- "theilsen"     # "theilsen" (robust) or "ols"
gold_ts_max_n   <- 120L           # above this, Theil-Sen samples pairs
gold_ts_pairs   <- 20000L         # pairs sampled when above the cap
gold_seed       <- 42L

# ── Reporting helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Every distribution printed by this chunk goes through one path. The old
# cat() + print(round(quantile(...))) pairs laid the same information out four
# different ways and re-wrapped depending on how wide the numbers happened to
# be, which made two runs hard to read against each other.
.qq    <- c(0, .1, .25, .5, .75, .9, 1)
.qlab  <- c("min", "p10", "p25", "med", "p75", "p90", "max")

.par_apply("params-gold-length-straightness")
```

```{r}
#| label: gold-length-straightness
#| code-summary: "Fit a line per window and gate pairs on straightness at a single gold length, with a silver-length weighting-only fallback"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

.qhead <- function(indent = "  ")
  cat(indent, sprintf("%-12s", ""), paste(sprintf("%9s", .qlab), collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "")
.pq <- function(lab, x, d = 3, indent = "  ") {
  q <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::quantile(x, .qq, na.rm = TRUE)),
                error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, length(.qq)))
  cell <- ifelse(is.na(q), "-", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), q))
  cat(indent, sprintf("%-12s", lab), paste(sprintf("%9s", cell), collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "")
}
.kv <- function(k, fmt, ...) cat(sprintf(paste0("  %-9s", fmt, "\n"), k, ...))

# ── Source: kept centres of the stems alive after 2.1.2 ───────────────────────
# The ledger always comes from Stage 1; what changes is which stems are allowed
# through. `stems_kept_*` are the MAD survivors, which already carry the
# pre-filter's effect because 2.1.1 fed 2.1.2. Nothing here recomputes a verdict.
.s1 <- if (exists("slice_fates_1_pre")) slice_fates_1_pre else
       if (exists("slice_fates_1"))     slice_fates_1     else NULL
.s2 <- if (exists("slice_fates_2_pre")) slice_fates_2_pre else
       if (exists("slice_fates_2"))     slice_fates_2     else NULL
if (is.null(.s1) && is.null(.s2))
  stop("slice_fates_1/2 not found - they travel in the Stage 1 checkpoint.")

.k1 <- if (exists("stems_kept_1"))     stems_kept_1     else
       if (exists("stems_pre_kept_1")) stems_pre_kept_1 else NULL
.k2 <- if (exists("stems_kept_2"))     stems_kept_2     else
       if (exists("stems_pre_kept_2")) stems_pre_kept_2 else NULL

.gold_stage <- if (exists("stems_kept_1") || exists("stems_kept_2"))
                 "post-MAD survivors (2.1.2)" else
               if (exists("stems_pre_kept_1") || exists("stems_pre_kept_2"))
                 "pre-filter survivors (2.1.1)" else
                 "FULL Stage 1 set (no stem filter has run)"

.sub <- function(d, ids) if (is.null(d)) NULL else
          if (is.null(ids)) d else
            d[as.character(d$TreeID) %in% as.character(ids), , drop = FALSE]
.s1 <- .sub(.s1, .k1); .s2 <- .sub(.s2, .k2)

g_src <- if (is.null(.s1)) .s2 else if (is.null(.s2)) .s1 else {
  kp <- intersect(names(.s1), names(.s2))
  rbind(.s1[, kp, drop = FALSE], .s2[, kp, drop = FALSE])
}
g_src <- g_src[g_src$status == "kept" &
               !is.na(g_src$center_x) & !is.na(g_src$center_y) &
               !is.na(g_src$slice_z), , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(g_src) == 0L) stop("No kept centres survive the stem filters.")
g_src$stem_key <- paste(g_src$epoch, g_src$TreeID, sep = "|")

.pairs_g <- if (exists("pairs_stem_mad")  && !is.null(pairs_stem_mad))  pairs_stem_mad  else
            if (exists("pairs_prefilter") && !is.null(pairs_prefilter)) pairs_prefilter else
            if (exists("pairs_stage1")) pairs_stage1 else NULL
if (is.null(.pairs_g) || nrow(.pairs_g) == 0L) stop("No pair table found.")

# Split once - the per-stem frames do not change between rungs, only the
# windows drawn on them do.
g_by_stem <- split(g_src, g_src$stem_key)

g_spans <- do.call(rbind, lapply(g_by_stem, function(d) {
  data.frame(epoch = d$epoch[1], TreeID = d$TreeID[1], stem_key = d$stem_key[1],
             z_lo = min(d$slice_z), z_hi = max(d$slice_z),
             span = diff(range(d$slice_z)), n_kept = nrow(d),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
rownames(g_spans) <- NULL

.pair_ids <- data.frame(TreeID_1 = as.character(.pairs_g$TreeID_1),
                        TreeID_2 = as.character(.pairs_g$TreeID_2),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
.span_of <- function(ids, ep)
  g_spans$span[match(paste(ep, ids, sep = "|"), g_spans$stem_key)]
.s1_all <- .span_of(.pair_ids$TreeID_1, "las_1")
.s2_all <- .span_of(.pair_ids$TreeID_2, "las_2")

# ── Line fitting ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Theil-Sen: median of all pairwise slopes, then the median intercept. Roughly
# 29% breakdown, against 0% for least squares - which matters because this gate
# exists to find stems whose centres are unreliable, and a fit dragged towards
# those centres would hide them.
set.seed(gold_seed)

.ts_slope <- function(z, v) {
  n <- length(z)
  if (n <= gold_ts_max_n) {
    ij <- utils::combn(n, 2L); i <- ij[1, ]; j <- ij[2, ]
  } else {
    i <- sample.int(n, gold_ts_pairs, replace = TRUE)
    j <- sample.int(n, gold_ts_pairs, replace = TRUE)
    ok <- i != j; i <- i[ok]; j <- j[ok]
  }
  dz <- z[j] - z[i]
  ok <- abs(dz) > 1e-9
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  median((v[j][ok] - v[i][ok]) / dz[ok])
}

.g_fit <- function(z, v) {
  if (gold_fit_method == "ols") {
    b <- cov(z, v) / var(z)
    return(c(median(v - b * z), b))
  }
  b <- .ts_slope(z, v)
  if (is.na(b)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  c(median(v - b * z), b)
}

# ── Sub-window partition ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Equal HEIGHT, cut on the requested window bounds rather than on the data
# range, so the four sections are the same physical thickness whether or not
# cleaning left a gap. Blocks may therefore come out unequal in count, which is
# handled explicitly in the bias correction below.
.g_blocks <- function(z, z_lo, z_hi, m)
  findInterval(z, seq(z_lo, z_hi, length.out = m + 1L),
               rightmost.closed = TRUE, all.inside = TRUE)

# Normal-theory variance of a sample median of k points, relative to sigma^2.
# Tabulated for small k because the asymptotic pi/(2k) is badly wrong there
# (k = 4: 0.298 against 0.393) and overcorrecting the between term would eat
# real curvature. Above the table, pi/(2k) is close enough.
.g_cmed <- c(1.000, 0.500, 0.449, 0.298, 0.287, 0.215, 0.210, 0.168)
.g_ck <- function(k) ifelse(k <= length(.g_cmed), .g_cmed[pmin(k, length(.g_cmed))],
                            pi / (2 * k))

# Theil-Sen slope efficiency against OLS, measured at each block size on
# equally spaced z. Efficiency is var_OLS / var_TS for the same noise, so the
# bend floor uses s2 / (Szz * eff): a low efficiency at small k widens the
# floor, which is the correction the asymptotic 3/pi was silently skipping.
# Spacing inside a block is near enough regular after two cleaning passes, and
# the ratio is in any case insensitive to it. Seeded, so this is deterministic.
.g_ts_eff_tab <- local({
  set.seed(gold_seed + 1L)
  vapply(2:gold_ts_eff_kmax, function(k) {
    zz  <- seq_len(k)
    Szz <- sum((zz - mean(zz))^2)
    ij  <- utils::combn(k, 2L)              # enumerated once, not per draw
    dz  <- zz[ij[2, ]] - zz[ij[1, ]]
    bb  <- vapply(seq_len(gold_ts_eff_sims), function(i) {
             y <- rnorm(k); median((y[ij[2, ]] - y[ij[1, ]]) / dz)
           }, numeric(1))
    bb  <- bb[is.finite(bb)]
    if (length(bb) < 30L) return(3 / pi)
    (1 / Szz) / stats::var(bb)          # both variances for unit noise
  }, numeric(1))
})
.g_eff <- function(k) ifelse(k > gold_ts_eff_kmax, 3 / pi,
                             .g_ts_eff_tab[pmin(pmax(k, 2L), gold_ts_eff_kmax) - 1L])
cat(sprintf("Theil-Sen efficiency measured on %d draws: k=3 %.3f | k=6 %.3f | k=12 %.3f | k=%d %.3f (asymptote %.3f)\n",
            gold_ts_eff_sims, .g_eff(3L), .g_eff(6L), .g_eff(12L),
            gold_ts_eff_kmax, .g_eff(gold_ts_eff_kmax), 3 / pi))

# Refit INSIDE the window. A line fitted over the full stem and evaluated on a
# sub-range would carry curvature from outside the window into the score.
.g_na <- data.frame(rms_cm = NA_real_, curv_cm = NA_real_,
                    curv_dir_cm = NA_real_, sbend_cm = NA_real_,
                    sag_cm = NA_real_, sag_raw_cm = NA_real_,
                    sag_floor_cm = NA_real_, noise_cm = NA_real_,
                    curv_f = NA_real_, bend_deg = NA_real_,
                    bend_floor_deg = NA_real_, bend_adj_deg = NA_real_,
                    bend_f = NA_real_, bend_pred_deg = NA_real_,
                    bend_pred_f = NA_real_, bend_span_m = NA_real_,
                    kappa = NA_real_,
                    R_curv = NA_real_, n_win = 0L, n_blk = 0L,
                    blk_min = NA_integer_, win_len = NA_real_)

# Fixed standard-normal draws, generated ONCE. The bend floor is estimated by
# simulation, and drawing fresh numbers inside .g_score would make each stem's
# floor depend on how many stems were scored before it. Reusing one deterministic
# block of draws keeps the ladder reproducible and costs nothing.
.g_z1 <- matrix(rnorm(gold_floor_sims * gold_n_blocks), nrow = gold_floor_sims)
.g_z2 <- matrix(rnorm(gold_floor_sims * gold_n_blocks), nrow = gold_floor_sims)

# Angle between two axis directions, in radians, vectorised over rows. Shared
# by the observed bend and the simulated floor, so the two are the same
# statistic.
#
# bend is now END TO END: the direction of the BOTTOM sub-window against the
# direction of the TOP one. Two gains over the previous widest-departure form.
# It is a single physical quantity - how far the stem has turned between its
# ends - rather than an extreme over sub-windows, so it does not inflate with
# block count; and it needs no reference axis, which removes the correlation
# between the score and the window-wide fit that the floor previously had to
# model. The cost is that a symmetric S-bend returns to its starting direction
# and scores near zero. Acceptable while bend is reported rather than gated,
# and curv_cm still sees an S-bend, as between-block deviation.
.g_ang <- function(sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2) {
  U <- cbind(sx1, sy1, 1); U <- U / sqrt(rowSums(U^2))
  V <- cbind(sx2, sy2, 1); V <- V / sqrt(rowSums(V^2))
  acos(pmin(1, pmax(-1, rowSums(U * V))))
}

.g_score <- function(d, z_lo, z_hi, n_blocks = gold_n_blocks, min_n_block = gold_min_n_block) {
  w <- d[d$slice_z >= z_lo - 1e-9 & d$slice_z <= z_hi + 1e-9, , drop = FALSE]
  n <- nrow(w)
  out <- .g_na; out$n_win <- n
  # The only window-wide count floor is the one the sub-window rule implies:
  # n_blocks x min_n_block. A separate parameter would either sit
  # below it and never bind, or above it and reject windows the coverage rule
  # would have accepted - two controls for one decision either way.
  if (n < n_blocks * min_n_block) return(out)
  z <- w$slice_z
  if (diff(range(z)) < 1e-6) return(out)
  out$win_len <- diff(range(z))

  # ---- window-wide robust line, and its residuals -------------------------
  fx <- .g_fit(z, w$center_x); fy <- .g_fit(z, w$center_y)
  if (any(is.na(c(fx, fy)))) return(out)
  ex <- w$center_x - (fx[1] + fx[2] * z)
  ey <- w$center_y - (fy[1] + fy[2] * z)
  out$rms_cm <- sqrt(mean(ex^2 + ey^2)) * 100

  b   <- .g_blocks(z, z_lo, z_hi, n_blocks)
  kb  <- tabulate(b, nbins = n_blocks)
  out$n_blk   <- sum(kb > 0L)
  out$blk_min <- min(kb)

  # Coverage gate. Every sub-window carries min_n_block centres or the
  # window is not scored at all: a sparse block is a vertical gap, and both
  # scores below would degrade silently rather than visibly. rms_cm is already
  # set above, so the stem still appears in the diagnostics with a reason.
  if (min(kb) < min_n_block) return(out)
  use <- seq_len(n_blocks)

  # ---- the shared noise estimate ------------------------------------------
  # Pooled MAD of the residuals after removing each block's median, inflated
  # for the dof spent on those medians (one per block per component). BOTH
  # scores are corrected against this same s2, so neither carries a floor the
  # other has removed.
  mx <- tapply(ex, factor(b, levels = use), median)
  my <- tapply(ey, factor(b, levels = use), median)
  rr <- c(ex - mx[as.character(b)], ey - my[as.character(b)])
  dof <- 2 * n - 2 * length(use)
  s2  <- if (dof > 0L) stats::mad(rr, center = 0)^2 * (2 * n) / dof else NA_real_

  # ---- between / within decomposition -------------------------------------
  # The between-block signal is the sequence of per-block median residual
  # vectors, bottom to top. The question is which PART of that sequence counts
  # as curvature.
  #
  # curv_cm is its RMS, bias-corrected for the noise those medians still
  # carry: how far this stem's sections sit from its own line, whatever shape
  # that departure takes. Undirected on purpose - see the note in the
  # parameters. A curve crosses its own fitted line, so "leaves and returns"
  # is the signature of the thing being measured, not a reason to discount it.
  #
  # The same sequence is ALSO decomposed onto orthogonal shapes in z, purely
  # to report what kind of departure it is. With the window-wide line already
  # removed, the constant and linear shapes are gone and what is left splits
  # into:
  #   mode 2 (quadratic)  - a single arc, curvature of one sign across the
  #                         window. Reported as curv_dir_cm.
  #   mode 3 (cubic)      - curvature that CHANGES SIGN: a genuine S, not
  #                         merely a residual that crosses zero. Reported as
  #                         sbend_cm.
  #   modes 4+            - shorter-wavelength wander, in curv_cm but in
  #                         neither mode.
  # Contrasts are built on the block z-CENTROIDS, not on block index, so
  # uneven blocks are placed where they actually sit.
  if (!is.na(s2)) {
    out$noise_cm <- sqrt(2 * s2) * 100

    B  <- mean(mx^2 + my^2)
    E0 <- 2 * s2 * mean(.g_ck(kb[use]))
    out$curv_cm <- sqrt(max(0, B - E0)) * 100
    out$curv_f  <- if (E0 > 0) B / E0 else NA_real_

    zb  <- vapply(use, function(bb) mean(z[b == bb]), numeric(1))
    m   <- length(use)
    deg <- min(3L, m - 1L)
    Pz  <- if (deg >= 2L)
             tryCatch(stats::poly(zb, degree = deg), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL

    # Amplitude of one shape, and the amplitude noise alone would produce.
    # u is scaled to mean(u^2) = 1, so a pattern of the form A*u has RMS |A|
    # over the blocks - the same scale the old statistic was on. The floor is
    # the u-weighted version of E0, so a shape leaning on a sparse block is
    # charged for that block's larger median error.
    .amp <- function(u) {
      Ax <- sum(u * mx) / m; Ay <- sum(u * my) / m
      Ev <- 2 * s2 * sum(u^2 * .g_ck(kb[use])) / m^2
      c(Ax^2 + Ay^2, Ev)
    }
    if (!is.null(Pz)) {
      a2 <- .amp(as.vector(Pz[, 2]) * sqrt(m))          # quadratic: one arc
      out$curv_dir_cm <- sqrt(max(0, a2[1] - a2[2])) * 100
      if (deg >= 3L) {
        a3 <- .amp(as.vector(Pz[, 3]) * sqrt(m))        # cubic: the reversal
        out$sbend_cm <- sqrt(max(0, a3[1] - a3[2])) * 100
      }
    }
    # Fewer than three usable blocks leaves no quadratic contrast, so the
    # mode split is simply absent; curv_cm itself is unaffected.
  }

  # ---- bend: direction change from the bottom sub-window to the top -------
  # Theil-Sen per block on the RAW centres, not the residuals: each block gets
  # its own local axis direction. The score is the angle between the LOWEST
  # and the HIGHEST scorable sub-window - the net turn across the window, read
  # at its two ends. Intermediate blocks do not enter the score; they still
  # drive curv_cm, which is where a stem that wanders and comes back shows up.
  dirs <- lapply(use, function(bb) {
    p <- which(b == bb)
    if (length(p) < min_n_block) return(NULL)
    zz <- z[p]
    if (diff(range(zz)) < 1e-6) return(NULL)
    sx <- .ts_slope(zz, w$center_x[p]); sy <- .ts_slope(zz, w$center_y[p])
    if (is.na(sx) || is.na(sy)) return(NULL)
    c(sx, sy)          # raw slopes - .g_ang does the normalising
  })
  ok_b <- !vapply(dirs, is.null, logical(1))
  if (sum(ok_b) >= 2L) {
    bset <- use[ok_b]                  # ascending in z, so block 1 is the base
    ends <- c(1L, length(bset))        # lowest and highest SCORABLE sub-window
    S <- do.call(rbind, dirs[ok_b])[ends, , drop = FALSE]
    out$bend_deg <- .g_ang(S[1, 1], S[1, 2], S[2, 1], S[2, 2]) * 180 / pi

    # The lever arm the turn is measured over: the gap between the two end
    # blocks' centres of mass, not the full window. Shorter than win_len by
    # roughly (m-1)/m, and it is the length the quadratic prediction below has
    # to use if the two are to be compared on equal terms.
    zbar <- vapply(bset[ends], function(bb) mean(z[b == bb]), numeric(1))
    out$bend_span_m <- diff(zbar)

    # ---- the bend noise floor ---------------------------------------------
    # A sub-window direction is itself estimated, so two noise-only directions
    # disagree by a non-zero angle and bend_deg has a floor exactly as curv_cm
    # does. The floor is dominated by the LEVER ARM, not the count: per block
    # and per component the Theil-Sen slope variance is s2 / (Szz * eff), with
    # Szz the within-block spread of z, so short sub-windows are expensive.
    #
    # Only the two end blocks contribute now, and their errors are independent
    # - there is no shared reference direction any more - so the Szz-weighted
    # correlation correction the widest-departure form needed has gone with it.
    # Still simulated rather than derived, because the lean-corrected angle
    # between two perturbed directions has no tidy closed form. The draws are
    # fixed, so this is deterministic.
    if (!is.na(s2)) {
      Szz <- vapply(bset[ends], function(bb) { zz <- z[b == bb]; sum((zz - mean(zz))^2) },
                    numeric(1))
      # Efficiency at THIS block's count, not one number for all of them.
      v_b <- sqrt(s2 / (Szz * .g_eff(kb[bset[ends]])))   # slope sd, per component

      # First-order lean correction. A given slope error turns into a smaller
      # ANGLE error on a stem that already leans, because d(theta)/d(slope) =
      # 1 / (1 + |slope|^2). Ignoring it would overstate the floor on the
      # steepest stems, which are the ones the gate is meant to keep.
      glean <- 1 / (1 + fx[2]^2 + fy[2]^2)

      E1 <- sweep(.g_z1[, 1:2, drop = FALSE], 2, v_b, `*`)   # x-slope error
      E2 <- sweep(.g_z2[, 1:2, drop = FALSE], 2, v_b, `*`)   # y-slope error
      sim <- .g_ang(E1[, 1], E2[, 1], E1[, 2], E2[, 2])      # base against top
      fl <- median(sim) * glean * 180 / pi
      out$bend_floor_deg <- fl

      # Subtracted in quadrature, matching how curv_cm removes its own floor.
      # Approximate - angles are not variances - but it is the same convention
      # applied consistently, and bend_f gives the raw ratio for anyone who
      # would rather read the two apart.
      out$bend_adj_deg <- sqrt(max(0, out$bend_deg^2 - fl^2))
      out$bend_f       <- if (fl > 0) out$bend_deg / fl else NA_real_
    }
  }

  # ---- quadratic curvature, and the sag it implies -------------------------
  # OLS, not Theil-Sen: Theil-Sen has no clean quadratic extension, and both
  # cleaning passes have already run. z is centred so the linear coefficient is
  # the slope at mid-window, which is the point the curvature is quoted at.
  if (n >= 4L) {
    zc <- z - mean(z)
    X  <- cbind(1, zc, zc^2)
    q  <- tryCatch(qr.solve(X, cbind(w$center_x, w$center_y)),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(q)) {
      bx <- q[2, 1]; cx <- q[3, 1]; by <- q[2, 2]; cy <- q[3, 2]
      kap <- 2 * sqrt(cx^2 + cy^2 + (bx * cy - by * cx)^2) /
             (1 + bx^2 + by^2)^1.5
      out$kappa  <- kap
      out$R_curv <- if (kap > 1e-9) 1 / kap else Inf

      # ---- sag: the same curvature read as a length -----------------------
      # The parabola's greatest departure from its own chord over a window of
      # length L is |c| L^2 / 8 per component, so the 2-D sag is that with the
      # two quadratic coefficients combined. This is the direct answer to "how
      # bent is this stem": one number, in centimetres, from every centre in
      # the window rather than from four block medians.
      #
      # It has a noise floor like everything else here - a quadratic fitted
      # through noise picks up a spurious c - and that floor IS derivable,
      # unlike the bend one: var(c) = sigma^2 [(X'X)^-1]_33 per component.
      # Corrected against the SAME s2 the block scores use, so the two are on
      # one noise model and can be read against each other.
      out$sag_raw_cm <- sqrt(cx^2 + cy^2) * out$win_len^2 / 8 * 100
      v33 <- tryCatch(solve(crossprod(X))[3, 3], error = function(e) NA_real_)
      if (!is.na(s2) && !is.na(v33)) {
        out$sag_floor_cm <- sqrt(2 * s2 * v33) * out$win_len^2 / 8 * 100
        out$sag_cm <- sqrt(max(0, cx^2 + cy^2 - 2 * s2 * v33)) *
                      out$win_len^2 / 8 * 100
      }

      # What bend_deg SHOULD be if the window really holds a smooth bend of
      # this curvature: direction change is kappa times the arc it is measured
      # over. That arc is bend_span_m - the gap between the two end blocks'
      # centres of mass - not the full window, because an end-to-end bend never
      # sees the stub of stem outside those blocks. The two are independent
      # estimates of the same geometry - one from sub-window slopes, one from a
      # quadratic through all the centres - so their ratio says whether
      # bend_deg is reading a bend or reading noise.
      .lev <- if (is.na(out$bend_span_m)) out$win_len else out$bend_span_m
      out$bend_pred_deg <- kap * .lev * 180 / pi
      if (!is.na(out$bend_deg) && out$bend_pred_deg > 1e-9)
        out$bend_pred_f <- out$bend_deg / out$bend_pred_deg
    }
  }

  out
}

# ── Do the scores scale with window length? ───────────────────────────────────
# Scored ONCE per stem, on fixed reference windows rather than on the rung, so
# the answer does not move as the ladder descends. A bend at constant curvature
# gives bend_long / bend_short = bend_ref_long / bend_ref_short; correlated
# centre error, which does not accumulate along the stem, gives a ratio near 1.
# This is the one check that needs no noise model - it is a scaling law, and
# either the statistic obeys it or it does not. curv_cm is measured on the same
# two references, because the group-B thresholds assume exponents (1 for an
# angle, 2 for a length) that have never been checked against the data.
.scale_chk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(g_by_stem), function(k) {
  d  <- g_by_stem[[k]]
  z0 <- min(d$slice_z)
  na <- data.frame(stem_key = k, bend_long = NA_real_, bend_short = NA_real_,
                   bend_ratio = NA_real_, curv_long = NA_real_,
                   curv_short = NA_real_, curv_ratio = NA_real_,
                   sag_long = NA_real_, sag_short = NA_real_,
                   sag_ratio = NA_real_,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (diff(range(d$slice_z)) < bend_ref_long - 1e-9) return(na)
  sl <- .g_score(d, z0, z0 + bend_ref_long)
  ss <- .g_score(d, z0, z0 + bend_ref_short)
  .rat <- function(a, b) if (!is.na(a) && !is.na(b) && b > 1e-9) a / b else NA_real_
  data.frame(stem_key = k,
             bend_long = sl$bend_deg, bend_short = ss$bend_deg,
             bend_ratio = .rat(sl$bend_deg, ss$bend_deg),
             curv_long = sl$curv_cm,  curv_short = ss$curv_cm,
             curv_ratio = .rat(sl$curv_cm, ss$curv_cm),
             sag_long = sl$sag_cm, sag_short = ss$sag_cm,
             sag_ratio = .rat(sl$sag_cm, ss$sag_cm),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
rownames(.scale_chk) <- NULL

# Exponent measured per stem, then medianed - not a ratio of medians, which
# would let a different subset of stems drive each end. p = log(ratio) / log(L
# ratio), so p = 1 is proportional growth and p = 0.5 is a random walk.
.Lr <- bend_ref_long / bend_ref_short
.exp_of <- function(r) {
  r <- r[!is.na(r) & r > 0]
  if (!length(r)) return(NA_real_)
  median(log(r) / log(.Lr))
}
gold_exp_bend <- .exp_of(.scale_chk$bend_ratio)
gold_exp_curv <- .exp_of(.scale_chk$curv_ratio)
gold_exp_sag  <- .exp_of(.scale_chk$sag_ratio)
# Each test carries its OWN group-B scaling now, measured on its own ratios.
# They are not the same number - an angle and two lengths have no reason to
# grow with window length at the same rate - and using one exponent for all
# three would mis-scale two of them on every short window.
.exp_or <- function(e) if (is.na(e)) curv_exp_fallback else e

cat(sprintf("\n\u2500\u2500 Scale check: %.1f m against %.1f m \u2500\u2500\n",
            bend_ref_long, bend_ref_short))
cat(sprintf("  %d of %d stem(s) long enough to score both references\n",
            sum(!is.na(.scale_chk$bend_ratio)), nrow(.scale_chk)))
if (any(!is.na(.scale_chk$bend_ratio))) {
  .qhead()
  .pq("bend_ratio", .scale_chk$bend_ratio)
  .pq("curv_ratio", .scale_chk$curv_ratio)
  .pq("sag_ratio",  .scale_chk$sag_ratio)
  cat(sprintf("  measured exponent: bend %.2f | curv %.2f | sag %.2f\n",
              gold_exp_bend, gold_exp_curv, gold_exp_sag))
  cat("  scale: 0 = does not accumulate | 0.5 = random walk | 1 = grows with length | 2 = with length squared\n")
  # An exponent near 1 for curv means deviation grows LINEARLY with window
  # length, so curvature falls with scale and the stems are not arcs. A bend
  # exponent near 0 means direction change does not accumulate at all, which
  # is why bend_deg is reported rather than gated on.
}

# The group-B threshold scaling now uses the MEASURED exponent. Deriving it
# rather than asserting it is the whole point: an assumed 2.0 tightened short
# windows by a factor the data does not support.
gold_scale_exp <- .exp_or(gold_exp_curv)     # curv's own, kept for the plots
cat(sprintf("  group-B thresholds will scale as L^%.2f (curv) | L^%.2f (sag) | L^%.2f (bend)\n",
            gold_scale_exp, .exp_or(gold_exp_sag), .exp_or(gold_exp_bend)))
if (anyNA(c(gold_exp_curv, gold_exp_sag, gold_exp_bend)))
  cat("  (a fallback of 1.00 stands in wherever too few stems span both references)\n")

# ── One full evaluation at a given window length ───────────────────────────────
# Everything downstream of the window length is recomputed here, because the
# length changes group membership, the group-A window AND the group-B
# threshold scale. n_blocks/min_n_block default to the gold-length values but
# are overridden for the silver-length fallback pass below (3 blocks instead
# of 4, since a shorter window has less room to partition).
.gold_eval <- function(L, n_blocks = gold_n_blocks, min_n_block = gold_min_n_block) {

  gp <- .pair_ids
  gp$span_1 <- .s1_all
  gp$span_2 <- .s2_all
  gp$usable <- !is.na(gp$span_1) & !is.na(gp$span_2)
  gp$group  <- ifelse(!gp$usable, NA_character_,
                ifelse(gp$span_1 >= L & gp$span_2 >= L, "A", "B"))

  .side <- function(tid, ep, grp, partner_span) {
    d <- g_by_stem[[paste(ep, tid, sep = "|")]]
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L)
      return(cbind(.g_na, z_lo = NA_real_, z_hi = NA_real_))
    z_lo <- min(d$slice_z)
    own  <- diff(range(d$slice_z))
    win  <- if (identical(grp, "A")) L else
            if (identical(groupB_window, "pair_min")) min(own, partner_span, L, na.rm = TRUE)
            else min(own, L)
    cbind(.g_score(d, z_lo, z_lo + win, n_blocks = n_blocks, min_n_block = min_n_block),
          z_lo = z_lo, z_hi = z_lo + win)
  }

  idx <- which(gp$usable)
  stems <- if (length(idx) == 0L) NULL else do.call(rbind, lapply(idx, function(i) {
    a <- .side(gp$TreeID_1[i], "las_1", gp$group[i], gp$span_2[i])
    b <- .side(gp$TreeID_2[i], "las_2", gp$group[i], gp$span_1[i])
    rbind(
      cbind(pair_row = i, epoch = "las_1", TreeID = gp$TreeID_1[i],
            group = gp$group[i], span = gp$span_1[i], a, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      cbind(pair_row = i, epoch = "las_2", TreeID = gp$TreeID_2[i],
            group = gp$group[i], span = gp$span_2[i], b, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    )
  }))
  if (is.null(stems)) return(NULL)
  rownames(stems) <- NULL

  # One threshold shape, applied three times. Per-stem base from that stem's
  # OWN measured floor, clamped, then the group-B length scaling on top with
  # that test's own measured exponent. A stem with no floor estimate falls
  # back to the absolute floor rather than to something derived from other
  # stems. Group A sits at the flat top of every curve by construction.
  .thresh <- function(noise, mult, lo, hi, expn) {
    base <- pmin(hi, pmax(lo, ifelse(is.na(noise), lo, mult * noise)))
    ifelse(stems$group == "A", base, base * (stems$win_len / L)^expn)
  }
  stems$curv_base   <- pmin(curv_thresh_max,
                       pmax(curv_thresh_cm,
                            ifelse(is.na(stems$noise_cm), curv_thresh_cm,
                                   curv_noise_mult * stems$noise_cm)))
  stems$thresh_curv <- .thresh(stems$noise_cm, curv_noise_mult,
                               curv_thresh_cm, curv_thresh_max, .exp_or(gold_exp_curv))
  stems$thresh_sag  <- .thresh(stems$sag_floor_cm, sag_noise_mult,
                               sag_thresh_cm, sag_thresh_max, .exp_or(gold_exp_sag))
  stems$thresh_bend <- .thresh(stems$bend_floor_deg, bend_noise_mult,
                               bend_thresh_deg, bend_thresh_max, .exp_or(gold_exp_bend))
  # ---- is this stem's bend readable as geometry? --------------------------
  # Reported, not applied. Two checks, both must pass for bend_trust. Kept so
  # the negative result can be stated per stem rather than only in aggregate.
  stems$bend_ratio <- .scale_chk$bend_ratio[
    match(paste(stems$epoch, stems$TreeID, sep = "|"), .scale_chk$stem_key)]
  .scale_ok <- !is.na(stems$bend_ratio) &
               stems$bend_ratio >= bend_scale_min & stems$bend_ratio <= bend_scale_max
  .pred_ok  <- !is.na(stems$bend_pred_f) & stems$bend_pred_f <= bend_pred_tol
  # An unscorable check counts as untrusted: a stem too short for the long
  # reference has not demonstrated that its bend scales, so it does not get
  # the benefit of the tight threshold.
  stems$bend_trust <- .scale_ok & .pred_ok

  # ---- the vote -----------------------------------------------------------
  # A score that could not be computed is a vote AGAINST, not an abstention. A
  # window too sparse to be decomposed is exactly the case this gate exists to
  # remove, and letting it abstain would hand it a pass on the other two.
  stems$ok_curv <- !is.na(stems$curv_cm)    & stems$curv_cm    <= stems$thresh_curv
  stems$ok_sag  <- !is.na(stems$sag_cm)     & stems$sag_cm     <= stems$thresh_sag
  stems$ok_bend <- !is.na(stems$bend_adj_deg) & stems$bend_adj_deg <= stems$thresh_bend

  .votes <- cbind(curv = stems$ok_curv, sag = stems$ok_sag, bend = stems$ok_bend)
  .votes <- .votes[, gate_tests, drop = FALSE]
  stems$votes    <- rowSums(.votes)
  stems$straight <- stems$votes >= gate_min_votes

  # score_cm keeps the plots and the sweep on one axis: the curvature score,
  # which is the one with a measured rather than derived noise floor.
  stems$score_cm <- stems$curv_cm

  # ---- the continuous straightness score ----------------------------------
  # Computed for EVERY stem, pass or fail. See the parameter block for why the
  # three tests enter as ratios to their own thresholds and are combined
  # geometrically.
  .ratio <- function(val, thr) {
    r <- val / thr
    r[!is.finite(r)] <- score_unscorable_r
    pmax(r, 0)
  }
  stems$r_curv <- .ratio(stems$curv_cm,      stems$thresh_curv)
  stems$r_sag  <- .ratio(stems$sag_cm,       stems$thresh_sag)
  stems$r_bend <- .ratio(stems$bend_adj_deg, stems$thresh_bend)

  # Only the tests actually in gate_tests contribute, so the score and the vote
  # always read the same evidence.
  .R <- cbind(curv = stems$r_curv, sag = stems$r_sag, bend = stems$r_bend)[, gate_tests, drop = FALSE]
  # Geometric mean. A floor of 1e-6 keeps log() finite for a perfectly straight
  # stem without changing any ordering at any realistic scale.
  stems$shape_ratio <- exp(rowMeans(log(pmax(.R, 1e-6))))

  # Length bonus: the window this was demonstrated over, relative to the gold
  # length. Group A is exactly 1 by construction; group B is < 1.
  stems$len_factor <- (pmin(1, stems$win_len / L))^score_len_exp
  stems$len_factor[!is.finite(stems$len_factor)] <- 0

  # Map to (0, 1], higher = straighter, so the number reads the same way round
  # as every other weight in this pipeline. shape_ratio = 0 -> 1 (perfect),
  # = 1 (exactly at threshold) -> 0.5, = 3 -> 0.25.
  stems$straight_score <- stems$len_factor / (1 + stems$shape_ratio)
  stems$straight_score[!is.finite(stems$straight_score)] <- 0

  .sparse <- !is.na(stems$blk_min) & stems$blk_min < min_n_block
  # Which tests voted against, so a failure can be read rather than guessed.
  .why <- apply(!.votes, 1L, function(r) paste(gate_tests[r], collapse = "+"))
  stems$fail_why <- ifelse(stems$straight, "",
                    ifelse(.sparse, "sparse_sub-window", .why))

  ok <- tapply(stems$straight, stems$pair_row, all)
  gp$straight <- FALSE
  gp$straight[as.integer(names(ok))] <- ok

  # A pair is only as straight as its WORSE stem - the same logic that makes the
  # gate require both sides to pass. Using the mean would let one excellent stem
  # carry a badly bent partner into the top of the ranking, and a temporal match
  # is a two-sided object: the shift it implies is only as good as the weaker
```
