```{r}
#| label: diag-gold-kept-stems
#| code-summary: "Gold-window bend/curvature/noise, ellipse count, and group-B window lengths for kept stems"

if (!exists("gold_stems") || !exists("gold_pairs"))
  stop("Run the gold-length-straightness chunk first.")

# Pair-level survival, not stem-level: a straight stem whose partner failed is
# not kept, so filtering on gold_stems$straight alone would overcount.
gk <- gold_stems[gold_stems$pair_row %in% which(gold_pairs$straight), , drop = FALSE]

if (nrow(gk) == 0L) {
  cat("No stems survive the gold-length gate.\n")
} else {

  if (gold_gate_active) {
    cat(sprintf("\n── Kept stems after the gold gate (gold length %.2f m) ──\n", gold_length))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("\n── Silver-length scores (%.2f m), WEIGHTING ONLY - every usable pair passed through, none filtered ──\n",
                silver_length))
  }
  cat(sprintf("%d stem(s) across %d surviving pair(s)\n\n",
              nrow(gk), sum(gold_pairs$straight)))

  tab <- gk[order(gk$group, gk$bend_adj_deg),
            c("epoch", "TreeID", "group", "span", "win_len", "n_win", "blk_min",
              "bend_adj_deg", "bend_deg", "bend_floor_deg", "bend_f",
              "bend_ratio", "bend_pred_f", "bend_trust",
              "curv_cm", "noise_cm", "curv_f", "R_curv", "rms_cm")]
  tab$span     <- round(tab$span, 2)
  tab$win_len  <- round(tab$win_len, 2)
  tab$bend_adj_deg   <- round(tab$bend_adj_deg, 3)
  tab$bend_deg       <- round(tab$bend_deg, 3)
  tab$bend_floor_deg <- round(tab$bend_floor_deg, 3)
  tab$bend_f         <- round(tab$bend_f, 2)
  tab$bend_ratio     <- round(tab$bend_ratio, 2)
  tab$bend_pred_f    <- round(tab$bend_pred_f, 2)
  tab$curv_cm  <- round(tab$curv_cm, 3)
  tab$noise_cm <- round(tab$noise_cm, 3)
  tab$curv_f   <- round(tab$curv_f, 2)
  tab$R_curv   <- round(tab$R_curv, 1)
  tab$rms_cm   <- round(tab$rms_cm, 3)
  print(tab, row.names = FALSE)

  .summ <- function(d, lab) {
    if (nrow(d) == 0L) { cat(sprintf("\n[%s] none kept.\n", lab)); return(invisible(NULL)) }
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] %d stem(s)\n", lab, nrow(d)))
    .qq <- c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1)
    cat("  bend_adj "); print(round(quantile(d$bend_adj_deg,   .qq, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
    cat("  bend_fl  "); print(round(quantile(d$bend_floor_deg, .qq, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
    cat("  curv_cm  "); print(round(quantile(d$curv_cm,  .qq, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
    cat("  noise_cm "); print(round(quantile(d$noise_cm, .qq, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
    cat("  R_curv   "); print(round(quantile(d$R_curv,   .qq, na.rm = TRUE), 1))
    cat("  rms_cm   "); print(round(quantile(d$rms_cm,   .qq, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
    cat("  n_win    "); print(round(quantile(d$n_win,    .qq), 1))
    cat("  blk_min  "); print(round(quantile(d$blk_min,  .qq), 1))
    cat(sprintf("  ellipses in window: %d total | mean %.1f per stem\n",
                sum(d$n_win), mean(d$n_win)))
  }

  .summ(gk[gk$group == "A", ], "group A")
  .summ(gk[gk$group == "B", ], "group B")

  # Group B windows vary per stem; group A windows are all exactly gold_length,
  # so only B needs its lengths reported.
  gb <- gk[gk$group == "B", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(gb) > 0L) {
    cat(sprintf("\n[group B] window lengths (m), %d stem(s):\n", nrow(gb)))
    print(round(quantile(gb$win_len, c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1)), 2))
    cat(sprintf("  mean %.2f m | as a fraction of gold: %.2f - %.2f\n",
                mean(gb$win_len), min(gb$win_len) / gold_length,
                max(gb$win_len) / gold_length))
    print(gb[order(gb$win_len), c("epoch", "TreeID", "win_len", "n_win", "blk_min",
                                  "bend_adj_deg", "curv_cm", "thresh_curv")],
          row.names = FALSE)
  }

  cat(sprintf("\nTotal kept ellipses inside gold windows: %d\n", sum(gk$n_win)))
}
```


## 2.2 Fit Stem Axis Vectors by Regression

Axes are fitted the same way straightness was measured in 2.1.3 – `x ~ z` and
`y ~ z` by Theil–Sen – rather than by PCA. Three reasons this matters here:

**Direction is determined, not arbitrary.** A PCA eigenvector has no inherent
sign; `prcomp` returns whichever the LAPACK routine produced, so half the stems
came back pointing down and had to be flipped by convention. A regression axis
is `(b_x, b_y, 1)` normalised – the `z` component is 1 before normalising, so
`vz > 0` always, by construction.

**The error model is right.** PCA assumes isotropic error across x, y and z.
Slice heights are a design parameter with no error, and PCA is not scale
invariant, so with `z` spanning metres and `x`/`y` centimetres the first
eigenvector is pinned near vertical by the variance ratio rather than by the
geometry.

**Robustness.** Theil–Sen tolerates roughly 29% contaminated centres; PCA is
least squares, so one bad centre with a long lever arm rotates the whole axis.

The window is the **bottom 4 m** of each stem's kept centres, not the gold
length – a refit, not a reuse of 2.1.3's line, since the gold length varies with
the ladder and the axis should not move when the ladder does.

```{r}
#| label: params-fit-axis-vectors-regression
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Stem axis vectors by Theil-Sen regression over the bottom 4 m; vz > 0 by construction"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
axis_window_m  <- 4.0        # bottom section used for the axis fit
axis_min_n     <- 6L         # kept centres required inside the window
axis_method    <- "theilsen" # "theilsen" or "ols"
axis_ts_max_n  <- 120L
axis_ts_pairs  <- 20000L
axis_seed      <- 42L

.par_apply("params-fit-axis-vectors-regression")
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-axis-vectors-regression
#| code-summary: "Stem axis vectors by Theil-Sen regression over the bottom 4 m; vz > 0 by construction"

# ── Pair set: survivors of the gold gate ──────────────────────────────────────
pairs_axis <- if (exists("pairs_gold") && !is.null(pairs_gold)) pairs_gold else
              if (exists("pairs_stem_mad") && !is.null(pairs_stem_mad)) pairs_stem_mad else
              pairs_stage1
if (is.null(pairs_axis) || nrow(pairs_axis) == 0L)
  stop("No surviving pairs - check the gold-length gate.")

cat(sprintf("Fitting axes for %d pair(s) over the bottom %.1f m.\n",
            nrow(pairs_axis), axis_window_m))

# ── Kept centres ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# g_src is left by 2.1.3: kept-status ledger rows for the stems still in play.
if (exists("g_src") && !is.null(g_src) && nrow(g_src) > 0L) {
  ax_src <- g_src
} else {
  .a1 <- if (exists("slice_fates_1_pre")) slice_fates_1_pre else slice_fates_1
  .a2 <- if (exists("slice_fates_2_pre")) slice_fates_2_pre else slice_fates_2
  kp <- intersect(names(.a1), names(.a2))
  ax_src <- rbind(.a1[, kp, drop = FALSE], .a2[, kp, drop = FALSE])
  ax_src <- ax_src[ax_src$status == "kept", , drop = FALSE]
  ax_src$stem_key <- paste(ax_src$epoch, ax_src$TreeID, sep = "|")
}
ax_by_stem <- split(ax_src, ax_src$stem_key)

# ── Fitter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(axis_seed)

.ax_ts <- function(z, v) {
  n <- length(z)
  if (n <= axis_ts_max_n) {
    ij <- utils::combn(n, 2L); i <- ij[1, ]; j <- ij[2, ]
  } else {
    i <- sample.int(n, axis_ts_pairs, replace = TRUE)
    j <- sample.int(n, axis_ts_pairs, replace = TRUE)
    ok <- i != j; i <- i[ok]; j <- j[ok]
  }
  dz <- z[j] - z[i]
  ok <- abs(dz) > 1e-9
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  median((v[j][ok] - v[i][ok]) / dz[ok])
}

.ax_slope <- function(z, v) {
  if (axis_method == "ols") return(cov(z, v) / var(z))
  .ax_ts(z, v)
}

# Returns a unit vector with vz > 0. No sign convention is applied or needed:
# the direction vector of x = a + b*z is (b_x, b_y, 1), whose z component is
# positive before normalising, so the axis points up by construction.
.fit_axis_reg <- function(tid, epoch) {

  d <- ax_by_stem[[paste(epoch, tid, sep = "|")]]
  na <- data.frame(vx = NA_real_, vy = NA_real_, vz = NA_real_,
                   n_win = 0L, win_len = NA_real_, rms_cm = NA_real_,
                   avg_semi_axis_m = NA_real_, bend_deg = NA_real_)
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(na)

  z_lo <- min(d$slice_z)
  w <- d[d$slice_z <= z_lo + axis_window_m + 1e-9, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(w) < axis_min_n) return(na)
  z <- w$slice_z
  if (diff(range(z)) < 1e-6) return(na)

  bx <- .ax_slope(z, w$center_x)
  by <- .ax_slope(z, w$center_y)
  if (is.na(bx) || is.na(by)) return(na)

  ax <- median(w$center_x - bx * z)
  ay <- median(w$center_y - by * z)
  ex <- w$center_x - (ax + bx * z)
  ey <- w$center_y - (ay + by * z)

  v <- c(bx, by, 1)
  v <- v / sqrt(sum(v^2))

  # Mean semi-axis inside the same window - the IRLS thickness weight reads
  # this rather than pair_summary, so the semi-axis and the axis describe
  # exactly the same slices. Per slice, average the semi-major and semi-minor
  # axis together (rather than taking the smaller of the two), then average
  # that across every kept ellipse in the window (window is up to 4 m; shorter
  # if fewer slices survived). Left in meters - no cm conversion.
  avg_semi_axis <- if (all(c("semi_a", "semi_b") %in% names(w)))
           mean((w$semi_a + w$semi_b) / 2, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_

  data.frame(vx = v[1], vy = v[2], vz = v[3],
             n_win = nrow(w), win_len = diff(range(z)),
             rms_cm = sqrt(mean(ex^2 + ey^2)) * 100,
             avg_semi_axis_m = avg_semi_axis,
             bend_deg = atan(sqrt(bx^2 + by^2)) * 180 / pi)
}

vecs_xy_1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_1), function(t)
  cbind(TreeID = t, .fit_axis_reg(t, "las_1"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
vecs_xy_2 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_2), function(t)
  cbind(TreeID = t, .fit_axis_reg(t, "las_2"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
rownames(vecs_xy_1) <- rownames(vecs_xy_2) <- NULL

# 2.3 joins on TreeID, and pairs_stage1 may carry integer IDs. Matching the
# type here avoids a join that silently produces all-NA vectors.
if (is.numeric(pairs_axis$TreeID_1)) vecs_xy_1$TreeID <- as.integer(vecs_xy_1$TreeID)
if (is.numeric(pairs_axis$TreeID_2)) vecs_xy_2$TreeID <- as.integer(vecs_xy_2$TreeID)

cat(sprintf("Valid stem vectors - las_1: %d of %d | las_2: %d of %d\n",
            sum(!is.na(vecs_xy_1$vx)), nrow(vecs_xy_1),
            sum(!is.na(vecs_xy_2$vx)), nrow(vecs_xy_2)))
cat(sprintf("All vz > 0: %s\n",
            all(c(vecs_xy_1$vz, vecs_xy_2$vz) > 0, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Lean (deg) - las_1 median %.2f | las_2 median %.2f\n",
            median(vecs_xy_1$bend_deg, na.rm = TRUE),
            median(vecs_xy_2$bend_deg, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Axis-window rms (cm) - median %.2f | max %.2f\n",
            median(c(vecs_xy_1$rms_cm, vecs_xy_2$rms_cm), na.rm = TRUE),
            max(c(vecs_xy_1$rms_cm, vecs_xy_2$rms_cm), na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Axis-window avg semi-axis (m) - median %.4f | range %.4f - %.4f\n",
            median(c(vecs_xy_1$avg_semi_axis_m, vecs_xy_2$avg_semi_axis_m), na.rm = TRUE),
            min(c(vecs_xy_1$avg_semi_axis_m, vecs_xy_2$avg_semi_axis_m), na.rm = TRUE),
            max(c(vecs_xy_1$avg_semi_axis_m, vecs_xy_2$avg_semi_axis_m), na.rm = TRUE)))

axis_thin <- c(vecs_xy_1$TreeID[is.na(vecs_xy_1$vx)],
               vecs_xy_2$TreeID[is.na(vecs_xy_2$vx)])
if (length(axis_thin) > 0L)
  cat(sprintf("Stems with fewer than %d centres in the bottom %.1f m (NA vector): %s\n",
              axis_min_n, axis_window_m, paste(axis_thin, collapse = ", ")))

# ── Ellipse frames for the visualisation chunks ───────────────────────────────
# These were previously built by a subset chunk that no longer exists, leaving
# the vis chunks referring to undefined objects. Rebuilt here from the pass-2
# survivors (post-refit geometry) and restricted to the surviving pairs.
ellipses_zt_1_valid <- ellipses_zt_1_valid2_all[as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_1)]
ellipses_zt_2_valid <- ellipses_zt_2_valid2_all[as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_2)]
ellipses_zt_1 <- ellipses_zt_1_all[as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_1)]
ellipses_zt_2 <- ellipses_zt_2_all[as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_2)]

overlap_ellipses <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_axis)), function(i) {
    t1 <- as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_1[i]); t2 <- as.character(pairs_axis$TreeID_2[i])
    c1 <- ellipses_zt_1_valid[[t1]]; c2 <- ellipses_zt_2_valid[[t2]]
    if (!is.null(c1) && nrow(c1) > 0) c1$abs_z <- c1$slice_z
    if (!is.null(c2) && nrow(c2) > 0) c2$abs_z <- c2$slice_z
    list(TreeID_1 = t1, TreeID_2 = t2,
         c1 = if (is.null(c1)) data.frame() else c1,
         c2 = if (is.null(c2)) data.frame() else c2)
  }),
  as.character(seq_len(nrow(pairs_axis)))
)

ax <- list(window_m = axis_window_m, min_n = axis_min_n,
           method = axis_method, n_pairs = nrow(pairs_axis))
```



### Vis - 3D stem points with regression axis vectors

This figure needs raw stem points, which Stage 2 does not load. It therefore
carries its own loader – toggle `vis_load_clouds` off if the clouds are already
in memory.

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-3d-stem-with-vectors
#| code-summary: "Parameters - fig-3d-stem-with-vectors"


# ── Point clouds for this figure ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# This stage does not load point clouds at the top, so this figure loads its own.
#   vis_load_clouds <- TRUE   read las_1 / las_2 from the paths below; the loader
#                             reapplies the Stage 1A alignment to las_1 so it
#                             matches the ellipse / vector geometry
#   vis_load_clouds <- FALSE  reuse the clouds already in memory (no disk read)
vis_load_clouds <- TRUE

# Source files. INHERITED by default, exactly as in Stage 3's params-stage3:
# this figure draws the clouds this stage's geometry was measured from, and
# typing a path here a second time is how they come apart. Under the driver this
# chunk is skipped outright, so what this guards is the by-hand run with figures
# on - where the old unconditional assignment would silently repoint las_1_path
# and las_2_path, which are in this stage's save manifest, at a hardcoded
# collection for every chunk that followed.
#
#   "inherit"  whatever Stage 1 measured (checkpoint, or session end to end)
#   "custom"   the two paths below - for a relocated or re-exported file
s2fig_paths <- "inherit"

s2fig_las_1_path_custom <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/Neighbor_Collection/1_i_b_BOS_2020_Schoen/Focal_1_with_neighbors_5m.las"
s2fig_las_2_path_custom <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/Neighbor_Collection/1_ii_2024_5m_Schoen/Focal_191_with_neighbors_5m.las"

if (identical(s2fig_paths, "custom")) {
  las_1_path <- s2fig_las_1_path_custom
  las_2_path <- s2fig_las_2_path_custom
} else if (!exists("las_1_path") || !exists("las_2_path")) {
  stop("[Stage 2 fig] s2fig_paths = \"inherit\", but no las path came from the ",
       "checkpoint or the session. Run the load chunk above first, or set ",
       "s2fig_paths <- \"custom\".")
}

.par_apply("params-fig-3d-stem-with-vectors")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-3d-stem-with-vectors
#| fig-cap: "3D stem points for all matched pairs with PCA stem axis vectors."

if (vis_load_clouds) {
  .miss <- c(las_1_path, las_2_path)[!file.exists(c(las_1_path, las_2_path))]
  if (length(.miss))
    stop("Point cloud not found:\n  ", paste(.miss, collapse = "\n  "))
}

# One call, one signature. .vis_point_clouds() is defined identically in Stages
# 2, 3, 4 and 5 (Step 0.2 Global Helpers) and always accepts las_1_path /
# las_2_path, so the formals()-sniffing fallback that used to guard this call is
# gone. apply_align defaults TRUE, which is what puts the returned las_1 points
# in the same frame as the ellipses and axis vectors drawn over them.
.vpc <- .vis_point_clouds(load        = vis_load_clouds,
                          las_1_path  = las_1_path,
                          las_2_path  = las_2_path,
                          apply_align = TRUE)

if (!exists("las_1") || !exists("las_2"))
  stop("las_1 / las_2 not in scope after loading - check what .vis_point_clouds() returns.")

if (params$make_plots) {

  max_pts_xy  <- 1000L
  half_len_xy <- (ransac_slice_top - ransac_slice_bot) / 2 * 3

  # Draw the las_1 points from the loader's RETURNED frame (.vpc$pts_1), which
  # carries the Stage 1A alignment, NOT from las_1@data - the LAS object is left
  # in the raw disk frame on purpose. Using the raw object here would put the
  # las_1 points in a different frame from the ellipse centres and axis vectors
  # (both aligned-frame), which is exactly the mismatch this loader exists to
  # avoid. las_2 is the reference cloud and is returned untransformed.
  src_1 <- .vpc$pts_1
  src_2 <- .vpc$pts_2
  if (is.null(src_1) || is.null(src_2))
    stop("Loader returned no pts_1 / pts_2 - check .vis_point_clouds() output.")

  stem_pts_xy <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_stage1)), function(i) {
    tid1 <- pairs_stage1$TreeID_1[i]
    tid2 <- pairs_stage1$TreeID_2[i]

    pts1_all <- src_1[src_1$TreeID == tid1, c("X","Y","Z","TreeID")]
    if (nrow(pts1_all) == 0) return(NULL)
    z0_1 <- min(pts1_all$Z)
    pts1 <- pts1_all[pts1_all$Z - z0_1 >= ransac_slice_bot &
                     pts1_all$Z - z0_1 <= ransac_slice_top, ]
    if (nrow(pts1) > max_pts_xy) pts1 <- pts1[sample.int(nrow(pts1), max_pts_xy), ]
    pts1 <- pts1 |> mutate(cloud = "las_1")

    pts2_all <- src_2[src_2$TreeID == tid2, c("X","Y","Z","TreeID")]
    if (nrow(pts2_all) == 0) return(NULL)
    z0_2 <- min(pts2_all$Z)
    pts2 <- pts2_all[pts2_all$Z - z0_2 >= ransac_slice_bot &
                     pts2_all$Z - z0_2 <= ransac_slice_top, ]
    if (nrow(pts2) > max_pts_xy) pts2 <- pts2[sample.int(nrow(pts2), max_pts_xy), ]
    pts2 <- pts2 |> mutate(cloud = "las_2")

    bind_rows(pts1, pts2)
  }))

  global_cx_xy <- mean(stem_pts_xy$X, na.rm = TRUE)
  global_cy_xy <- mean(stem_pts_xy$Y, na.rm = TRUE)
  stem_pts_xy  <- stem_pts_xy |>
    mutate(X_local = X - global_cx_xy, Y_local = Y - global_cy_xy)

  pts_1_xy <- stem_pts_xy |> filter(cloud == "las_1")
  pts_2_xy <- stem_pts_xy |> filter(cloud == "las_2")

  # ── Vector-placement helper: XY from mean of kept-ellipse centres ─────────
  # Positions the PCA vector's XY location at the average (center_x, center_y)
  # of that tree's kept/valid ellipses for this epoch (ellipses_zt_*_valid),
  # rather than the centroid of the raw extracted stem points. Z is still
  # taken from the raw stem-point centroid, unchanged from before.
  make_vec_segs_xy_ellipse_centre <- function(vecs_df, pts_df, ell_valid_list,
                                              local_cx, local_cy) {
    z_centroids <- pts_df |>
      dplyr::group_by(TreeID) |>
      dplyr::summarise(cz = mean(Z, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

    ellipse_centroids <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(ell_valid_list), function(tid_chr) {
      df <- ell_valid_list[[tid_chr]]
      if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) return(NULL)
      tibble::tibble(
        TreeID = as.integer(tid_chr),
        cx     = mean(df$center_x, na.rm = TRUE),
        cy     = mean(df$center_y, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
    }))

    centroids <- dplyr::inner_join(ellipse_centroids, z_centroids, by = "TreeID")

    dplyr::inner_join(vecs_df, centroids, by = "TreeID") |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        x0 = (cx - vx * half_len_xy) - local_cx,
        y0 = (cy - vy * half_len_xy) - local_cy,
        z0 =  cz - vz * half_len_xy,
        x1 = (cx + vx * half_len_xy) - local_cx,
        y1 = (cy + vy * half_len_xy) - local_cy,
        z1 =  cz + vz * half_len_xy
      )
  }

  segs_xy_1 <- tryCatch(
    make_vec_segs_xy_ellipse_centre(vecs_xy_1, pts_1_xy, ellipses_zt_1_valid,
                                    global_cx_xy, global_cy_xy),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  segs_xy_2 <- tryCatch(
    make_vec_segs_xy_ellipse_centre(vecs_xy_2, pts_2_xy, ellipses_zt_2_valid,
                                    global_cx_xy, global_cy_xy),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  p_xy3d <- plot_ly(
    data = stem_pts_xy, x = ~X_local, y = ~Y_local, z = ~Z,
    color = ~cloud, colors = c("las_1" = COL_1, "las_2" = COL_2),
    type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
    marker = list(size = 2, opacity = 0.6), hoverinfo = "none"
  )

  if (!is.null(segs_xy_1) && nrow(segs_xy_1) > 0) {
    p_xy3d <- p_xy3d |> add_trace(
      x = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_1$x0, segs_xy_1$x1, NA)),
      y = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_1$y0, segs_xy_1$y1, NA)),
      z = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_1$z0, segs_xy_1$z1, NA)),
      type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "PCA vector las_1",
      line = list(color = COL_1, width = 6),
      hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (!is.null(segs_xy_2) && nrow(segs_xy_2) > 0) {
    p_xy3d <- p_xy3d |> add_trace(
      x = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_2$x0, segs_xy_2$x1, NA)),
      y = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_2$y0, segs_xy_2$y1, NA)),
      z = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_2$z0, segs_xy_2$z1, NA)),
      type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "PCA vector las_2",
      line = list(color = COL_2, width = 6),
      hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE
    )
  }

  p_xy3d |> layout(
    title = "Stem points (overlap window, 1000 pts/tree) with PCA stem vectors",
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "X local (m)"),
      yaxis = list(title = "Y local (m)"),
      zaxis = list(title = "Z (m)"),
      aspectmode = "data",
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.5, y = 1.5, z = 0.8))
    ),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Cloud / Vector"))
  )
}
```

### Vis - 3D stem centres with regression axis vectors

The two other 3-D stem visualisations from earlier revisions of this workflow
(raw stem points with vectors, and the per-tree single-stem panel) required
`las_1`/`las_2` in memory and have therefore been dropped from Stage 2. This
panel uses only the Stage 1 ellipse centres, so it works with no point-cloud
data loaded. It shows only the pairs whose stems both survived the 2.1.2
stem-level MAD filter.

```{r}
#| label: fig-3d-centers-with-vectors
#| fig-cap: "3D stem centres for pairs kept after the 2.1.2 stem MAD filter, with PCA stem axis vectors."

if (params$make_plots) {

  # Draw only the pairs that survived the 2.1.2 stem-level MAD filter.
  # pairs_stem_mad is built in the diag-stem-mad-kept-count chunk: it is the
  # input pair table restricted to stems in stems_kept_1 / stems_kept_2 (NULL if
  # none survive, and the full input set when run_stem_mad = FALSE).
  if (!exists("pairs_stem_mad"))
    stop("pairs_stem_mad not found - run the 2.1.2 stem-MAD chunk before this figure.")

  vis_pairs_ctr <- pairs_stem_mad

  if (is.null(vis_pairs_ctr) || nrow(vis_pairs_ctr) == 0) {
    cat("No pairs survived the 2.1.2 stem MAD filter - nothing to plot.")
  } else {

    half_len_xy <- (ransac_slice_top - ransac_slice_bot) / 2 * 3

    slice_pts_xy <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(vis_pairs_ctr)), function(i) {
      tid1     <- vis_pairs_ctr$TreeID_1[i]
      tid2     <- vis_pairs_ctr$TreeID_2[i]
      tid1_chr <- as.character(tid1)
      tid2_chr <- as.character(tid2)

      c1 <- ellipses_zt_1_valid_all[[tid1_chr]]
      c2 <- ellipses_zt_2_valid_all[[tid2_chr]]

      bind_rows(
        if (!is.null(c1) && nrow(c1) > 0)
          c1 |> mutate(X = center_x, Y = center_y, Z = slice_z,
                       TreeID = tid1, cloud = "las_1") else NULL,
        if (!is.null(c2) && nrow(c2) > 0)
          c2 |> mutate(X = center_x, Y = center_y, Z = slice_z,
                       TreeID = as.integer(tid2), cloud = "las_2") else NULL
      )
    }))

    if (nrow(slice_pts_xy) > 0) {
      global_cx_xy <- mean(slice_pts_xy$X, na.rm = TRUE)
      global_cy_xy <- mean(slice_pts_xy$Y, na.rm = TRUE)
      slice_pts_xy <- slice_pts_xy |>
        mutate(X_local = X - global_cx_xy, Y_local = Y - global_cy_xy)

      pts_1_xy <- slice_pts_xy |> filter(cloud == "las_1")
      pts_2_xy <- slice_pts_xy |> filter(cloud == "las_2")

      segs_xy_1 <- tryCatch(
        make_vec_segs_xy(vecs_xy_1, pts_1_xy, global_cx_xy, global_cy_xy),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      segs_xy_2 <- tryCatch(
        make_vec_segs_xy(vecs_xy_2, pts_2_xy, global_cx_xy, global_cy_xy),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )

      p_xy3d <- plot_ly(
        data = slice_pts_xy, x = ~X_local, y = ~Y_local, z = ~Z,
        color = ~cloud, colors = c("las_1" = "darkslategrey", "las_2" = "tomato4"),
        type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(size = 3, opacity = 0.7),
        text = ~paste("TreeID:", TreeID), hoverinfo = "text"
      )

      if (!is.null(segs_xy_1) && nrow(segs_xy_1) > 0) {
        p_xy3d <- p_xy3d |> plotly::add_trace(
          x = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_1$x0, segs_xy_1$x1, NA)),
          y = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_1$y0, segs_xy_1$y1, NA)),
          z = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_1$z0, segs_xy_1$z1, NA)),
          type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "PCA vector las_1",
          line = list(color = COL_1, width = 6),
          hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE
        )
      }

      if (!is.null(segs_xy_2) && nrow(segs_xy_2) > 0) {
        p_xy3d <- p_xy3d |> plotly::add_trace(
          x = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_2$x0, segs_xy_2$x1, NA)),
          y = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_2$y0, segs_xy_2$y1, NA)),
          z = as.vector(rbind(segs_xy_2$z0, segs_xy_2$z1, NA)),
          type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "PCA vector las_2",
          line = list(color = COL_2, width = 6),
          hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE
        )
      }

      p_xy3d |> plotly::layout(
        title = "Matched Stem Centres & PCA Vectors (kept after 2.1.2 stem MAD)",
        scene = list(
          xaxis = list(title = "X local (m)"),
          yaxis = list(title = "Y local (m)"),
          zaxis = list(title = "Z (m)"),
          aspectmode = "data",
          camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.8, y = 1.8, z = 1.0))
        ),
        legend = list(title = list(text = "Cloud / Vector"))
      )
    } else {
      cat("No valid stem centres found to plot.")
    }
  }
}
```

### Vis - 3D single-stem regression axis vectors

```{r}
#| label: params-fig-stem-axis-vectors-per-tree
#| code-summary: "Parameters - fig-stem-axis-vectors-per-tree"


# ── Point clouds for this figure ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stage 2 does not load point clouds at the top, so this figure loads its own. It
# defaults to FALSE because the figure above will normally have loaded them
# already in the same session.
#   vis_load_clouds <- TRUE   read las_1 / las_2 from disk
#   vis_load_clouds <- FALSE  reuse the clouds already in memory (no disk read)
vis_load_clouds <- FALSE

vis_all_paired_trees_s2 <- FALSE
vis_selected_tids_s2    <- c(1)
s2_vis_max_pts          <- 1000L
s2_ring_n               <- 60L

.par_apply("params-fig-stem-axis-vectors-per-tree")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-stem-axis-vectors-per-tree
#| fig-cap: "3-D stem points with fitted PCA axis vector and kept-ellipse rings, one tree per plot."

.vpc <- .vis_point_clouds(load = vis_load_clouds)

# las_1 stem points in the Stage 1A-aligned frame (matches the vectors + rings);
# las_2 is the untransformed reference. Draw points from these, not las_*@data.
pts_1_aligned <- .vpc$pts_1
pts_2_aligned <- .vpc$pts_2


s2_vec_half_len         <- (ransac_slice_top - ransac_slice_bot) / 2 * 3

# ── extract_stem_pts_window: defined here, used only in this chunk ─────────
# Stem points for one tree, windowed to the same [ransac_slice_bot,
# ransac_slice_top] range the ellipses/axis vector were fit on. Takes a plain
# point frame (X/Y/Z/TreeID) from the loader - .vpc$pts_1 for las_1 carries the
# Stage 1A alignment, so the points share the vectors' frame; reading las_1@data
# directly would put them back in the raw disk frame.
extract_stem_pts_window <- function(pts, tid, max_pts) {
  df <- pts[pts$TreeID == tid, c("X", "Y", "Z")]
  if (nrow(df) < 3L) return(NULL)
  z0  <- min(df$Z)
  df  <- df[df$Z - z0 >= ransac_slice_bot & df$Z - z0 <= ransac_slice_top, ]
  if (nrow(df) < 3L) return(NULL)
  if (nrow(df) > max_pts) df <- df[sample.int(nrow(df), max_pts), ]
  df
}

if (vis_all_paired_trees_s2) {
  vis_pairs_s2 <- pairs_stage1
} else {
  vis_pairs_s2 <- pairs_stage1[pairs_stage1$TreeID_1 %in% vis_selected_tids_s2, ]
  if (nrow(vis_pairs_s2) == 0L)
    warning("[vis s2] None of vis_selected_tids_s2 matched pairs_stage1$TreeID_1.")
}

if (params$make_plots && nrow(vis_pairs_s2) > 0L) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(vis_pairs_s2))) {
    tid1 <- vis_pairs_s2$TreeID_1[i]; tid2 <- vis_pairs_s2$TreeID_2[i]
    ax1  <- vecs_xy_1[vecs_xy_1$TreeID == tid1, c("vx", "vy", "vz")]
    ax2  <- vecs_xy_2[vecs_xy_2$TreeID == tid2, c("vx", "vy", "vz")]

    sp1 <- extract_stem_pts_window(pts_1_aligned, tid1, s2_vis_max_pts)
    if (!is.null(sp1) && nrow(ax1) == 1L && !anyNA(ax1)) {
      # NOTE: build_pair_rings still receives the raw las_1 object. If it uses
      # las_1 for any Z reference, that is the raw disk frame while the ellipse
      # centres (and now the stem points) are Stage 1A-aligned - the rings could
      # sit off the stem. build_pair_rings is defined outside this file; check it
      # and pass an aligned Z source if so.
      rg1 <- build_pair_rings(ellipses_zt_1_valid, tid1, las_1, s2_ring_n)
      cx1 <- mean(sp1$X); cy1 <- mean(sp1$Y); cz1 <- mean(sp1$Z)
      sp1$Xloc <- sp1$X - cx1; sp1$Yloc <- sp1$Y - cy1

      seg1 <- data.frame(
        x0 = -ax1$vx * s2_vec_half_len, x1 = ax1$vx * s2_vec_half_len,
        y0 = -ax1$vy * s2_vec_half_len, y1 = ax1$vy * s2_vec_half_len,
        z0 = cz1 - ax1$vz * s2_vec_half_len, z1 = cz1 + ax1$vz * s2_vec_half_len
      )

      p1 <- plot_ly() |>
        add_trace(data = sp1, x = ~Xloc, y = ~Yloc, z = ~Z,
                  type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers", name = "las_1 pts",
                  marker = list(size = 1.5, color = COL_1, opacity = 0.5))
      if (!is.null(rg1) && nrow(rg1) > 0L) {
        rg1$Xloc <- rg1$X - cx1; rg1$Yloc <- rg1$Y - cy1
        p1 <- p1 |> add_trace(
          data = rg1, x = ~Xloc, y = ~Yloc, z = ~Z,
          type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "ellipses las_1",
          line = list(color = COL_1, width = 3), hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE)
      }
      p1 <- p1 |> add_trace(
        x = c(seg1$x0, seg1$x1), y = c(seg1$y0, seg1$y1), z = c(seg1$z0, seg1$z1),
        type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "PCA vector las_1",
        line = list(color = "gold", width = 6), hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE)
      p1 <- p1 |> layout(
        title = sprintf("las_1 Tree %d \u2014 PCA stem axis vector", tid1),
        scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "X local (m)"),
                     yaxis = list(title = "Y local (m)"),
                     zaxis = list(title = "Z (m)"), aspectmode = "data"))
      print(p1)
    }

    sp2 <- extract_stem_pts_window(pts_2_aligned, tid2, s2_vis_max_pts)
    if (!is.null(sp2) && nrow(ax2) == 1L && !anyNA(ax2)) {
      rg2 <- build_pair_rings(ellipses_zt_2_valid, tid2, las_2, s2_ring_n)
      cx2 <- mean(sp2$X); cy2 <- mean(sp2$Y); cz2 <- mean(sp2$Z)
      sp2$Xloc <- sp2$X - cx2; sp2$Yloc <- sp2$Y - cy2

      seg2 <- data.frame(
        x0 = -ax2$vx * s2_vec_half_len, x1 = ax2$vx * s2_vec_half_len,
        y0 = -ax2$vy * s2_vec_half_len, y1 = ax2$vy * s2_vec_half_len,
        z0 = cz2 - ax2$vz * s2_vec_half_len, z1 = cz2 + ax2$vz * s2_vec_half_len
      )

      p2 <- plot_ly() |>
        add_trace(data = sp2, x = ~Xloc, y = ~Yloc, z = ~Z,
                  type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers", name = "las_2 pts",
                  marker = list(size = 1.5, color = COL_2, opacity = 0.5))
      if (!is.null(rg2) && nrow(rg2) > 0L) {
        rg2$Xloc <- rg2$X - cx2; rg2$Yloc <- rg2$Y - cy2
        p2 <- p2 |> add_trace(
          data = rg2, x = ~Xloc, y = ~Yloc, z = ~Z,
          type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "ellipses las_2",
          line = list(color = COL_2, width = 3), hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE)
      }
      p2 <- p2 |> add_trace(
        x = c(seg2$x0, seg2$x1), y = c(seg2$y0, seg2$y1), z = c(seg2$z0, seg2$z1),
        type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines", name = "PCA vector las_2",
        line = list(color = "gold", width = 6), hoverinfo = "none", inherit = FALSE)
      p2 <- p2 |> layout(
        title = sprintf("las_2 Tree %d \u2014 PCA stem axis vector", tid2),
        scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "X local (m)"),
                     yaxis = list(title = "Y local (m)"),
                     zaxis = list(title = "Z (m)"), aspectmode = "data"))
      print(p2)
    }
  }
}
```

## 2.3 XYZ Rotation from Stem Vectors (IRLS + SVD)

Solves a full 3D rotation from the paired stem vectors by IRLS with Tukey
biweighting. The SVD operates on 3D unit vectors, so the solver sees tilt
magnitude and tilt direction, and the solved rotation retains its yaw content.
Stage 3 applies it to the cloud; Stage 5 solves a further Z-only rotation from
the inter-tree line network, and Stage 6 composes the two.

The input is pairs_axis: pairs surviving the stem pre-filter (2.1.1), the
kept-count MAD filter (2.1.2) and the gold-length straightness gate (2.1.3).

Seven static weights are computed per stem and multiplied into a pair
weight. Two come from the 4 m axis window the vectors were fitted on, two from
the kept-centre ledger built in 2.2, and three from the 2.1.3 gold window, which
measures shape and precision over more of the stem and separates them from one
another:

weight	source	direction
thickness	avg_semi_axis_m	larger is better
straightness (bend)	bend_adj_deg, gold window, floor removed – angle between the base and top sub-window directions	smaller is better
straightness (shape)	geometric mean of curv_cm and sag_cm, gold window, both floor-removed	smaller is better
centre precision	noise_cm, gold window	smaller is better
length	win_len / 4, capped at 1	longer is better
bottom-2 m count	kept ellipses with slice_z in the bottom 2 m, count / 10 capped at 1	more is better
bottom-2 m span	bottom 2 m split into two 1 m halves; 1 if both are represented by a kept ellipse, 0.5 if only one is	more coverage is better

curv_cm and sag_cm are two estimators of one property, so they enter as a
single shape weight: a stem is penalised when both agree it is bent. Each
weight is scaled across the body of its distribution – norm_clip trims a
quantile from each end before the ramp is laid down, and stems beyond the clip
sit on the floor – so a long tail cannot compress the rest of the set into the
top of the ramp. The chunk reports how many stems each category separates.

Categories combine multiplicatively, with thickness raised to the second power;
influence is additive in log space, so the exponent is a twofold weighting. The
angular-difference table is computed first as a pre-solve diagnostic, to be read
against the residuals the solver produces from the same vectors.


```{r}
#| label: params-irls-svd-xyz
#| code-summary: "Parameters - IRLS + SVD full 3D rotation from paired regression stem vectors, yaw retained"

# ── IRLS settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
irls_max_iter   <- 30
irls_tol        <- 1e-6
irls_weight_exp <- 1.0

# ── Static weight settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Categories multiply, so influence is additive in log space and an exponent is
# literally an n-fold weighting.
#
# Shape is ONE category, not two. 2.1.3 produces curv_cm and sag_cm - block
# medians against a quadratic through every centre - and they are two
# estimators of a single property, not two properties. Given a category each
# they would count stem shape twice; combined as a geometric mean the category
# is worth one weight and gains robustness, since a stem is penalised when both
# estimators agree it is bent rather than whenever the harsher one says so.
pw_diameter    <- 2
pw_bend        <- 1
pw_shape       <- 1
pw_length      <- 1
pw_count       <- 1
pw_span        <- 1
pw_noise       <- 1

# Floors keep every per-stem weight in [floor, 1]. Without them the
# worst-in-sample stem would score exactly 0 and, because pair weights are a
# product, would annihilate its pair rather than merely down-weighting it.
w_min_diameter <- 0.20
w_min_bend     <- 0.30
w_min_shape    <- 0.30
w_min_length   <- 0.10
w_min_noise    <- 0.20

diam_weight_exp     <- 0.2   # shape of the thickness ramp
bend_weight_exp     <- 1.0   # shape of the bend ramp
shape_weight_exp    <- 1.0   # shape of the curvature/sag ramp
noise_weight_exp    <- 1.0   # shape of the centre-precision ramp

# The ramp is laid across the BODY of each distribution, not across its full
# range. These inputs are long-tailed, and a min/max denominator hands the
# single most extreme stem the entire dynamic range: every other stem then
# lands within a couple of percent of 1 and the weight cannot separate the
# stems it exists to rank. Trimming a quantile from each end puts the ramp
# where the stems actually are and lets the tail sit on the floor, which is
# what the floor is for.
norm_clip <- 0.05   # quantile trimmed from each end before scaling

# Bottom-2 m section settings: count is read straight off the kept-centre
# ledger (no fitted quantity involved), so, unlike the other categories,
# count and span get no floor - a stem with nothing in the bottom 2 m should
# be able to zero its pair, not merely be down-weighted.
bottom2m_window_m <- 2.0   # length of the "bottom 2 m" section examined here
count_scale       <- 10    # kept-ellipse count / count_scale, capped at 1

IRLS_ANNEAL_ITERS <- 4   # iterations to hold the wide, fixed bandwidth before

.par_apply("params-irls-svd-xyz")
```

```{r}
#| label: irls-svd-xyz
#| code-summary: "IRLS + SVD full 3D rotation from paired regression stem vectors, yaw retained"

# ── Vector lookup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# By TreeID, never by row position: vecs_xy_* are built from pairs_axis, so
# positional indexing breaks the moment the pair set is filtered.
.vt_get <- function(vt, tid, col) {
  i <- match(as.character(tid), as.character(vt$TreeID))
  if (is.na(i)) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(vt[[col]][i])
}
.v_of <- function(vt, tid) {
  i <- match(as.character(tid), as.character(vt$TreeID))
  if (is.na(i)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_))
  as.numeric(vt[i, c("vx", "vy", "vz")])
}

# ── Angular differences (pre-solve diagnostic) ────────────────────────────────
# Full 3D angle between paired stem vectors, plus the tilt-only angle.
pair_table_xy <- data.frame(
  TreeID_1 = pairs_axis$TreeID_1,
  TreeID_2 = pairs_axis$TreeID_2,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

pair_table_xy$angle_deg <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_table_xy)), function(i) {
  a <- .v_of(vecs_xy_1, pair_table_xy$TreeID_1[i])
  b <- .v_of(vecs_xy_2, pair_table_xy$TreeID_2[i])
  if (any(is.na(a)) || any(is.na(b))) return(NA_real_)
  acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, sum(a * b)))) * 180 / pi
}, numeric(1))

pair_table_xy$tilt_angle_deg <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_table_xy)), function(i) {
  a <- .v_of(vecs_xy_1, pair_table_xy$TreeID_1[i])
  b <- .v_of(vecs_xy_2, pair_table_xy$TreeID_2[i])
  if (any(is.na(a)) || any(is.na(b))) return(NA_real_)
  compute_tilt_angle(a, b)
}, numeric(1))

angular_diag <- pair_table_xy
cat(sprintf("Angular differences for %d pair(s) | 3D median %.2f deg | tilt median %.2f deg\n",
            sum(!is.na(pair_table_xy$angle_deg)),
            median(pair_table_xy$angle_deg, na.rm = TRUE),
            median(pair_table_xy$tilt_angle_deg, na.rm = TRUE)))


# ── Subset to pairs with valid stem vectors in both epochs ────────────────────
# pairs_axis is the gated set. Solving on pairs_stage1 would silently readmit
# every stem 2.1.1, 2.1.2 and 2.1.3 removed. Joined by TreeID rather than bound
# positionally, so the join stays correct however the pair set is filtered.
pairs_valid_xyz <- pairs_axis |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    vecs_xy_1 |> dplyr::select(TreeID, vx1 = vx, vy1 = vy, vz1 = vz),
    by = c("TreeID_1" = "TreeID")
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    vecs_xy_2 |> dplyr::select(TreeID, vx2 = vx, vy2 = vy, vz2 = vz),
    by = c("TreeID_2" = "TreeID")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vx1), !is.na(vx2))

V1_xyz <- as.matrix(pairs_valid_xyz[, c("vx1","vy1","vz1")])
V2_xyz <- as.matrix(pairs_valid_xyz[, c("vx2","vy2","vz2")])

# ── Per-stem weight inputs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Shape is no longer read from here. rms_cm confounds bend, wander and centre
# error in one number, and its length rescaling assumed deviation grows as L^2 -
# an exponent 2.1.3 measures at roughly 0.84 on this data. The separated gold-
# window scores are used instead.
.stem_vals <- function(vt, ids) {
  rad  <- vapply(ids, function(t) .vt_get(vt, t, "avg_semi_axis_m"), numeric(1))
  len  <- vapply(ids, function(t) .vt_get(vt, t, "win_len"),   numeric(1))
  frac <- pmin(1, len / axis_window_m)
  list(rad = rad, frac = frac, len = len)
}

sv1 <- .stem_vals(vecs_xy_1, pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_1)
sv2 <- .stem_vals(vecs_xy_2, pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_2)

# A missing value falls back to the pooled median, so a gap down-weights
# nothing rather than zeroing a pair.
.fill2 <- function(a, b) {
  m <- median(c(a, b), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(m)) m <- 1
  list(replace(a, !is.finite(a), m), replace(b, !is.finite(b), m))
}
.t <- .fill2(sv1$rad, sv2$rad);           sv1$rad <- .t[[1]];      sv2$rad <- .t[[2]]
.t <- .fill2(sv1$frac, sv2$frac);         sv1$frac <- .t[[1]];     sv2$frac <- .t[[2]]

# ── Bottom-2 m section: kept-ellipse count and span weights ───────────────────
# Read directly from the kept-centre ledger (ax_by_stem, built in 2.2) rather
# than from vecs_xy_*, since the axis-window vectors only carry n_win over the
# full 4 m window and say nothing about how those centres are distributed
# within its bottom half. z_lo mirrors the definition in .fit_axis_reg (the
# lowest kept centre for that stem), so "bottom 2 m" here is the same origin
# the axis fit itself used.
#
# count : kept ellipses with slice_z in [z_lo, z_lo + 2 m], scaled by
#         count_scale and capped at 1.
# span  : the 2 m section split into two 1 m halves; 1 if both halves contain
#         at least one kept ellipse, 0.5 if only one half does, 0 if neither.
.bottom2m_stats <- function(tid, epoch) {
  d <- ax_by_stem[[paste(epoch, tid, sep = "|")]]
  if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(c(count = 0, span_w = 0))

  z_lo  <- min(d$slice_z)
  half  <- bottom2m_window_m / 2
  bin1  <- d$slice_z <= z_lo + half + 1e-9
  bin2  <- d$slice_z >  z_lo + half + 1e-9 & d$slice_z <= z_lo + bottom2m_window_m + 1e-9
  n_bins_present <- sum(any(bin1), any(bin2))

  c(count  = sum(bin1 | bin2),
    span_w = c(0, 0.5, 1)[n_bins_present + 1])
}

bs1 <- vapply(as.character(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_1), .bottom2m_stats,
              numeric(2), epoch = "las_1")
bs2 <- vapply(as.character(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_2), .bottom2m_stats,
              numeric(2), epoch = "las_2")

w_count_1 <- pmin(1, bs1["count", ] / count_scale)
w_count_2 <- pmin(1, bs2["count", ] / count_scale)
w_span_1  <- bs1["span_w", ]
w_span_2  <- bs2["span_w", ]

# ── Normalise each category to [floor, 1] across all stems in the solve ───────
# Pooled over both epochs, so a stem is scored against the whole surviving set
# rather than against its own cloud. The scale comes from quantiles rather than
# from min and max - see norm_clip above - and values beyond the clip are
# pinned to the ends of the ramp rather than dropped, so an extreme stem lands
# on the floor instead of defining the scale for everyone else.
.rng <- function(all_x) {
  q <- stats::quantile(all_x, c(norm_clip, 1 - norm_clip), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (diff(q) < 1e-9) q <- range(all_x, na.rm = TRUE)   # degenerate: fall back
  as.numeric(q)
}
.norm_up <- function(x, all_x, floor_w, expo) {
  r <- .rng(all_x)
  u <- if (diff(r) < 1e-9) rep(1, length(x))
       else pmin(1, pmax(0, (x - r[1]) / diff(r)))
  floor_w + (1 - floor_w) * u^expo
}
.norm_down <- function(x, all_x, floor_w, expo) {
  r <- .rng(all_x)
  u <- if (diff(r) < 1e-9) rep(1, length(x))
       else 1 - pmin(1, pmax(0, (x - r[1]) / diff(r)))
  floor_w + (1 - floor_w) * u^expo
}

rad_all <- c(sv1$rad, sv2$rad)

# ── Shape and precision weights, from the 2.1.3 gold window ──────────────────
# Four scores that rms_cm previously rolled into one:
#   bend_adj_deg - angle between the base and top sub-window directions, floor
#                  removed. Reads DIRECTION rather than position.
#   curv_cm      - deviation of the sub-window median centres from the stem's
#                  own line, noise floor removed. Robust, undirected.
#   sag_cm       - kappa L^2 / 8 from the quadratic through every centre. Same
#                  property as curv_cm, different estimator.
#   noise_cm     - the RANSAC centre precision those floors were measured from.
# Separating them matters because they act on the solve differently. A bent
# stem still yields a well-determined direction vector, just not one that
# represents a straight axis. A stem with jittery centres yields a direction
# vector that is simply imprecise, whatever its shape. Weighting on rms_cm
# treated those as the same defect.
#
# Read from the GOLD window, not the 4 m axis window the vectors were fitted
# on: these are properties of the stem, and the gold window measures them over
# more of it.
.gold_of <- function(ids, epoch, col) {
  i <- match(paste(epoch, as.character(ids), sep = "|"),
             paste(gold_stems$epoch, gold_stems$TreeID, sep = "|"))
  as.numeric(gold_stems[[col]][i])
}
bd1 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_1, "las_1", "bend_adj_deg")
bd2 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_2, "las_2", "bend_adj_deg")
cv1 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_1, "las_1", "curv_cm")
cv2 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_2, "las_2", "curv_cm")
sg1 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_1, "las_1", "sag_cm")
sg2 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_2, "las_2", "sag_cm")
nz1 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_1, "las_1", "noise_cm")
nz2 <- .gold_of(pairs_valid_xyz$TreeID_2, "las_2", "noise_cm")
.t <- .fill2(bd1, bd2); bd1 <- .t[[1]]; bd2 <- .t[[2]]
.t <- .fill2(cv1, cv2); cv1 <- .t[[1]]; cv2 <- .t[[2]]
.t <- .fill2(sg1, sg2); sg1 <- .t[[1]]; sg2 <- .t[[2]]
.t <- .fill2(nz1, nz2); nz1 <- .t[[1]]; nz2 <- .t[[2]]
bend_all  <- c(bd1, bd2)
curv_all  <- c(cv1, cv2)
sag_all   <- c(sg1, sg2)
noise_all <- c(nz1, nz2)

w_diam_1     <- .norm_up(sv1$rad, rad_all, w_min_diameter, diam_weight_exp)
w_diam_2     <- .norm_up(sv2$rad, rad_all, w_min_diameter, diam_weight_exp)
w_bend_1     <- .norm_down(bd1, bend_all, w_min_bend, bend_weight_exp)
w_bend_2     <- .norm_down(bd2, bend_all, w_min_bend, bend_weight_exp)

# The two shape estimators are normalised separately - they are on different
# scales, sag running about 1.5x curv - then combined geometrically, so the
# category as a whole still spans [floor, 1].
w_curv_1     <- .norm_down(cv1, curv_all, w_min_shape, shape_weight_exp)
w_curv_2     <- .norm_down(cv2, curv_all, w_min_shape, shape_weight_exp)
w_sag_1      <- .norm_down(sg1, sag_all,  w_min_shape, shape_weight_exp)
w_sag_2      <- .norm_down(sg2, sag_all,  w_min_shape, shape_weight_exp)
w_shape_1    <- sqrt(w_curv_1 * w_sag_1)
w_shape_2    <- sqrt(w_curv_2 * w_sag_2)

w_length_1   <- w_min_length + (1 - w_min_length) * sv1$frac
w_length_2   <- w_min_length + (1 - w_min_length) * sv2$frac
w_noise_1    <- .norm_down(nz1, noise_all, w_min_noise, noise_weight_exp)
w_noise_2    <- .norm_down(nz2, noise_all, w_min_noise, noise_weight_exp)

# ── Pair weights: the product of the two stems ────────────────────────────────
# A rotation constraint depends on both axes, so both stems must be good for
# the pair to count. Multiplying is stricter than averaging - two mediocre
# stems compound rather than cancel.
w_diam     <- w_diam_1     * w_diam_2
w_bend     <- w_bend_1     * w_bend_2
w_shape    <- w_shape_1    * w_shape_2
w_length   <- w_length_1   * w_length_2
w_count    <- w_count_1    * w_count_2
w_span     <- w_span_1     * w_span_2
w_noise    <- w_noise_1    * w_noise_2

w_static_raw <- w_diam^pw_diameter * w_bend^pw_bend * w_shape^pw_shape *
  w_length^pw_length * w_count^pw_count * w_span^pw_span * w_noise^pw_noise
w_static     <- w_static_raw / max(w_static_raw, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("Per-pair weights - thickness %.3f-%.3f | length %.3f-%.3f\n",
            min(w_diam), max(w_diam), min(w_length), max(w_length)))
cat(sprintf("Per-pair weights - bend %.3f-%.3f (bend_adj %.2f-%.2f deg)\n",
            min(w_bend), max(w_bend), min(bend_all), max(bend_all)))
cat(sprintf("Per-pair weights - shape %.3f-%.3f (curv %.2f-%.2f cm | sag %.2f-%.2f cm)\n",
            min(w_shape), max(w_shape), min(curv_all), max(curv_all),
            min(sag_all), max(sag_all)))
cat(sprintf("Bottom %.0f m kept-ellipse count - las_1 %d-%d | las_2 %d-%d\n",
            bottom2m_window_m, min(bs1["count", ]), max(bs1["count", ]),
            min(bs2["count", ]), max(bs2["count", ])))
cat(sprintf("Per-pair weights - bottom-2m count %.3f-%.3f | bottom-2m span %.3f-%.3f\n",
            min(w_count), max(w_count), min(w_span), max(w_span)))
cat(sprintf("Per-pair weights - centre precision %.3f-%.3f (noise_cm %.3f-%.3f cm)\n",
            min(w_noise), max(w_noise), min(noise_all), max(noise_all)))
# Two correlations worth watching. If the shape estimators agree closely the
# geometric mean is redundant and one could be dropped; if they disagree, the
# mean is doing real work. curv_cm and noise_cm are related by construction -
# curv is floor-subtracted using noise - so a high correlation there means the
# two weights are partly the same weight and one of pw_shape / pw_noise should
# come down.
cat(sprintf("Correlation - the two shape estimators %.2f | shape and precision %.2f\n",
            suppressWarnings(cor(curv_all, sag_all,   use = "complete.obs")),
            suppressWarnings(cor(curv_all, noise_all, use = "complete.obs"))))
# A weight that puts nearly every stem at 1, or nearly every stem on the floor,
# is not ranking anything. This counts how many it actually separates.
.spread <- function(w, fl) sum(w > fl + 1e-6 & w < 1 - 1e-6)
cat(sprintf("Stems strictly between floor and 1 (of %d): thickness %d | bend %d | shape %d | precision %d\n",
            2 * nrow(V1_xyz),
            .spread(c(w_diam_1, w_diam_2),   w_min_diameter),
            .spread(c(w_bend_1, w_bend_2),   w_min_bend),
            .spread(c(w_shape_1, w_shape_2), w_min_shape),
            .spread(c(w_noise_1, w_noise_2), w_min_noise)))
cat(sprintf("Combined w_static: %.3f-%.3f (median %.3f)\n",
            min(w_static), max(w_static), median(w_static)))

# ── IRLS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The SVD receives full 3D unit vectors so both tilt magnitude and tilt
# direction (compass azimuth of lean) inform the rotation estimate.
# Residuals are true 3D angular differences – the angle between v1 after
# rotation and v2 – rather than the tilt-only residual used previously.
# This ensures the outlier weighting correctly penalises pairs that disagree
# in any direction, not only in tilt magnitude.

C_IRLS_INIT       <- 6 * pi / 180
C_IRLS_FLOOR      <- 1.5 * pi / 180
                         # switching to the adaptive MAD-based one

# ── Seed rotation from an unweighted (static-only) Kabsch fit ─────────────────
# Starting the loop from R = identity means the very first residual vector
# *is* the raw pre-alignment misalignment. When that misalignment is small,
# this is harmless: the raw residual cloud is already centred near zero, so
# the adaptive MAD-based bandwidth below correctly isolates real outliers
# from a tight inlier cluster. When the true misalignment is large (e.g. the
# ~11 deg case), the raw residual cloud is instead centred around ~11 deg –
# and if the true inliers happen to cluster tightly there too (which they
# will, since they reflect the same real rotation), MAD stays small and the
# resulting c_irls becomes a narrow band centred on 11 deg. The redescending
# Tukey weight then hard-zeroes (not just downweights) any pair sitting even
# a bit outside that narrow band, which at this stage is likely to include
# plenty of genuinely good pairs. Once a majority of true inliers are zeroed
# in iteration 1, the next SVD fit is built from whatever small, possibly
# geometrically-degenerate subset survived – which can lock the whole loop
# onto a self-consistent but wrong answer (classic IRLS collapse from a bad
# initialization / breakdown of a redescending M-estimator).
#
# Seeding with a static-weighted-only fit (no redescending term, so nothing
# gets hard-zeroed) uses every pair to get R_rot_xyz close to the truth
# *before* the Tukey stage ever runs, so the adaptive bandwidth below starts
# from a residual cloud that is already centred near zero regardless of how
# large the original misalignment was.
R_rot_xyz <- solve_rotation_weighted(V1_xyz, V2_xyz, w_static)

w_xyz         <- rep(1, nrow(V1_xyz))
residuals_xyz <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(V1_xyz))

for (iter in seq_len(irls_max_iter)) {

  # Apply current rotation estimate to las_1 vectors
  V1_rotated <- t(R_rot_xyz %*% t(V1_xyz))

  # True 3D angular residual: angle between rotated v1 and v2
  residuals_xyz <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(V1_xyz)), function(i) {
    acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, sum(V1_rotated[i, ] * V2_xyz[i, ]))))
  }, numeric(1))

  # Bandwidth: hold the wide, fixed C_IRLS_INIT for the first few iterations
  # so a still-settling rotation estimate can't prematurely collapse the
  # adaptive MAD-based threshold and start permanently zeroing good pairs.
  mad_res <- mad(residuals_xyz, na.rm = TRUE, constant = 1)
  c_irls  <- if (iter <= IRLS_ANNEAL_ITERS) {
    max(C_IRLS_FLOOR, C_IRLS_INIT)
  } else {
    max(C_IRLS_FLOOR, 3 * mad_res)
  }
  u_xyz   <- residuals_xyz / c_irls
  w_irls  <- ifelse(abs(u_xyz) < 1, (1 - u_xyz^2)^2, 0)

  # Combine IRLS Tukey weights with static weights; normalise to [0, 1]
  w_agg_raw <- w_irls * w_static
  w_agg_max <- max(w_agg_raw, na.rm = TRUE)
  w_new     <- if (w_agg_max > 1e-10) w_agg_raw / w_agg_max else w_agg_raw

  # Don't allow early convergence while still on the fixed anneal bandwidth –
  # weights during that phase aren't yet the adaptive ones we want to settle on.
  if (iter > IRLS_ANNEAL_ITERS && max(abs(w_new - w_xyz)) < irls_tol) {
    w_xyz <- w_new
    break
  }
  w_xyz     <- w_new

  # SVD on full 3D vectors – solver sees tilt direction, not just magnitude
  R_rot_xyz <- solve_rotation_weighted(V1_xyz, V2_xyz, w_xyz)
}

# Final solve with converged weights
R_rot_xyz <- solve_rotation_weighted(V1_xyz, V2_xyz, w_xyz)

# ── Post-convergence diagnostics ──────────────────────────────────────────────
V1_rotated    <- t(R_rot_xyz %*% t(V1_xyz))
residuals_xyz <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(V1_xyz)), function(i) {
  acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, sum(V1_rotated[i, ] * V2_xyz[i, ]))))
}, numeric(1))

mad_res_final <- mad(residuals_xyz, na.rm = TRUE, constant = 1)
c_irls_final  <- max(C_IRLS_FLOOR, 3 * mad_res_final)
u_final       <- residuals_xyz / c_irls_final
w_irls_final  <- ifelse(abs(u_final) < 1, (1 - u_final^2)^2, 0)

n_out_xyz     <- sum(residuals_xyz > c_irls_final)
angle_rot_xyz <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, (sum(diag(R_rot_xyz)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi

cat(sprintf("Full 3D rotation angle: %.4f deg\n", angle_rot_xyz))
cat("Rotation matrix R_rot_xyz:\n"); print(round(R_rot_xyz, 6))

# ── XY tilt present in R_rot_xyz (pitch+roll only, excludes yaw) ──────────────
# Angle between the rotated +Z axis and the original +Z axis: a pure Z-axis
# spin (yaw) leaves +Z unchanged, so this isolates the tilt-away-from-vertical
# component of the full solved rotation.
z_axis_rotated_xyz <- R_rot_xyz %*% c(0, 0, 1)
xy_tilt_in_rot_xyz_deg <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, z_axis_rotated_xyz[3]))) * 180 / pi
cat(sprintf("XY tilt present in R_rot_xyz: %.4f deg\n", xy_tilt_in_rot_xyz_deg))

# ── Keep the full solved rotation (yaw retained, not stripped) ───────────────
# Earlier revisions extracted and cancelled the yaw component here, so the
# exported matrix held only pitch/roll and was named R_tilt_only. That
# stripping step is gone: R_xyz / angle_xyz below are simply aliases of the
# FULL solved 3D rotation R_rot_xyz / angle_rot_xyz, yaw included – which is
# why the variable is no longer called "tilt_only".
#
# NOTE: Stage 5 independently solves a further Z-only rotation from the
# inter-tree line network, and Stage 6 composes it on top of R_xyz. Because
# yaw is retained here rather than cancelled, that composition can
# double-count yaw. Stage 6 therefore exposes independent toggles for the XYZ
# and Z-only rotations so the two can be applied separately and compared.
yaw_in_R_xyz <- atan2(R_rot_xyz[2,1] - R_rot_xyz[1,2],
                      R_rot_xyz[1,1] + R_rot_xyz[2,2])   # diagnostic only
R_xyz     <- R_rot_xyz
angle_xyz <- angle_rot_xyz

cat(sprintf("Yaw present in R_rot_xyz: %.4f deg\n", yaw_in_R_xyz * 180 / pi))

# ── Tilt direction from weighted mean of per-pair XY vector differences ────────
# Reports which compass direction the global tilt correction points toward.
# Diagnostic – not used in the solve.
w_norm <- w_xyz / sum(w_xyz)

tilt_diff_mat <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(V1_xyz)), function(i) {
  c(V2_xyz[i, 1] - V1_xyz[i, 1], V2_xyz[i, 2] - V1_xyz[i, 2])
}, numeric(2)))
mean_tilt_xy     <- colSums(tilt_diff_mat * w_norm)
tilt_dir_deg     <- (atan2(mean_tilt_xy[2], mean_tilt_xy[1]) * 180 / pi) %% 360
tilt_consistency <- sqrt(sum(mean_tilt_xy^2))
cat(sprintf(
  "Tilt direction (XY plane, 0\u2013360\u00b0 CCW from +X): %.2f deg  |  consistency: %.4f\n",
  tilt_dir_deg, tilt_consistency
))

# ── Z-rotation component isolated from stem vector azimuths ──────────────────
az1    <- atan2(V1_xyz[, 2], V1_xyz[, 1])
az2    <- atan2(V2_xyz[, 2], V2_xyz[, 1])
az_diff_weighted <- atan2(
  sum(w_norm * sin(az2 - az1)),
  sum(w_norm * cos(az2 - az1))
)
z_rot_from_xyz_deg <- az_diff_weighted * 180 / pi

avg_ang_diff_weighted_deg <- sum(residuals_xyz * w_norm) * 180 / pi

# ── No sanity gate on the solved rotation ─────────────────────────────────────
# A 20-degree ceiling on angle_rot_xyz used to replace R_rot_xyz with the
# identity here. It gated on the TOTAL angle, which is dominated by the yaw
# component - and yaw is not what this step solves. Stem axes are near-vertical
# by the time they reach the SVD, so spinning them about Z barely moves the
# vectors and the yaw the solve returns is largely unconstrained (watch
# tilt_consistency, typically < 0.1). Stage 6 re-solves the Z rotation on its
# own terms regardless. The result was that a sound tilt correction could be
# discarded because it arrived alongside a large but irrelevant yaw, leaving the
# rough Stage 1A leg as the whole answer and its tilt error uncorrected.
# R_rot_xyz is now always kept; judge it from the reported angle, tilt and
# consistency rather than having it silently swapped for the identity.

# ── Combined per-pair diagnostic table ────────────────────────────────────────
# One row per pair actually used in the solve (pairs_valid_xyz). Pre-rotation
# angle/tilt come from the pair_table_xy diagnostic computed at the top of this
# chunk (joined by TreeID key, since pair_table_xy spans all of pairs_axis while
# pairs_valid_xyz is the subset with valid vectors in both epochs). Post-rotation
# angle/tilt are recomputed here from the FINAL converged R_rot_xyz. All static
# weight inputs/outputs (diameter, bend, shape, precision, length, bottom-2m
# count, bottom-2m span, per-epoch and combined) and the final aggregate
# cross-category weight (w_static) are carried through unchanged from the blocks
# above – nothing here is re-derived independently. Both shape inputs are shown
# beside the single weight they produce, so a stem where the two estimators
# disagree can be spotted from the table.

post_tilt_deg <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(V1_xyz)), function(i) {
  compute_tilt_angle(V1_rotated[i, ], V2_xyz[i, ])
}, numeric(1))

xyz_solve_diag <- pairs_valid_xyz |>
  dplyr::select(TreeID_1, TreeID_2) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pair_table_xy, by = c("TreeID_1", "TreeID_2")) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    angle_deg_pre_rot = angle_deg,
    tilt_deg_pre_rot  = tilt_angle_deg
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    angle_deg_post_rot   = residuals_xyz * 180 / pi,
    tilt_deg_post_rot    = post_tilt_deg,

    diam_e1              = sv1$rad,
    diam_e2              = sv2$rad,
    diam_w_e1            = w_diam_1,
    diam_w_e2            = w_diam_2,
    diam_w_comb          = w_diam,

    bend_e1              = bd1,
    bend_e2              = bd2,
    bend_w_e1            = w_bend_1,
    bend_w_e2            = w_bend_2,
    bend_w_comb          = w_bend,

    curv_e1              = cv1,
    curv_e2              = cv2,
    sag_e1               = sg1,
    sag_e2               = sg2,
    shape_w_e1           = w_shape_1,
    shape_w_e2           = w_shape_2,
    shape_w_comb         = w_shape,

    noise_e1             = nz1,
    noise_e2             = nz2,
    noise_w_e1           = w_noise_1,
    noise_w_e2           = w_noise_2,
    noise_w_comb         = w_noise,

    length_e1            = sv1$len,
    length_e2            = sv2$len,
    length_w_e1          = w_length_1,
    length_w_e2          = w_length_2,
    length_w_comb        = w_length,

    count_e1             = bs1["count", ],
    count_e2             = bs2["count", ],
    count_w_e1           = w_count_1,
    count_w_e2           = w_count_2,
    count_w_comb         = w_count,

    span_w_e1            = w_span_1,
    span_w_e2            = w_span_2,
    span_w_comb          = w_span,

    # Display-only re-normalisation. w_static itself stays scaled to a max of
    # 1, since that's the scale the IRLS loop and solve_rotation_weighted
    # expect - rescaling it here would change the solve, not just the table.
    # agg_weight is a separate column so it can read as each pair's SHARE of
    # total influence, which sums to 1 and is what a reader expects from a
    # weight distribution.
    agg_weight           = w_static / sum(w_static, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    TreeID_1, TreeID_2,
    angle_deg_pre_rot, angle_deg_post_rot,
    tilt_deg_pre_rot, tilt_deg_post_rot,
    diam_e1, diam_e2, diam_w_e1, diam_w_e2, diam_w_comb,
    bend_e1, bend_e2, bend_w_e1, bend_w_e2, bend_w_comb,
    curv_e1, curv_e2, sag_e1, sag_e2, shape_w_e1, shape_w_e2, shape_w_comb,
    noise_e1, noise_e2, noise_w_e1, noise_w_e2, noise_w_comb,
    length_e1, length_e2, length_w_e1, length_w_e2, length_w_comb,
    count_e1, count_e2, count_w_e1, count_w_e2, count_w_comb,
    span_w_e1, span_w_e2, span_w_comb,
    agg_weight
  )

cat("\nFull per-pair IRLS + SVD diagnostic table:\n")
print(xyz_solve_diag, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)

# ── Build pairs_stage2 – a NEW object, never a mutation of pairs_axis ────────
# pairs_axis is left untouched, so re-running this chunk always starts from the
# same input no matter how many times it has already run. Outlier pairs are
# identified by their TreeID_1/TreeID_2 key (not row position/index) and
# excluded via anti_join, so this is correct even when pairs_valid_xyz has
# fewer rows than pairs_axis (pairs missing a valid stem vector are left IN
# pairs_stage2 – only residual outliers are ever dropped here).
#
# pairs_stage2 is the pair list Stage 3 consumes.

pairs_valid_xyz$residual_xyz <- residuals_xyz
pairs_valid_xyz$w_irls_final <- w_irls_final
pairs_valid_xyz$w_static     <- w_static

outlier_pair_keys <- pairs_valid_xyz |>
  dplyr::filter(residual_xyz > c_irls_final) |>
  dplyr::select(TreeID_1, TreeID_2)

pairs_stage2 <- pairs_axis |>
  dplyr::anti_join(outlier_pair_keys, by = c("TreeID_1", "TreeID_2"))

n_outliers_xyz <- nrow(outlier_pair_keys)

.tally(n_pairs_irls_in   = nrow(pairs_axis),
       n_pairs_irls_kept = nrow(pairs_stage2))

# ── Diagnostics (reported at the end) ─────────────────────────────────────────
cat(sprintf("Paired stem vectors for 3D rotation solve: %d (of %d gated pair(s))\n",
            nrow(V1_xyz), nrow(pairs_axis)))
cat("NA in V1_xyz:", sum(is.na(V1_xyz)), " | NA in V2_xyz:", sum(is.na(V2_xyz)), "\n")
cat("NA/Inf in w_static:", sum(!is.finite(w_static)), "\n")
cat(sprintf("MAD residuals: %.4f deg\n", mad_res_final * 180 / pi))
if (n_outliers_xyz > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "Dropped %d outlier pair(s) into pairs_stage2 (residual > c_irls_final = %.4f deg)\n",
    n_outliers_xyz,
    c_irls_final * 180 / pi
  ))
}
cat(sprintf("IRLS-weighted average 3D angular residual: %.4f deg\n",
            avg_ang_diff_weighted_deg))
```

#| label: fig-irls-residuals-xyz
#| fig-cap: "True 3D angular residual per stem vector pair after IRLS convergence. Black circles show the pre-rotation 3D angular difference."

# Pre-rotation true 3D residuals (diagnostic only – computed outside IRLS)
residuals_3d_pre <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(V1_xyz)), function(i)
  acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, sum(V1_xyz[i, ] * V2_xyz[i, ])))) * 180 / pi,
  numeric(1))

# Post-rotation residuals are already in residuals_xyz (in radians); convert
residuals_3d_post <- residuals_xyz * 180 / pi

irls_df_xyz <- data.frame(
  pair         = seq_len(nrow(V1_xyz)),
  residual     = residuals_3d_post,
  weight       = w_xyz,

)

ggplot(irls_df_xyz, aes(pair, residual)) +

irls_df_inliers <- irls_df_xyz |> dplyr::filter(!true_outlier)

y_pad <- 0.05 * diff(range(irls_df_inliers$residual, na.rm = TRUE))
