## 2.4 Pair Set for the Stage 3 Z-Translation

The rotation solve and the Z-translation do not want the same pairs, and until
now they were handed the same list.

`R_xyz` is three parameters fitted to unit vectors. A handful of genuinely
straight pairs determines it well, and a bent stem does not merely add noise to
it – it contributes an axis direction that does not represent a straight stem at
all, which is a *bias*, not a variance. So the rotation set stays exactly as the
2.1.3 vote left it, minus the IRLS residual outliers: `pairs_stage2`, unchanged.

The Stage 3 Z-translation is a different animal. It matches features – bumps,
hollows, protrusion peaks – up the length of each stem and averages the implied
shift across pairs, so its precision falls off directly with the pair count. A
mildly bent stem carries those features perfectly well. Starving that step of
pairs to protect it from curvature it does not care about is the wrong trade.

`pairs_ztrans` is therefore assembled here, from the ranking 2.1.3 produced:

| mode | rotation (`pairs_stage2`) | Z-translation (`pairs_ztrans`) |
|---|---|---|
| `gate` | gate survivors, IRLS-filtered | the same |
| `topup` | gate survivors, IRLS-filtered | the same, **plus** the best-ranked non-passing pairs, up to `ztrans_target_pairs` |
| `irls_all` | every usable pair, IRLS-filtered | the same – the gate filtered nothing, so the IRLS residual filter is the only selection |

Topped-up pairs were never in the IRLS solve, so there is no residual to filter
them on; they enter on their rank alone and are flagged as such in
`pairs_ztrans$source`.

```{r}
#| label: ztrans-pair-set
#| code-summary: "Assemble pairs_ztrans - the pair set Stage 3 uses for the Z-translation"

if (!exists("pairs_stage2"))
  stop("[2.4] pairs_stage2 not found - run the Step 2.3 IRLS solve first.")
if (!exists("ztrans_mode") || !exists("ztrans_rank"))
  stop("[2.4] ztrans_mode / ztrans_rank not found - run the Step 2.1.3 gate first.")

.key <- function(d) paste(d$TreeID_1, d$TreeID_2, sep = "|")

# Base: whatever survived the rotation pipeline. In "irls_all" this is already
# the whole answer - the gate filtered nothing, so every pair that reached the
# solve and was not thrown out on residual is in here.
pairs_ztrans <- pairs_stage2
pairs_ztrans$source <- "gate"

if (identical(ztrans_mode, "topup") && nrow(ztrans_topup) > 0L) {

  # Only pairs not already present, and only the columns pairs_stage2 carries,
  # so the two blocks bind cleanly however the pair table is shaped.
  .add <- ztrans_topup[!(.key(ztrans_topup) %in% .key(pairs_stage2)), , drop = FALSE]
  .cols <- intersect(names(pairs_stage2), names(.add))
  .add <- .add[, .cols, drop = FALSE]
  for (nm in setdiff(names(pairs_stage2), .cols)) .add[[nm]] <- NA
  .add <- .add[, names(pairs_stage2), drop = FALSE]
  .add$source <- "topup"

  pairs_ztrans <- rbind(pairs_ztrans, .add)
  rm(.add, .cols)
}

# Attach the score every pair was ranked on, so Stage 3 can weight or audit on it
# without re-deriving anything.
pairs_ztrans$pair_score <-
  ztrans_rank$pair_score[match(.key(pairs_ztrans), .key(ztrans_rank))]
pairs_ztrans <- pairs_ztrans[order(-pairs_ztrans$pair_score), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(pairs_ztrans) <- NULL

ztrans_n_gate  <- sum(pairs_ztrans$source == "gate")
ztrans_n_topup <- sum(pairs_ztrans$source == "topup")

.tally(n_pairs_ztrans_set = nrow(pairs_ztrans),
       n_pairs_ztrans_topup = ztrans_n_topup)

cat("── Z-translation pair set (Stage 3 input) ────────────────────────────────\n")
cat(sprintf("  mode                : %s\n", ztrans_mode))
cat(sprintf("  rotation set        : %d pair(s)  [pairs_stage2 - unchanged]\n",
            nrow(pairs_stage2)))
cat(sprintf("  Z-translation set   : %d pair(s)  [pairs_ztrans]\n", nrow(pairs_ztrans)))
cat(sprintf("    from the gate     : %d\n", ztrans_n_gate))
cat(sprintf("    topped up on rank : %d (target %d)\n", ztrans_n_topup, ztrans_target_pairs))
if (identical(ztrans_mode, "topup") &&
    nrow(pairs_ztrans) < ztrans_target_pairs)
  cat(sprintf("    NOTE: only %d pair(s) available in total - the target could not be met\n",
              nrow(pairs_ztrans)))
if (nrow(pairs_ztrans) > 0L) {
  .pt <- pairs_ztrans[, c("TreeID_1", "TreeID_2", "source", "pair_score")]
  .pt$pair_score <- round(.pt$pair_score, 4)
  print(.pt, row.names = FALSE)
}
rm(.key)
```

## 2.5 Compose the Rough Alignment with the XYZ Rotation

`R_align_1` (Stage 1A) verticalises `las_1`; `R_xyz` (Step 2.3) is solved from
the resulting aligned-frame stem vectors. **Both turn about the same point.**
Stage 1A fixes `pivot1` before it rotates and does not recompute it afterwards,
so `align_pivot_1` and `pivot1` are the same coordinates, and the composed
raw -> final map is a *pure rotation about that one point* - no translation.

That is the intended behaviour, not a coincidence, and it is asserted below
rather than assumed. A rotation should not produce a shift; if these two pivots
ever drift apart again, every stage downstream inherits a translation that no
stage solved and that nothing in the data corresponds to.

This step records the total map as a new object. `R_xyz` and `R_align_1` are
left exactly as they are – everything downstream that applies them separately is
unaffected. `R_align_xyz_1` is the composed rotation; `T_align_xyz_1` is the
matching 4×4 homogeneous transform that reproduces the two Stage-1A + Step-2.3
steps in one application to raw `las_1`.

```{r}
#| label: compose-align-xyz
#| code-summary: "Compose R_align_1 (Stage 1A) with R_xyz (Step 2.3) into one raw->final transform (record only)"

if (!exists("R_xyz"))
  stop("[2.5] R_xyz not found - run the irls-svd-xyz chunk first.")
if (!exists("R_align_1") || !exists("align_pivot_1") || !exists("pivot1"))
  stop(paste0("[2.5] R_align_1 / align_pivot_1 / pivot1 not found - this Stage 1 ",
              "checkpoint predates rough alignment. Re-run Stage 1 (which records ",
              "them, identity in the run_rough_alignment = FALSE case) and reload."))

# ── Frames ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#   x_aligned = R_a (x_raw     - p_a) + p_a      Stage 1A, about p_a = align_pivot_1
#   x_final   = R_x (x_aligned - p_1) + p_1      Step 2.3, about p_1 = pivot1
# with p_a == p_1 == p by construction, so this collapses to a single rotation
# about a single point:
#   x_final = R_c (x_raw - p) + p,   R_c = R_x %*% R_a
# and in the affine form the rest of the pipeline uses,
#   x_final = R_c x_raw + t_c,       t_c = p - R_c %*% p
# t_c is therefore purely the pivot-recentring term. It is NOT a shift: it
# carries no information the rotation does not already carry, and it must never
# be reported as one.
R_a <- R_align_1
R_x <- R_xyz
p_a <- as.numeric(align_pivot_1)
p_1 <- as.numeric(pivot1)

# ── The rough leg must still be the product of its own parts ──────────────────
# Stage 1A can apply up to three rotations about the pivot - a 45 deg sideways
# probe yaw, a 90 deg tip, and the residual verticalisation - and records
# R_align_1 as their composition. Stage 1 verified that composition against the
# cloud itself; this re-checks the matrices after they have crossed the
# checkpoint, because everything from here on composes onto R_align_1 alone and
# a silently wrong rough leg is unrecoverable downstream.
if (exists("R_residual") && exists("R_sideways_pre")) {
  .comp_gap <- max(abs(R_align_1 - R_residual %*% R_sideways_pre))
  if (.comp_gap > 1e-9)
    stop(sprintf(paste0("[2.5] R_align_1 != R_residual %%*%% R_sideways_pre (max element ",
                        "difference %.3e). The Stage 1A legs and their recorded ",
                        "composition disagree."), .comp_gap))
  cat(sprintf("  Stage 1A legs recompose to R_align_1 (max element diff %.2e)\n", .comp_gap))
  rm(.comp_gap)
}

# ── The two pivots must be the same point ─────────────────────────────────────
# Enforced, not hoped for. A tolerance rather than identical() because the two
# arrive by different routes (one stored pre-rotation, one carried through the
# checkpoint) and a last-bit difference is meaningless; anything above a
# millimetre is a real divergence and means Stage 1A has started recomputing
# pivot1 again.
.pivot_gap <- sqrt(sum((p_a - p_1)^2))
if (.pivot_gap > 1e-3)
  stop(sprintf(paste0("[2.5] align_pivot_1 and pivot1 differ by %.4f m. The rough ",
                      "alignment and the fine XYZ rotation must turn about the SAME ",
                      "point, or their composition acquires a translation that no ",
                      "stage solved. Check that Stage 1A.4 is not recomputing pivot1 ",
                      "from the rotated bounding box."), .pivot_gap))

R_align_xyz_1 <- R_x %*% R_a
t_align_xyz_1 <- as.numeric(p_1 - R_align_xyz_1 %*% p_1)
T_align_xyz_1 <- rbind(cbind(R_align_xyz_1, t_align_xyz_1), c(0, 0, 0, 1))

# Composed rotation angle (about its own axis), for the methods / tilt tables.
angle_align_xyz_1 <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, (sum(diag(R_align_xyz_1)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi

# ── Matrix-derived rotation specs, mirroring the Step 2.3 report ───────────────
# The same descriptors 2.3 prints for R_rot_xyz, here computed for the composed
# raw->final rotation (and, for comparison, for each component):
#   angle    - total rotation about the matrix's own axis, acos((tr(R) - 1) / 2)
#   tilt     - tilt away from vertical: angle between R %*% +Z and +Z, which a
#              pure yaw (Z-axis spin) leaves at 0. Isolates the pitch+roll content.
#   tilt_dir - direction that tilt points: azimuth of the rotated +Z's horizontal
#              projection, CCW from +X in [0, 360). NA when there is no tilt.
#   yaw      - Z-axis spin, atan2(R[2,1] - R[1,2], R[1,1] + R[2,2])
# All four come from the rotation matrix alone, so they describe these quantities
# for a rotation that is now composed. NOTE: 2.3 also prints a tilt_dir_deg, but
# that one is the direction of the weighted mean (V2 - V1) vector difference - a
# data-derived quantity, not a matrix property - so the R_xyz row here need not
# equal 2.3's tilt_dir_deg exactly; this is the matrix-intrinsic tilt direction.
.rot_specs <- function(R) {
  ang  <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, (sum(diag(R)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
  z    <- as.numeric(R %*% c(0, 0, 1))
  tilt <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, z[3]))) * 180 / pi
  tdir <- if (tilt < 1e-9) NA_real_ else (atan2(z[2], z[1]) * 180 / pi) %% 360
  yaw  <- atan2(R[2, 1] - R[1, 2], R[1, 1] + R[2, 2]) * 180 / pi
  c(angle = ang, tilt = tilt, tilt_dir = tdir, yaw = yaw)
}
specs_align_1     <- .rot_specs(R_a)
specs_xyz         <- .rot_specs(R_x)
specs_align_xyz_1 <- .rot_specs(R_align_xyz_1)

# Persist the composed specs alongside angle_align_xyz_1 for downstream tables.
xy_tilt_in_align_xyz_1_deg   <- as.numeric(specs_align_xyz_1["tilt"])
tilt_dir_in_align_xyz_1_deg  <- as.numeric(specs_align_xyz_1["tilt_dir"])
yaw_in_align_xyz_1_deg       <- as.numeric(specs_align_xyz_1["yaw"])

# ── Self-check: the composite must reproduce the two-step transform exactly ────
# A pure algebraic identity, but cheap insurance against a future edit flipping
# a multiply order or a pivot sign. Tested on a handful of off-origin points.
.chk_raw  <- matrix(c( 3.0, -2.0,  5.0,
                      -4.0,  1.0, 12.0,
                       0.5,  7.0,  1.5,
                      10.0, 10.0, 10.0), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
.two_step <- t(apply(.chk_raw, 1, function(x) {
  xa <- as.numeric(R_a %*% (x - p_a) + p_a)   # Stage 1A
  as.numeric(R_x %*% (xa - p_1) + p_1)         # Step 2.3
}))
.one_step <- t(apply(.chk_raw, 1, function(x)
  as.numeric(R_align_xyz_1 %*% x + t_align_xyz_1)))
.compose_err <- max(abs(.two_step - .one_step))
if (.compose_err > 1e-8)
  stop(sprintf("[2.5] composed transform disagrees with the two-step transform (max err %.3e m).",
               .compose_err))

cat("-- Composed rough + XYZ rotation (record only; R_xyz / R_align_1 unchanged) --\n")
# Per-rotation spec table: the same angle / XY tilt / tilt dir / yaw 2.3 reports,
# for each rotation and the composite. Tilt, tilt direction and yaw of the
# composite are the headline; the two component rows show how they combine.
cat(sprintf("  %-22s %10s %12s %13s %10s\n",
            "Rotation", "angle(deg)", "XY tilt(deg)", "tilt dir(deg)", "yaw(deg)"))
cat(sprintf("  %-22s %10.4f %12.4f %13.4f %10.4f\n", "R_align_1 (Stage 1A)",
            specs_align_1["angle"], specs_align_1["tilt"],
            specs_align_1["tilt_dir"], specs_align_1["yaw"]))
cat(sprintf("  %-22s %10.4f %12.4f %13.4f %10.4f\n", "R_xyz (Step 2.3)",
            specs_xyz["angle"], specs_xyz["tilt"],
            specs_xyz["tilt_dir"], specs_xyz["yaw"]))
cat(sprintf("  %-22s %10.4f %12.4f %13.4f %10.4f   (det %.6f, should be 1)\n",
            "R_align_xyz_1 (composed)",
            specs_align_xyz_1["angle"], specs_align_xyz_1["tilt"],
            specs_align_xyz_1["tilt_dir"], specs_align_xyz_1["yaw"],
            det(R_align_xyz_1)))

# The same free-text lines 2.3 emits, for the composed rotation.
cat(sprintf("\n  Full 3D rotation angle: %.4f deg\n", angle_align_xyz_1))
cat("  Rotation matrix R_align_xyz_1:\n"); print(round(R_align_xyz_1, 6))
cat(sprintf("  XY tilt present in R_align_xyz_1: %.4f deg\n", xy_tilt_in_align_xyz_1_deg))
cat(sprintf("  Tilt direction in R_align_xyz_1 (0\u2013360\u00b0 CCW from +X): %.4f deg\n",
            tilt_dir_in_align_xyz_1_deg))
cat(sprintf("  Yaw present in R_align_xyz_1: %.4f deg\n", yaw_in_align_xyz_1_deg))

cat(sprintf("\n  single rotation pivot        : (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
            p_1[1], p_1[2], p_1[3]))
cat(sprintf("  align_pivot_1 vs pivot1      : %.2e m apart (must be ~0 - one pivot, no induced shift)\n",
            .pivot_gap))
cat(sprintf("  composite vs two-step check  : max err %.2e m\n", .compose_err))

rm(R_a, R_x, p_a, p_1, .pivot_gap, .chk_raw, .two_step, .one_step, .compose_err, .rot_specs)
```

## 2.6 Save/Load – Stage 2

```{r}
#| label: params-save-load_Stage2
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Save or load the combined Stage 1 + Stage 2 object set"


# ── Toggles ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage2_save <- TRUE
stage2_load <- FALSE

# ── Output path ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage2_rds_path <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/SaveLoad/Stage2_BOS_F1_aii_man.rds"

.par_apply("params-save-load_Stage2")
```

```{r}
#| label: save-load_Stage2
#| code-summary: "Save or load the combined Stage 1 + Stage 2 object set"

# A batch decides these itself, whatever they are left set to above. Both are
# read a few lines below, in this same chunk, so the driver's overrides land
# too late to reach them - and a stage left switched to LOAD after an
# interactive session would otherwise make a batch write no checkpoint at all
# and say nothing about it. Saving is what a batch is for; loading is a no-op
# in one, since every stage runs in the same session.
if (.in_batch()) { stage2_save <- TRUE; stage2_load <- FALSE }


# ── Stage 1 objects are INHERITED, not re-listed ──────────────────────────────
# .stage1_required / .stage1_optional are defined in the load_Stage2 chunk,
# which always runs. Carrying them forward by reference rather than by a
# hand-copied duplicate is the whole point: a hand-copied list drifts, and the
# previous copy had drifted far enough that it demanded objects Stage 1 no
# longer saves (the old clean_*_e parameters) - which, since .stage_save ERRORS
# on a missing required object, made this chunk unable to run at all - while
# silently dropping the refit and pass-2 products and the slice-fate ledger that
# Stage 1 does save and Stage 3 needs.
# .manifest_from() below falls back to whatever checkpoint was last loaded, so
# this no longer has to be a hard stop - a session that loaded any checkpoint
# can still save. It stops only when nothing has been loaded at all.

.stage2_own <- c(
  # -- Step 2.1 stem-set filters: surviving pair/stem tables ---------
  "pf",
  "sp",
  # -- Step 2.1.3 straightness gate: settings + selected gold length -
  "gold_count_basis",
  "gate_tests",
  "gate_min_votes",
  "gold_length",
  "gold_n_use",
  "gold_gate_active",
  "silver_length",
  "run_counts",
  # -- Step 2.1.3 continuous straightness score + Step 2.4 pair sets -
  "ztrans_target_pairs",
  "ztrans_mode",
  "ztrans_rank",
  "ztrans_topup",
  "pairs_ztrans",
  "score_unscorable_r",
  "score_len_exp",
  # -- Step 2.2 stem axis vectors ----------------------------------
  "pairs_axis",
  "vecs_xy_1",
  "vecs_xy_2",
  "ax",
  "ellipses_zt_1_valid",
  "ellipses_zt_2_valid",
  # -- Step 2.3 pre-solve angular diagnostic -----------------------
  "angular_diag",
  # -- Step 2.3 solved rotation ------------------------------------
  # Stage 2 APPLIES nothing: R_xyz is written here and first used at the
  # start of Stage 3. angle_xyz and the yaw / tilt scalars travel with it
  # for the downstream reports and the Stage 6 tilt summary.
  "R_xyz",
  "angle_xyz",
  "yaw_in_R_xyz",
  "xy_tilt_in_rot_xyz_deg",
  "tilt_dir_deg",
  "tilt_consistency",
  # -- Step 2.5 composed rough + fine rotation (record only) --------
  # R_align_xyz_1 = R_xyz %*% R_align_1: the single rotation carrying RAW
  # las_1 to the final XYZ-aligned frame. T_align_xyz_1 is its 4x4 form
  # (rotation about pivot1, in affine form), applicable to raw las_1
  # in one step; t_align_xyz_1 is that translation on its own. R_xyz and
  # R_align_1 are still saved separately and applied separately downstream.
  "R_align_xyz_1",
  "t_align_xyz_1",
  "T_align_xyz_1",
  "angle_align_xyz_1",
  # -- Pair ledger after Stage 2 -----------------------------------
  "pairs_stage2"
)

.stage2_optional_own <- character(0)

.stage2_required <- c(.manifest_from(".stage1_required", "required"), .stage2_own)
.stage2_optional <- setdiff(c(.manifest_from(".stage1_optional", "optional"),
                             .stage2_optional_own),
                            .stage2_required)

if (stage2_save) {
  stage2_rds_written <- .stage_save(stage2_rds_path, .stage2_required,
                                    .stage2_optional, label = "Stage 2")
  cat(sprintf("Stage 3 should load: %s\n", stage2_rds_written))
}

if (stage2_load) {
  .stage_load(stage2_rds_path, .stage2_required, .stage2_optional, label = "Stage 2")
  cat(sprintf("\nStage 2 restored: XYZ rotation %.4f deg | %d pair(s) carried forward\n",
              angle_xyz, nrow(pairs_stage2)))
  cat(sprintf("Gold length %.1f m | %d straight %s | gate: %d of %d votes (%s)%s\n",
              gold_length, gold_n_use,
              if (identical(gold_count_basis, "pairs")) "pair(s)" else "stem(s)",
              gate_min_votes, length(gate_tests), paste(gate_tests, collapse = ", "),
              if (isTRUE(gold_gate_active)) "" else
                sprintf(" -- SILVER FALLBACK (%.1f m): weighting only, no straightness filtering applied",
                        silver_length)))
  cat(sprintf("  curv clamp(%.2f x noise, %.2f, %.2f) cm, L^%.2f\n",
              curv_noise_mult, curv_thresh_cm, curv_thresh_max, gold_exp_curv))
  cat(sprintf("  sag  clamp(%.2f x floor, %.2f, %.2f) cm, L^%.2f\n",
              sag_noise_mult, sag_thresh_cm, sag_thresh_max, gold_exp_sag))
  cat(sprintf("  bend clamp(%.2f x floor, %.2f, %.2f) deg, L^%.2f\n",
              bend_noise_mult, bend_thresh_deg, bend_thresh_max, gold_exp_bend))
  .report_pivot1()
  .report_slice_fates()
}
```

Run `Stage3_ZTranslation.qmd`. It loads this checkpoint, reloads and re-filters
the point clouds, and is the first stage to actually apply `R_xyz` – about
